entries.0f25147e51442b6c40e2f38fc1bf371abe029326: Presentation of the 2025 Achievements in Universal Accessibility and the list of actions followed in 2026
entries.2cec4fcbc5cbe8469826b444559a255675334273: In 2011, the City of Montreal adopted its Municipal Policy on Universal Accessibility (AU) to make Montreal a universally accessible city, where everyone, regardless of their capacity, can have access to information, places, equipment, jobs, democratic life, services and programs in an independent, non-discriminatory and equitable manner. In accordance with the Act to ensure that persons with disabilities exercise their rights for school, professional and social integration, the City is required to produce and file annually an action plan for persons with disabilities and an assessment with political authorities.
entries.c2c8fb3691faa8c0c8f126bde02b007f71655370: Tabling of the Commission's report on the Inspector General entitled "Study of recommendations reports following an investigation into subcontracting in the execution of contracts for the collection and transportation of residual materials arising from the 23-19726 call for tender in the Saint-Laurent and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension arrondissements"
entries.b9863091242e6da82c5ba48d90e67a882fe0750c: Declaration for Latin American Heritage Month
entries.b1d1957cc275829c4f754c6941c75a48770c2d3e: Exercising the one-year extension option / Authorize an additional expenditure of $5,108,788.24, including taxes, for cleanliness brigade management services in the 19 boroughs for the year 2027 under the contract awarded to Alphanet Maintenance Services Inc. (CM25,1405), thus increasing the total contract amount to $10,217,576.48, including taxes
entries.a9db7140708dc2b002fc2b735b32e4f3c8ca10f7: To enter into an 18-month framework agreement, whereby Construction DJL Inc., the lowest compliant bidder, undertakes to provide the City, upon request, with cold coatings (for Lot 1) for a period of 18 months, up to $527,746.58, including taxes, in accordance with public tender documents 26-21468 (5 som.)
entries.baa9753fe06c58160e0c2fd706182fb870d0baa7: The purpose of this file is to enter into three framework agreements for the provision and delivery on request of cold-coated and water-reactive coatings, primarily for prescribed work for spot pavement repairs as well as temporary choke-closing and localized pavement repair. Framework agreements will be made available to all business units in the City of Montreal. In April 2025, the contract for the supply and delivery on demand of cold-rolled oil coatings was awarded, in accordance with public tender documents 24-20811, to the lowest compliant bidder, namely Tech-Mix, Bau-Val Division, Inc., for an estimated total amount of $192,071.33, including taxes.
entries.0bfbc89e3340c2931cfe604810b729d5b841b654: Contract with REM. Groupe Extrême inc., for towing services for snow removal operations in the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough, for a period of one winter season, including an option to extend a winter season - Total expenditure of $372,519, including taxes - Public tender 26-21535 (1 sum)
entries.199bd3ce8bc77183389341c673a6ead5b7d0cb6d: The Agglomeration Council's Regulation on Delegation of Authority in Respect of Towing to Related Municipalities (RCG 19-016) came into force on May 22, 2019. It provides for the delegation to each related municipality, including the City of Montreal, of towing activities related to snow removal operations, including the granting, monitoring and administrative management of such activities. Thus, the borough consultation and civic experience department (SCAEC) is responsible for the integrated planning of towing operations carried out as part of snow clearing operations since January 1, 2020, the launching of tenders and the award of related contracts.
entries.8410f159bca7f76f0d1275b4dfe7ebf43a4e3020: Provide six contracts to Ramcor Construction Inc., MWM Specialty Equipment and Les Entreprises Michaudville Inc., for the rental of equipment with operator for snow removal operations, for a winter season for the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough, including an option to extend a winter season - Total expenditure of $2,969,202.13, taxes included - Public tender 26-21544 (5 som.)
entries.bfdbdfdbe89d32df393e2a99d195994d23794b13: The Service de la concertation des boroughes et de l'expérience citoyenne (SCAEC) is responsible for the integrated planning of snow removal operations on pavements and sidewalks, the launching of tenders and the award of related contracts. On August 24, 2026, the Supply Service launched a call for tender 26-21544 for equipment rental with operator for snow removal operations for the Plateau-Mont-Royal district. A notice was published on August 24, 2026 on the Government of Quebec electronic tendering system (SEAO) as well as in the daily Le Devoir.
entries.d8b6a8ced2110c3999c215c03eeb2192022cde4e: Grant an OTC contract to Para-Sol Design n.e.c., for professional services in the design and realization of a museum experience of "Tentier pieds nudes - Les pieds sur terre" at the Jardin botanique de Montréal - Total expenditure of: $293,146.02, including taxes / Approve draft convention to this effect
entries.7e8bfd85c0c4ee7de1f7f12c54075cc40709af09: Each year, during the summer, the Botanical Garden offers diverse and attractive programming to its visitors. These activities have a significant impact on visitors. In 2027, as part of this summer program, an original and fun experience of Sentier pieds nudes, entitled Les pieds sur terre, will be offered to Montreal's general public and tourists.
entries.56af20195d9667240cffaac01e527ebe226030d8: Approve the proposed premises lease agreement whereby the City rents a sports venue and platters at the Claude-Robillard Sports Complex from November 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028 at the Baseball Academy Canada for its activities / Authorize receipt of estimated $68,453.17, including taxes for this purpose / Authorize technical support of $117,568.25, including taxes
entries.9fc50751d7cad2f66ecb2612d5f6d8d27618a9b9: Approve the premises loan contract whereby the City lends, free of charge, to Culture Montréal for a period of four years, effective December 1, 2026, premises 314, 315 and 317 located at 3680 Jeanne-Mance Street in the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough, with an area of approximately 185.35 square metres (1,995.08 square feet), for sociocultural activities. The total amount of the real estate grant is estimated at $199,510.76 (Building 2453-104)
entries.d67d56109e979120fd9b773ad2c3f0a6cbf5bb42: The Strathearn Centre, located at 3680 Jeanne-Mance Street, is a socioculturally oriented municipal building that hosts several organizations, including SME-ART, Atelier d'artistes, Ex aequo and Danse-Cité. Since December 1, 2002, Culture Montréal has occupied free of charge room number 317 on the third floor of the building. In August 2005, a second agreement was reached to allow the organization to occupy, also free of charge, room number 314, located on the same floor.
entries.1fc911e66c1499f3952197395fd519fb28e8a9b8: Provide financial support totalling $463,450, in connection with the Reflex 3 agreement with the Government of Quebec and estimated technical support of $400,000 to four organizations under the 2026-2027 Winter Strategy / Authorize a $463,450 budget transfer from the Economic Development Service to the Culture, Sports and Recreation Service / Approve draft conventions to this effect
entries.3f775a295ef801ce5326768a2880ca00548a58f4: As part of the implementation of the 2025-2028 Winter Strategy and the 2024-2030 Downtown Strategy, the City of Montreal is continuing its efforts to animate the city centre in winter with a diverse cultural, tourist and event offering. This strategy is based on three areas of intervention: atmosphere, programming and communications. The present dossier aims to support four projects that will contribute to the animation of the city center during the winter 2026-2027: Igloo Fête 2027, produced by Festival Igloo Le Grand Minuit de Montréal, produced by Festival Igloo The preparatory matches for the LNI, produced by the Théâtre de la Ligue nationale d'improvisation Le Grand Marché de Noël, produced by La Lutinerie The events Le Grand Minuit de Montréal and Le Grand Marché de Noël had already been selected following the call for special projects launched in 2024 and are receiving ongoing support from the City.
entries.60d1f4726666b3d50e83408f118813b8d1aa66dc: Provide CIBC Mellon Trust Company with an over-the-counter contract to issue lump sum payments from the Montreal Pension Plan Office for a five-year period, including a 12-month extension option - Total expenditure of $296,307.83, including taxes
entries.928576f2fae1974b0471e0092ea73731df9b884c: The City of Montreal Act allows the City of Montreal to establish and maintain defined benefit pension plans in which its employees and former employees participate. The Montréal Pension Plan Office ("BRRM") administers the following plans established by the City: - The Ville de Montréal Executive Pension Plan; - The Ville de Montréal Blue Cols Pension Plan; - The Ville de Montréal foreman Pension Plan; - The Ville de Montréal White Cols Pension Plan; - The Ville de Montréal Firefighter Pension Plan; - The Ville de Montréal Professional Pension Plan. The six defined benefit pension plans are administered by commissions that have delegated the majority of administrative tasks to the City of Montreal.
entries.df4d931ac92ba758e6ffa0345bcdce6e8d3d8f07: Approve the proposed premises loan contract whereby the City of Montreal lends to the Société historique de Montréal, for a period of five years, effective January 1, 2027, premises with an area of approximately 169.55 square metres (1,825 square feet) located on the floors and basement of the building bearing number 462, Place Jacques-Cartier, in the borough of Ville-Marie. The amount of the real estate grant awarded for the duration of the agreement is $157,750 (Building 8543)
entries.285096d9870c14fc0cf45f0f555ec11b57df8674: Exercising the option of the second 12-month extension / Authorize an additional expenditure of $313,523.03, including taxes, for the supply of Kebony wood for the City's specialized workshops, under the framework agreement with North On Sixty (CM24,0689), thus increasing the total amount of the agreement to $1,111,390.80, including taxes
entries.21f2726ea9c7bb5a1d066f5b6840e1954928e905: The rolling stock and workshop department (SMRA) is responsible for, among other things, the manufacture, maintenance, repair and rehabilitation of various components of urban furniture used in the territory of the City of Montreal. These activities are based on a continuous supply of specialized materials that meet the city's standards of quality, durability and environmental requirements. Among the required materials, Kebony wood is regularly used by SMRA carpentry workshops for the manufacture, maintenance and repair of several urban furniture equipment, including benches, baskets and picnic tables.
entries.75ab5c64d54abb3028e7b0f744f3c2ba2de13a11: Contract with Le Groupe St-Lambert (2862-5622 Québec inc.), for the renovation of the Henry-Teuscher Auditorium of the Administrative Building of the Botanical Garden - Total expenditure of $3,043,312.11 including taxes - Public Call for Bids IMM-15991 (10 Som.)
entries.fc0602247d9b12163a14a9990ca3a535fd719c17: Located in the heart of the Marie-Victorin building of the Botanical Garden of Montreal, the Henry-Teuscher Auditorium is an important venue for dissemination in the east of the metropolis. In the 1930s North American Art Deco movement, the hall provides a variety of cultural events for the general public and corporate clientele. Its facilities include a 60 m2 stage, a room with a capacity of 282 seats, as well as technical equipment to meet the various needs of sound and lighting.
entries.1f39e3f799aa270205a237125712a414e9b3c43b: Approve the proposed fourth lease extension agreement whereby the City leases to L'Office des congrès et du tourisme du grand Montréal inc., for a period of three years, effective January 1, 2027, spaces on the ground floor of the building located at 174 Notre-Dame Street East, in the borough of Ville-Marie, with an area of approximately 50.35 square metres (542 square feet), for tourist office purposes, for a total rent of $77,250, excluding taxes (Building 8543-001)
entries.9b1debc7696c432317f19c4e99292891d9510da7: Take note of the report of the Standing Committee on the Review of Contracts
entries.8e8a35eb8cd11e5d4cc809c08fca608ca9c4c020: The Districts and Citizen Experience Coordination Service (CASS) is responsible for the integrated planning of snow removal operations on roads and sidewalks, the launching of tenders and the award of related contracts. In a context where the availability of snow transportation resources remains an important issue for industry, CASS continues to diversify its modes of service retention in order to ensure the resilience of its operations while remaining responsive to market realities and business constraints. This approach aims to maintain a balance between the City's needs, operational efficiency and the attractiveness of proposed contracts to the industry.
entries.c75076b3b09add1bc27fa3b2a27d12a149f0f54d: In March 2019, the owner of the Molson site had agreed to sell its industrial site to a developer wishing to carry out a residential project there. The City then held various rights on the site allowing it to intervene in the transaction, including first-time contract refusal rights dating from 1987 and 1990 as well as a pre-emption right imposed in 2018. The Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal (SHDM) also enjoyed surface rights on certain lots of the site.
entries.582294540b2c1a29fa5b12f4517919cb29e2d1bf: Accept the offer of services from the Technical Services and Logistics Support Division to the facilities of the arrondissement of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, from January 1, 2027 to December 31, 2028, in accordance with section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4)
entries.86c9c3f4da67b4f4b902a4d8c5386f116a517148: In accordance with sections 85 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4), this file recommends acceptance of the service provided by the Technical Services and Facilities Support Division (DSTSLI) of the Office de projets et du développement des services aux citoyens de l'arrondissement de Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve. For several years, the Technical Services and Facilities Support Division (DSTSLI) has been providing loan, carpentry, maintenance, assembly and disassembly services for various types of facilities and events throughout Montréal.
entries.8b79f8623ab80ddca33b2fe6e227ed3bd4834900: Increase the allocation of the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough, through the Environmental Liability of Contaminated Soils Program, for $733,409.62 net taxes, to fund environmental rehabilitation costs for the Baldwin Park South Redevelopment Project, located on Lot 1,424,067 of the Québec cadastre, Montréal Land Registry District, in the De Lorimier district at the intersection of Fullum Street and Rachel East, Plateau-Mont-Royal District
entries.3d8929b7afe0b8c22feff890bcdae4c136350961: The Land Development and Technical Studies Directorate of the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough wishes to refurbish the southern area of Baldwin Park. It is a busy neighbourhood park and a destination for leisure, recreation and event events. The district is keen to create and offer a new quality sports centre in order to enhance its range of sports plateau services and meet the needs of users in the De Lorimier district.
entries.fd7df1e708ea5ddd42271062d72d60e8a759065b: Increase the endowment of Plateau-Mont-Royal borough, through the Environmental Liabilities Reserve, to $19,438.55 net taxes, in order to retain the professional services required for the completion of the additional environmental studies necessary to estimate the costs associated with decontamination and soil rehabilitation of the Alma and Carmel aisle development project, located in the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough
entries.8acc4dd9de091e164852e4274b58878f392df207: The Arrondissement du Plateau-Mont-Royal wishes to continue the revitalization of the Saint-Viateur East sector through the development of the Alma and Carmel aisles. These pedestrian paths, located on the axis of Alma Street between Rue Maguire and the Saint-Viateur driveway, as well as in the axis of Avenue du Carmel between the future Alma and Henri-Julien Avenue, will promote active transport and help unblock the area. Previous studies have been carried out on the site to identify the present contamination: - SNC+Lavallin, 2016.
entries.0f2a553b85e75221b546501d0418e2654f25808f: Increase the allocation of the borough of Montréal-Nord, through environmental liability for contaminated soils, in the amount of $142,422.81 net taxes, for environmental characterization services Phase II of soil and biogas on Lot 1,990,031 of the cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montreal, located in the borough of Montréal-Nord (Friche Charleroi)
entries.398f3a8ef08445baf71e83c793d10486ca11c08e: The purpose of this addendum is to request the City Council to increase the allocation of the Montréal-Nord borough, through environmental liability for contaminated soils, in the amount of $142,422.81 (net taxes), in order to cover the costs of Phase II environmental characterization services for soils and biogas on Lot 1,990,031 of the Cadastre du Québec, located in the arrondissement of Montreal-Nord (Charleroi friche).
entries.840b8dcee677458ca3dbffae31f78860c9a7cc8c: Remove from the public domain as an alley, part of Lot 3,725,849 from the cadastre du Québec, Registration Division of Montreal, located northwest of Jean-Talon Street East, between Christophe-Colomb Avenue and De La Roche Street, in the borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, with an area of 75.2 square metres, to contribute it to the public domain as a local park, as part of the renovation project for Le Prévost Park
entries.f33325c5638a79395081722db5999c6effdfea67: By resolution CA26 14,0220, adopted at its September 1, 2026 sitting, the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension District Council recommends that the City Council remove from the public domain as an alley part of Lot 3,725,849, identified in Plan J-169 Saint-Denis, minute 1222, prepared by Gabriel Cadrin-Tourigny, surveyor-geometer, dated April 1, 2026, with an area of 75.2 square metres, to be transferred to the public domain as a local park, as part of the Le Prévost Park Redevelopment Project. The purpose of this summary is therefore to transmit the file to the City Council.
entries.7a91fd880e1e8c83c8af0327bdf8225496c5a707: Accept the offer of services of the borough of Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, in accordance with section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4), to take over the work of repairing carriageways on the administrative arterial network of the City on the territory of the borough, as part of the Program of rehabilitation of carriageways by planage-revealment - Artériel
entries.9dc22f88d6464fce0e86398649c35b75e6ef184a: The Service des infrastructures du réseau route (SIRR) is responsible for the rehabilitation and maintenance of the assets of the arterial road network of the City of Montreal (RAAV), which is the jurisdiction of the council of the City under the Charter of the City (section 87, paragraph 6, and section 105). Knowing that the sections of streets on which it wishes to intervene fall within the jurisdiction of the council of the City, the Arrondissement de Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie offered to carry out the work there pursuant to section 85, paragraph 2, of the Charter of the City of Montréal, which states that "A borough council may, on such terms as it determines, provide to the council of the City a service connected with a jurisdiction falling within the latter; the resolution of the borough council takes effect from the date of adoption by the council of the City of a resolution accepting the provision of services".
entries.d20d0783eb5ec17ede0578459e1126940913e0c2: Offer to the borough of Ville-Marie, in accordance with section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montréal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4), to assume responsibility for planning and carrying out the development work of the Place du Village permanente, including the management of works, as part of the Sainte-Catherine Est project
entries.6f81edefb6d7c0688b5ed93004e688f829a41789: The Place du Village is a public place located at the corner of Atateken and Sainte-Catherine East streets, in the heart of the Village. Acquised by the City in 2014, this site has been temporarily set up. Animation and event programming are also deployed on this site, which falls under the jurisdiction of the borough of Ville-Marie.
entries.bdb24b9061eca6915dc249192327d6c3cca0d09d: Offer to the borough of Outremont, in accordance with section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4), to assume, as of November 2026, the activity "Information technology - office and telecommunications support"
entries.2ce6945af230f31b243386985b04bbd10ee6fcb8: The Information Technology Service (IT) is a key player in the digital modernization of the City of Montreal. By positioning technology as a strategic lever, it develops and deploys solutions tailored to internal needs to improve the performance and quality of services for citizens and municipal staff. Its role is to align technological initiatives with the City's objectives by promoting accessibility, efficiency and quality of services.
entries.e2db8d91aba0baedc7f0b80df3424ef070323d9a: Accept a budgetary transfer of $17,300 in 2026 from Outremont borough to Information Technology Service (ITS) / Authorize a recurring adjustment to the budget base for a person-year of $105,400 from Outremont borough to ITS starting in 2027
entries.ae2f666b7c5d5c62dfd008d37c0b57617deb724b: Accept the offers of services of all borough councils, in accordance with section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4), to take responsibility for the design and execution of the street development work of the administrative arterial road network of the City
entries.947618647dd7d3289e049d4e1645b2d4d06269ff: The City of Montreal's Urban Planning and Mobility Service (SUM) is responsible for the planning and development of the city's arterial road network (RAAV), which falls under the jurisdiction of the City Council under the City Charter (Art. 87(6) and Art. 105). Knowing that the streets on which they wish to intervene fall within the jurisdiction of the City Council, boroughs have offered to carry out the work there pursuant to section 85 of the City of Montréal Charter, which states that "A borough council may, on such terms as it determines, provide the City Council with a service connected to a jurisdiction falling within its jurisdiction; the resolution of the borough council shall take effect from the date of adoption by the City Council of a resolution accepting the provision of services." Acceptance of borough offers of services, in respect of redevelopment projects to be carried out in 2026 and 2027, constitutes the subject matter of this file.
entries.5483faf6db9dd32c886ce5ded0eea0a2c659bde3: To extend, pursuant to section 85.5 of the Charter of the City of Montréal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4), for a period of three years, the declaration of jurisdiction of the municipal council with respect to the implementation of the obligations incumbent on the City under the Charter of the French Language (RLRQ, c. C-11)
entries.e854669a04c776849d013946174f497b49512995: On October 21, 2024, the City Council adopted Resolution CM24 1107, by which it declared itself competent for a period of two years with respect to certain obligations arising from the Charter of the French Language. This decision was intended to ensure coherent linguistic governance at the municipal level following the entry into force of the new obligations introduced by the Act respecting the official and common language of Quebec, French. Since the adoption of this resolution, the City has continued to implement its linguistic obligations in a centralized manner under the leadership of the Office de la langue française, which acts as coordinator and centre of expertise for all central services and boroughs.
entries.c74c437058f38988d62c1e8433475313df8d5312: To extend, for a period of two years, the declaration of jurisdiction of the council of the city with regard to the adoption and application of the rules relating to respect for the person in relation to the mechanisms for supporting and processing requests for intervention, reports and complaints set out in the Policy on Respect for the Person, pursuant to section 85.5 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4)
entries.52afcb6af5a0a3641d4ddebf3adb2ab17268ad3a: On August 2, 2012, the Executive Committee adopted the new Policy on Respect for the Person (CE12 1208). The Policy specified that it should be revised after five years. On May 2, 2018, steps were taken by the Respect for the Person Division in the Human Resources Service and the Comptroller General, with members of the Presidency Commission, to propose that the review of the Policy on Respect for the Person be carried out in a comprehensive manner, so that the Policy applies to the entire municipal community: elected persons, employees, public servants and cabinet staff.
entries.7c1fa49507e6779ed52ef3250b6e0983074734b2: Authorize the submission of four applications for funding to the Department of Transport and Sustainable Mobility under Project Call 2027-2028 of the Urban Active Transportation Development Financial Assistance Program for projects at the Gadbois Pole, the redevelopment of Notre-Dame Street West, the Sunnybrooke Bicycle Link between Ceres Street and Lucerne Street, and the Wellington Project
entries.42320cd85edd6d0fe6d0954595fe683c08b06fbe: As part of the Sustainable Mobility Policy 2030 and in line with the objectives of the Government of Quebec's 2030 Green Economy Plan, the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable (MTMD) is seeking to develop alternative modes of transportation for cars, including cycling and walking, in order to encourage the people of Québec, the ultimate clientele of the program, to opt for these more healthy, economical, ecological and safe means. The Program d'aide financière au développement des transports actives dans les aménagements urbains (TAPU) is intended as a support tool for municipalities that aims to help them take or continue a marked shift in the provision of active transportation infrastructure in Québec. The financial assistance provided by the Ministry through these programs can cover 50% of eligible expenses up to a maximum amount.
entries.8cb62d63985672210689340ef8a4921bf246b594: Adopt the terms and conditions governing the payment of advances under section 31.5.5.1 of the Act respecting the treatment of municipal elected officials
entries.39db1c959eeba068296d9d3f9a0c1195b0b11a0a: On June 11, 2026, Bill No. 22 introduced section 31.5.5.1 of the Act on the Treatment of Municipal Elected Persons, which now allows a municipality to authorize advance payments to elected officials in respect of sums intended for the reimbursement of research and support expenses.
entries.ac6ae31ddab8675aa4b62c61f76afb3b0bc9598c: Allow advance payments to eligible elected officials for a total amount of $290,397.58 for fiscal year 2026
entries.1cc40de067df51ab677c8743e1ef28c07047c325: Notice of Motion and Tabling - Regulations Establishing the Process for Dealing with Complaints or Reports of Conduct by Certain Officers under Municipal Council
entries.f218310535544c20668fb37bed33c1fc96e64bfc: The City of Montreal Personnel Code of Conduct and the Respect for the Person Policy are two regulations adopted by the City Council that apply to all members of the City's staff. A member of the staff, a victim or witness of a breach of any of these regulations, may make a report or complaint to the Comptroller General for failure to comply with a rule set out in the Code of Conduct, or to the Complaints Support Centre (CAPP) for failure to comply with the Compliance Policy. The Comptroller General may also intervene on his/her own initiative.
entries.eb369aa270c5198cba085dad5d13cda249dfa8c6: In 2021, the City Council passed the Domestic Animal Guidance Regulations (21-012) , a regulation that is harmonized with the Provincial Regulations under the Act to Promote the Protection of Persons through the Establishment of Dog Frameworks (RLRQ, c. P-38.002, r. 1) . Since the coming into force of the provincial regulations (March 2020), the City of Montreal has applied its by-laws with respect to domestic animals and provincial regulations.
entries.d91d2e484926a4706143d31f9d4b407862a08429: Notice of Motion and Tabling - Regulations Amending the Public Water and Sewer System Connections and Rainwater Management Regulations (20-030)
entries.f942451e88a1e66a5b17143d5ba07f6ff3464149: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. The Regulations Respecting Connections to Public Water and Sewage Systems and the Management of Rainwater Systems (20-030), as amended by Regulations 20-030-1, 20-030-2, 20-030-3 and 20-030-4, are intended primarily to protect the structure and capacity of municipal systems so that each user can connect to the water and sewer system without putting other users at risk and without affecting the reliability of the networks.
entries.7be4eebee6ce119c07635354f40e431ed8df997f: Notice of Motion and Tabling - Regulations for the Closure of an alley northeast of 57th Avenue, between 5th Street and Maurice-Duplessis Boulevard, in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, for transfer to riparian owners
entries.7154c0693815b567d182d0972e84eee7abfa6363: The Department of Real Estate Strategy and Housing (SSIH) has received a request from a citizen to acquire the riparian lane at its property, located northeast of 57 Avenue, between 5th Street and Maurice-Duplessis Boulevard, in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairie–Pointe-aux-Trembles. Analysis of this application reveals that the alley, formerly known as Lot 1,510,437 of the Quebec cadastre and shown as an indication on plans B, C and P annexed, is occupied by several riparian owners, numbering eighteen (18) and may be disposed of. The necessary steps have been taken, with a view to divestment of this alley, under administrative framework number C-OG-GPI-D-17-002 "Crossing of lanes to riparian owners – Terms and conditions", and the provisions of sections 179 to 185 of Schedule C of the Charter of the City of Montreal (EnFramement).
entries.5487c2bed2e5c3b8f5bd1a2589326cbeec378818: Notice of Motion and Filing - Regulations Amending the By-Laws of the City Council on the Delegation of Authority from the City Council to the Executive Committee on Planning, Planning and Heritage (15-077)
entries.db99fdf82c89d8425a7768e910f768cd115b8e55: In an effort to modernize the regulatory powers of local municipalities with respect to demolition and expand its scope, primarily for the purpose of protecting real estate heritage, the Government of Quebec assented to the Act to amend the Cultural Heritage Act and other legislative provisions on April 1, 2021.
entries.be7ed6fad35e2e72e00738bf53ddc2b2adb18199: Adoption - Regulation respecting the closure of an alley to the northeast of 18th Avenue between Ontario Street East and De Montigny Street, in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, for transfer to riparian owners
entries.287e7045177335207331ea6b070af062766d75b2: The Real Estate Strategy and Housing Service (SSIH) has received an application from a citizen to acquire the riparian lane at its property, located northeast of 18th Avenue, between Ontario Street East and De Montigny Street, in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairie–Pointe-aux-Trembles. Analysis of this application reveals that the alley, formerly known as Lots 1,261,875, 1,261,881 and 1,261,882 of the Quebec cadastre and shown as an indication on plans B, C and P annexed, is occupied by several riparian owners, numbering fifteen (15) and may be disposed of. The necessary steps have been taken, with a view to divestment of this alley, under administrative framework number C-OG-GPI-D-17-002 "Transfer of lanes to riparian owners – Terms and conditions", pursuant to the provisions of sections 179 to 185 of Schedule C of the Charter of the City of Montreal (Enguidement).

entries.2b0a1f518119db254e441efb5f85551ab08a6354: On January 1, 2015, a new version of the City's administrative arterial network (RAAV) came into force, amending the City's arterial network regulations (02-003). At the time of its adoption, the City Administration anticipated that an annual update would be made to reflect adjustments and normal developments in the road network (1144637006). This proposed amendment to the Regulations reflects adjustments to the additions or deletions of sections of the road network since the last amendment to the regulations adopted on September 18, 2023.

entries.125058a766fc03e51c872e0d7ebcd2e21fc39a85: For decades, nightlife has been an important cultural, tourism, commercial and economic niche for Montreal and contributes to its international reach. In November 2024, the City of Montreal adopted a Nightlife Policy with 3 main directions: 1. Fostering a dynamic and safe nightlife for people and tourists, building on entrepreneurship, Montréal's cultural experience and responsible festive practices as factors of social cohesion and quality of life. 2.

entries.80d8f73f40576e9d77cec865261afd100b2c03cf: Appoint Mathieu Arsenault, Professor of History, as Chair of the Advisory Committee in Recognition for a first three-year renewable term beginning on October 20, 2026
entries.ceef13f5c2ed408cd11fb44888666959698e5bb8: The Advisory Committee on Recognition (ACR) is the City of Montreal's advisory body on recognition. Its mandate is to provide advice in order to inform the City's decisions regarding proposed commemorative ceremonies, material commemoration, toponymy and identification regulations referred to in section 121 of the Quebec Cultural Heritage Act. The committee was established by the adoption of the Regulation respecting the Advisory Committee on Recognition (22-044) on September 20, 2022.

entries.2cbb5dbc259d5f7526ac0772969dab2820cd7478: The Montreal Fire Safety Service (IMS) has approximately 110 officers, officers, firefighters and firefighters whose specialty is the intervention involving hazardous materials, located in two specialized barracks serving the entire Montréal area. As part of its commitment to occupational health and safety, the SIM aims to ensure optimal protection against chemical hazards while maintaining a high level of protection, performance and compliance with current standards. The equipment sought must include excellent heat resistance, breathability, moisture management and body heat evacuation characteristics in order to improve the comfort, safety and operational efficiency of personnel during interventions in addition to meeting applicable NFPA standards.
entries.560c4941d0269c614bd2b73a35da03abb87cdacb: Completing framework agreements with Goodyear Canada Inc., Michelin North America (Canada) Inc., Continental Tire Canada, Inc., Toyo Tire Canada Inc., Hankook Tire Canada Corp., to use standing contracts for the supply of various new tires as part of the City's bid solicitation conducted by the Government Procurement Centre 2026-8109-50-02 for 36 months - Estimated amount of agreements: $5,124,895.65, including taxes
entries.cac5739f5c1c1a072c0e63cc35ce4510ed33614d: The Executive Committee authorized the City of Montreal to join a consolidated purchase file organized by the Government Acquisitions Centre (GAC) in order to ensure the continuity of the supply of tires for the municipal fleet at the end of the current standing contract on March 31, 2026 (CE25,0772). Pursuant to section 5, second paragraph, of the Public Bodies Contracts Act (PSCA), the City committed itself, upon joining the purchasing pool, to acquire the goods from suppliers selected as part of this process. Furthermore, section 573.3.2 of the Cities and Cities Act allows a municipality to obtain any movable property or service from or through the Government Acquisitions Centre (GAC).

entries.b8c8ab1f1cf1bed2c49d863388da1680de29e99f: The Urban Planning and Mobility Service (UMS) is responsible for planning and guiding the realization of an attractive, inclusive and resilient Montréal for the benefit of today's and future populations. It guides the development of living environments, landscape and heritage as well as developing ecological mobility solutions. The Urban Development Projects Directorate (UADD) translates Montreal's territorial plans and strategies into relevant municipal interventions.

entries.fc4f369ddb2aed2438dfb64d3ff533ecdf5b2099: The Ville de Montréal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water to the Montreal community, manage stormwater and clean up wastewater, to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations.As part of the program to repair drinking water plants in the Drinking Water Branch (DEP) of the Service de l'eau, active maintenance work is required to preserve the sustainability of its works, including potable water production plants, various reservoirs and pumping stations. Given the nature of certain projects, the continued operation of plants during the completion of the work, as well as the possibility that several interventions will take place simultaneously at one site, the City of Montréal is acting as the prime contractor within the meaning of the Act respecting occupational health and safety (LSST).

entries.f6a5baf94cfe7b928852734f8a0bc9f9f991b74a: Approve the agreement between the Minister of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food of Quebec and the City relating to the provision of personal and confidential information concerning agricultural operations located on the territory of the agglomeration for the purpose of promoting the development of agricultural activities or the protection of agricultural territory
entries.e214cedbe5412d2d79135819df2e4d98bd5c518b: As part of the revision of the Plan d'aménagement et de développement de l'agglomeration de Montréal (Schema), government guidelines for land use planning (OGAT) require a characterization of the agricultural area. In accordance with OGAT, the City of Montreal must also provide a portrait of urban farming activities on the territory of the agglomeration and identify agricultural potentials in urban areas. To do so, the City must obtain detailed data from the Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ) on registered farms and their location at the agglomeration level.
entries.b16c006d21cb63486d5eebb12e626b5a217f676b: Approve the draft act under which the City acquires from Logistec Services Maritimes SRI, a real and perpetual easement of public utilities for the construction, operation and maintenance of a storm and sanitary collector, including the volumetric plate, with an area of 9,119 square metres on the ground, strikes part of Lot 4,683,647 of the cadastre du Québec, Registration Division of Montreal, located in the east-west axis of the Island of Montréal, in the City of Montreal East, for $490,780 plus applicable taxes

entries.7c5afdba6017d7e6be1b1ac47795d4ef85fc1b7c: The Coopérative d'habitation Ste-Anne (Montréal) (the Seller) approached the City of Montreal (the City) to investigate its interest in acquiring vacant land known and designated as Lot 1 853 591 of the Quebec cadastre (the Building), located on Rue de la Montagne, west of Wellington Street. As a result of the analysis of this opportunity by the relevant stakeholders, the South West borough (the Arrondissement) expressed its interest in acquiring the Building for the purpose of developing a local park there, especially for urban farming purposes. Thus, the Arrondissement and the Urban Planning and Mobility Service (UMS) mandated the Real Estate Strategy and Housing Service (SSIH) to negotiate freely with the Seller the conditions for acquiring the Property.
entries.f39379af0148fbf240fa479c31b8bbca908ce527: Approve the draft addendum 1 to the financial contribution agreement between the City and Mission Old Brewery, arising from contributions from the social component of the Regulations aimed at improving the supply of social, affordable and family housing in addition to the financial support received under the TOIT Capital Fund of the Fonds de solidarité FTQ, in order to increase by $475,000 the amount of the financial contribution, for the construction of a building located at 1685-1693 Church Avenue, in the Southwest District
entries.c35abf84448218bc8c47f87ff408d74d5db5131f: The OBM-De l'Église project aims to implement an affordable housing project for women who have lived in homelessness or are at risk of living it. It is funded under the Fonds capital pour TOIT initiative of the Fonds de solidarité FTQ. A financial aid agreement has been concluded between Fonds capital pour TOIT s.e.c. and Mission Old Brewery (Organism) for an amount of $2,275,000.
entries.e4fe5e8e9b307d19126bc1cfb6e18b8eb184ead9: Approve Addenda 1 to the financial contribution agreements between the City and three different organizations (CG25 0507), to extend the term of the agreements to December 31, 2027 and for a total additional financial support of $860,692, increasing the total amount of financial contributions to $1,560,011, as part of the agglomeration budget of the Diversity and Social Inclusion Service and the Office of Homelessness
entries.025e6b298b9504ff2ff4784b20591948f412b06c: The three shuttle projects supported (CG25 0507) by the City of Montréal are complementary interventions that contribute to the establishment of an adapted transportation offer for people in a situation of homelessness in Montreal. Deployed in separate sectors, these projects participate in a concerted response to mobility issues observed in the territory and promote access to a network of support and accommodation resources. In order to better meet the needs observed and foster continuity of services, the City of Montreal wishes to enhance, at the request of the recipient organizations, the projects currently supported and ensure their continuation in 2027.

entries.24bb88e728ea598dffb80ddac1abe0b011270b2c: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater, ensure public health and safety, and protect the environment, today and for future generations. Its activities contribute to the protection of public health, the safety of the population and the preservation of the environment.

entries.5e67a309313e7099462a78395b756e630e9dc3e8: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (SMRA) is to ensure the availability and reliability of specialized vehicles and equipment required for the operations of the boroughs and central services of the City of Montreal. entries.bfc4e158349a83c7a0d413f7511dac185e182f56: Provide financial support of $8,600,000 to Mission Unités for the construction of a building on part of Lot 1,276,444 of the cadastre du Québec, Montréal Land Registry District, located in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairies– Pointe-aux-Trembles, to develop housing for low- and modest-income seniors as part of the financial contribution agreement for affordable housing between the Société d'habitation du Québec, Mission Units and the Fédération des Caisses Desjardins du Québec / Authorize the additional revenue and expenditure budgets equivalent to $6,519,080.72 for fiscal year 2026 and $2,080,919.28, for 2028 / Approve the Framework Agreement for this purpose
entries.f0d0351379039fc3c0615b7ed8b6ce752a93ec64: In order to address the housing shortage that particularly affects seniors in Quebec, Luc Maurice, founder of Groupe Maurice, who has created more than 12,000 units for older people, set up a non-profit organization Mission Unités (l'Organisme) whose mission is to develop affordable housing for households made up of independent elderly persons aged 65 and over with low incomes. In February 2024, the Organization entered into a Financial Contribution Agreement for the Development of Affordable Housing with the Société d'habitation du Québec (SHQ) and the Fédération des Caisses Desjardins du Québec (l'Agreement) for the construction of 10 buildings with 100 apartments each, totaling 1,000 affordable housing units intended for clients in the territory of Quebec. A first project in Montréal, in the Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve district, was carried out under this agreement and has been operating by the Montreal Municipal Housing Office (OMHM) since April 2026.
entries.c74679f75640ce819b54f71092f230cce005a9b4: Provide $500,000 in financial support to Société de développement Écoquartier Louvain from contributions from the social component of the Regulations aimed at improving the supply of affordable, family and social housing for the design of an off-market housing project in the borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville / Approve the draft convention to this effect
entries.4a24e61df3cffa1ff1c752e619cdcd50a75463d9: The City owns land in the borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville, bounded by the Canadian National (CN) railway right-of-way to the north, Rue de Louvain East to the south, rue Saint-Hubert to the west and Avenue Christophe-Colomb to the east. The City and Société de développement Écoquartier Leuven (SDEL) signed a collaborative agreement dated 9 July 2024 for the development of this site. This agreement is based on the will of the City and SDEL to develop and manage an exemplary and supportive neighbourhood that is part of the ecological transition and contributes to the resilience of the community of the entire sector (Ecoquartier) in accordance with the vision of affordability of housing, the sustainability of the Ecoquartier and its values, and the eco-citizenship.

entries.3d1f4e396e2224b18dbbc79a6c0f2f0dd847a138: Provide seven OTC professional services contracts to various agencies for the implementation of the Special Camp Intervention Program (SSP) - Total expenditure of $3,025,000, including taxes / Approve draft service agreements for this purpose / Authorize a budgetary transfer of $3,130,144 in 2027, $3,174,742 in 2028 and $3,205,346 in 2029 from the Office of Homelessness to the Diversity and Social Inclusion Service
entries.b81545646f9b0321e303cdcd809937d3eaa41672: The City of Montreal has established a Municipal Camp Management Protocol to provide coherent, concerted and respectful guidance for interventions with homeless people living in camps on its territory. The implementation of this protocol is based, among other things, on an accompanying approach by the persons concerned, as well as on sustained coordination between municipal, institutional and community partners. In this context, the Diversity and Social Inclusion Service (DISS) has put in place the Special Camp Intervention Program (PISC) to support the deployment of the Municipal Camp Management Protocol in territories with specific realities and needs for intervention.
entries.8a270ac0ae3231825190c9bc66aba231534641a0: Approve the draft Addendum 1 to the OTC Professional Services Agreement between the City and Mission Old Brewery (CG26 0472), to extend the term of the agreement to January 29, 2027 and authorize an additional expenditure of $176,220 including taxes, thereby increasing the total contract amount to $325,740, including taxes
entries.cef3f2aaa82814c455e5cc18036f755eafa9be63: Authorize the submission of an application for financial assistance under Component 2 of the Accelerating Local Climate Transition / Attest that all programming projects submitted in support of the application will meet the eligibility criteria and terms of the program, including, but not limited to, a partial or complete climate plan approved by the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change Control, Wildlife and Parks
entries.e6c2d437d86d65b823ceaac4b00dcaad1057529d: In December 2020, the Montréal agglomeration adopted Climate Plan 2020-2030 to deliver on its commitments to mitigate and adapt to climate change, as well as support for the ecological transition. This plan is part of the City of Montreal's objectives set out in its Strategic Plan Action for Montreal 2026- 2030 and is directly linked to the Government of Quebec's Green Economy (GEP) 2030 Plan, an ambitious initiative that recognizes the essential role of municipalities in achieving climate goals across Québec. The ENP Implementation Plan 2023-2028 provides that the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing (MAMH) and the Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) are jointly responsible for Action 4.2.1.2 – Accelerating local climate transition (ATCL).
entries.944645d6e1d7ee1139eb012f6f721989c8df1497: Authorize application for funding under the Municipal Water Infrastructure Program, Component 1 - Water Infrastructure, for various projects related to the main water system, main sewer system and wastewater treatment plant
entries.f480277aa0883f2faa7c087889459f14b9736aa5: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montreal community, manage stormwater and clean up wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety, as well as protect the environment, today and for future generations. The City of Montréal is committed to an ambitious program to rehabilitate and repair its water infrastructure, both in terms of the production and distribution of drinking water and the collection and purification of wastewater. To help municipalities ensure the sustainability of their infrastructure, the governments of Canada and Quebec have implemented several grant programs, including the Municipal Water Infrastructure Program (PRIMEAU).
entries.e18e276af94834152d82028ed21516390156a97d: To authorize an additional budget of $470,730.17 in expenditures equivalent to the additional revenue to the City of Montreal Police Service for 2026 from the Department of Homeland Security to transform proceeds of crime into concrete levers for action to strengthen public security
entries.331d90d6a3b13f55c08616463c4d31ace72837e1: Decree No. 328-2024, adopted in February 2024, aimed at amending the Law on Confiscation, Administration and Allocation of Illegal Proceeds and Instruments, introducing a simplified civil confiscation regime based on a reversal of the burden of proof and providing for a distribution of confiscated sums: 50 per cent to the Fund for Assistance to Victims of Crime; and 50 per cent to be shared by each organization that participated in the operations leading to the confiscation of property. This new framework allows for a significant increase in income related to the confiscation of criminal assets, particularly for municipal police forces.
entries.28d97cae132cfb02a5b69d9f65114ad045243cb6: Authorize the submission of an application for a grant to the Government of Canada's Natural Infrastructure Fund / Approve the Contribution Agreement for the Frédéric-Back Park Development Project, located in the Saint-Michel Environmental Complex
entries.76833dd386048832642b148ad6b29e4af3229887: Announced in June 2021, the Natural Infrastructure Fund (NIF) supports projects using natural or hybrid approaches to protect the natural environment, foster healthy and resilient communities, and contribute to economic growth and job creation. Natural infrastructure is a means for communities to use their ecosystems to improve quality of life, reduce pollution, improve biodiversity and habitats, and build resilience to climate change. The City of Montreal is strongly confronted with the effects of climate change and thus multiplies its actions to provide people with resilient living environments.
entries.b83fb8ebad75ed150eb4e47148410f386ec5d829: Return an amount of $203,429.70 to the Agglomeration Road Reserve / Authorize a transfer of $532,000 from the Highway Reserve to the Operating Budget of the Urban Planning and Mobility Service, to fund studies or analyses, as part of major partnership transportation projects and urban development projects
entries.db914a10650a330c66c34c97d356229fcccf304a: The Urban Planning and Mobility Service (UMS) is responsible for planning and guiding the realization of an attractive, inclusive and resilient Montreal for the benefit of the present and future population. It guides the development of living environments, landscape and heritage, while developing ecological mobility solutions. In recent years, several transfers have been authorized from the urban road reserve to finance studies prior to several projects carried out by the service.
entries.95d1c5b1d10975bdaa258248c3386a73fad7b556: On June 11, 2026, Bill No. 22 introduced section 31.5.5.1 of the Act respecting the treatment of municipal elected officials , which now allows a municipality to authorize advance payments to elected representatives in respect of amounts intended for the reimbursement of research and support expenses. This provision also provides that the council shall determine the terms and conditions applicable to the payment of such advances, including those relating to the repayment of sums paid in excess of the amount to which the elected officer is ultimately entitled. Up to now, the amounts intended for research and support expenses were not reimbursed until after the expenditure had been made and the required supporting documents had been submitted.
entries.b4bb19172bba8e5e4b51fe356141a19c0b30368d: Authorize advance payments to eligible elected members of the city council
entries.d383b61944c59b39b7b8ad60954669fea5ef84f8: Adoption - Regulations authorizing a $10,430,000 loan for the financing of the Biosphere Upgrade Project
entries.3be5c1f43de4b699588791dbc0daed28a564edd6: The only museum in North America dedicated to the socio-ecological transition, the Biosphere is a unique museum institution, an innovation space and an internationally recognized Montréal architectural icon. Since 2021, it has also been one of the five museum institutions of Space for Life. A place of exploration and dialogue, the Biosphere combines science, art and citizen perspectives to foster a better understanding of contemporary environmental challenges.
entries.ae1646f8dc63b79d01b6898f7d137f5afcce1217: Adoption - Regulations Amending the Regulations Respecting the Rate Share for the Provision of Meters and Related Delegated Activities (RCG 13-005)
entries.0643e5d59b5c2d9d4e064c31d3e16c98a0f7c70a: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. The Water Systems Directorate is responsible for the distribution of quality drinking water and the collection of wastewater by carrying out projects to upgrade and develop network assets, while ensuring their operation and maintenance. As part of the management of the Measurement of Water Consumption (MCE) program, the Water Service applies a rate share to distribute a portion of the cost of the program equitably among related municipalities based on the number of water meters installed in their territory.
entries.2b22c79564c0d262ef3208de708e86f64a677134: Renewing the mandate of Élyne Roko as an independent administrator on the Board of Directors of the Metropolitan Transport Network for a period of four years
entries.f8a16bc0400dfe93fdf06f164f94519f1a8cea69: Verdun District Council Resolution CA26 210161 - Statement to ask the next government of Quebec for a firm commitment to a high school in L'Île-des-Sœurs
entries.08939a405f69559fa0b51b180b573bf74773e662: Southwest District Council Resolution CA26 22 0154 - Statement in Tribute to Oliver Jones
entries.bdcdb1430be7e92d49cebe417931de9d27893f5f: Filing of the 2025 Review of Processing Access to Documents Requests
entries.c18f520da0ff702db959a892702ebf77c0227257: In June 2016, the City Council adopted a resolution providing for the production and filing of an annual review on the processing of applications for access to documents held by the City. The purpose of this report is to provide a structured and transparent overview of the number of applications received, the processing times, the types of decisions rendered, and trends observed over time. The City Council reaffirms its commitment to open and accountable governance.

entries.9d159fd8d10797505e81a329067b6fece1e02401: Declaration to mark the International Day of Democracy
entries.f175edca34cc58f264e3e1d1db064969bbba635b: Contract with 9125-5661 Québec inc. (Groupe Specs), for the supply and delivery of lighting equipment for Quartier des spectacles (Lot 1) - Total expenditure of $309,086.79, including taxes - Public tender 26-21395 (4 som.)
entries.4436a30b5782a33534ae390672057f8a30e32477: The Quartier des spectacles – Secteur de la Place des Arts project is a major initiative to strengthen Montréal's central role as a cultural metropolis. It focuses on three main areas: the development of public spaces that promote user-friendliness and accessibility; the redevelopment of streets to improve travel flow and user safety; the reconstruction of underground infrastructure to ensure the sustainability and modernization of essential networks.Strategic objectives: To consolidate the cultural vocation of the sector by providing places adapted to the holding of artistic and festive events; To position the Quartier des spectacles as an international destination, capable of hosting large-scale events; To create an attractive and inclusive urban environment, conducive to the cohabitation of residents, visitors and cultural actors.
entries.21895e9f820eba53891dc6714514aebb524a006d: Approve the agreement by which the City lends, free of charge, to the Centre de services scolaire de Montréal, for a period of two years and 15 days, effective August 17, 2026, Lot 6,641,111 du cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montreal, located south of Paré Street and north of Buchan Street, in the borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, with an area of 415.2 square metres for the purpose of installing trailer construction sites and parking workers' vehicles as part of the construction of a primary school. The amount of the real estate subsidy is $203,230.53 plus applicable taxes
entries.0258ac3f9d93626deff904828731332528a28a64: The Centre de services scolaire de Montréal (CSSDM) is preparing to build a primary school in the area of Triangle Paré-Buchan, specifically on Lot 6,641,112 du Cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montreal. A land for installing site trailers and parking workers' vehicles is required by the CSSDM in the vicinity of that construction site. Lot 6,641,111 du Cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montreal, has been identified by the CSSDM to accommodate the temporary facilities necessary to carry out the primary school project in the area of Triangle Paré-Buchan.
entries.d0521dcceafb12bcf4ebae0c981fcc7c608ac8ee: Allow an additional expenditure of $552,100, including taxes as contingencies, for air conditioning and dehumidification under the ice and in the changing rooms of Verdun's auditorium under the contract awarded to Construction Di Paolo Inc. (CM24 0875) / Authorize the transfer of $200,000, including taxes, from incidental expenses to contingent expenditures, thus increasing the maximum cost of the contract to $8,949,867.62, including taxes
entries.b2b4265242e24b0b95826c61b3052596e00445a0: The construction contract was awarded to Construction Di Paolo inc. on August 19, 2024. The work is aimed at increasing the capacity of air conditioning and dehumidification systems under ice as well as in the changing rooms of the Verdun Auditorium. Work began on September 23, 2024.
entries.498bcdd6aad4a99e25f2a8179a04ee4109cbb846: Contract with Can-Explore Inc. for reverse connection screening services in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairies– Pointe-aux-Trembles - Pointe-aux-Trembles area (Lot 1), for a 12-month period - Total expenditure of $321,925.69, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 26-21491 (1 compliant sum)
entries.f445dfa4f446fd920a778b196dfb2eb96cb2b31a: The mission of the City of Montreal's Water Service is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. Reverse connections are an important source of contamination in the rivers on the Island of Montreal. This problem arises when a sanitary connection is connected to the storm system or, conversely, when a storm connection is connected to the sewer system.
entries.c93a09509df34d3ee9fe80957b841966b28d7505: Conclude framework agreements with Guillevin International cie (lots 1-2-6), for the supply and delivery of street lighting equipment for the City of Montreal, for a period of 24 months, including three extension options. Estimated amount of framework agreements: $770,595.56, including taxes - Public tender 26-21430 (3 sum)
entries.e1e7b6efe1edd62d5df7b9e4a924721955f35151: The purpose of this file is to conclude six framework agreements for the supply and delivery on demand of street lighting equipment, primarily intended to maintain the assets of the public lighting system and replace damaged equipment. These framework agreements will be made available to all business units in the City of Montreal. In June 2024, contracts for the provision and delivery upon request of pedestrian drums, LED lights, nodes and gateways to the smart street lighting system for inventory were awarded, in accordance with the documents of the Public Call for Bids 24-20392, to the lowest compliant bidders, namely Metal Pole-Lite Inc., NEDCO Québec, Guillevin International Cie and LMPG Inc., for an estimated total amount of $3,688,224.93, including taxes.
entries.fc77d0b757443d7caf2c86aed5a4fc56f3290d6d: The purpose of this file is to conclude eight framework agreements for the supply of fire terminals and sewage and waterworks, primarily for repair and maintenance work for the City of Montreal's sewerage and water system. These framework agreements will be made available to all business units in the City of Montréal. In August 2025, contracts for the supply of fire stations and sewage and waterworks were awarded, in accordance with public tender documents 25-20801, to the lowest compliant bidders, namely Albert Viau and St-Germain Égouts & Aqueducts Inc., for an estimated total amount of $2,051,374, including taxes.
entries.263eba2d053277e6248a49bbf9a8dcde49477991: Approve the proposed bilateral promise by which the City undertakes to acquire from Claudio and Giorgio Masciotra and Michelina Fiorda (The C.G.A.S.E.N.C. Buildings) and Michelina Fiorda, on a personal basis, for local park purposes, vacant land with an area of approximately 400 square metres, known and designated as part of Lot 1,668,071 of the cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montreal, adjacent to the building bearing numbers 12265 to 12295 Rolland Boulevard, in the arrondissement of Montréal-Nord, for the price of $500,000, plus applicable taxes
entries.1c5c5bf582c9832e087ad7434a7c2b910575a3dd: Approve the proposed lease by which the City leases Speranza Spir, for a period of 16 months, effective October 1, 2026, room number 8, located at 251-A, Avenue des Pins Ouest, in the Plateau-Mont-Royal district, with a total area of 7.15 square metres, for office purposes for care activities and osteopathic and somatic workshops, for a total rent of $2,537.92, excluding sales taxes
entries.cd78c0dd7ab696a8b2c9b86f47616a64031a7567: In 2017, the City of Montreal (City) acquired the Religious Hospitallers of Saint-Joseph la Cité-des-Hospitalières (Cité), located at 201 to 251-A, Avenue des Pins Ouest (L'Immeuble). The City, as owner of this heritage site, has the responsibility to protect this environment and its cultural and landscape heritage. The City's protection efforts and the project to enhance the site must comply with the following five principles, enshrined in the act of sale: The preservation of the spirit of the place; Respect for the values of the Religious and their spiritual mission; Protection and sustainability of the built and natural heritage; Consistency with the history of the site; Openness to the community and the response to its needs.
entries.180facd929f2ad52f6a2972cfb26896edf971634: Approve the proposed lease by which the City rents Laurie Castels, doing business as My Creative Magic, for a period of 17 months, effective September 1, 2026, room number 1, located at 251-A, Avenue des Pins Ouest, in the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough, with a total area of 9.47 square metres, for office purposes and energy care activities, for a total rent of $3,580.65, excluding sales taxes
entries.48f6558b956ecc7c81a9f996ba5a1c764cd4c70b: Contract with Jacques Olivier Ford inc. (Lot 2) for the supply of vans and chassis-cabins with aluminium dumpsters - Total expenditure of $1,563,458.10, including taxes - Public tender 26-21455 (7 som.)
entries.88cc18e46c3783b78014c4e2020fd0783ba9068e: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (SMRA) is to ensure the availability, reliability and performance of municipal vehicles and equipment in support of the operational activities of the boroughs and corporate services. As part of the road network maintenance activities, the City of Montreal is facing a significant increase in response needs related to pavement degradation, particularly due to repeated freeze and thaw cycles. This situation results in an increase in pothole sealing operations and requires specialized equipment to improve the speed, efficiency and quality of interventions.
entries.1ae2db439b327a7f027be3378d2e2ad51833aef6: Grant a contract to Les Terrasses Multi-Landages inc., for development work in Jarry Park - Total expenditure of $1,386,774.32 including taxes - Public tender 25-6022 (4 som.)
entries.01962ae93c3b9fbb29add38d54a1bcb02beb6b9e: Jarry Park, located in the district of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension, is an emblematic green space that is highly appreciated by the population, both for the quality of its landscapes and for the diversity of its recreational activities. The frequent passage of the park's clientele, at the same places, has gradually created trails outside the official routes, justifying an intervention. This project aims to formalize and consolidate the informal paths of Jarry Park.
entries.31026808ca5632578f57598d1ad69898f082928c: Authorize the modification of the source of funding for the renovation work on the walls of the Querbes subway under the contract awarded to Construction Demathieu & Bard (CDB) inc. (CM26 0083)
entries.1a362f4df2dbbfea30679f8caa33347378151940: The Querbes subway is located on the axis of the Metropolitan Highway (A-40) in Montreal. These structures were built in 1957. The northern part of the subway is located in the Ahuntsic-Cartierville borough, while the southern part is located in the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough.
entries.019de633a279f19e08e9ddc4bc5e8cf49169475e: Conclude a framework agreement with Paris, Ladouceur et Associés inc. for professional property valuation services under Regulation 17-055 respecting contribution for park purposes, for a period of 24 months - Estimated amount of the agreement: $525,723.19, including taxes - Call for tender 26-21401 (2 Som.)
entries.af74da1a47fea53a5f02d3b321efbb2e7c481fe4: As part of the application of the Regulations Respecting the Disposal of Land or the Payment of an Amount for the Establishment, Maintenance and Improvement of Parks and Playgrounds and the Preservation of Natural Spaces or School Service Centres in the Territory of the City of Montreal (17-055), the boroughs of the City must have a certified assessor establish the value of a site, in accordance with section 6 of those Regulations, requiring the use of property valuation services. Effective June 19, 2018, these regulations require that any owner who applies for a subdivision permit to fragment land or construction permits in certain situations, including for the completion of a redevelopment project involving more than 2 housing units, assigns land free of charge or pays compensation for park purposes, as the case may be. This contribution shall not exceed 10% of the area or value of the site, while taking into account previous contributions.
entries.92bd9e8cec079fe11b4028bc8c202c423c4ea3f3: Provide financial support totalling $3,998,632 to various organizations for the period from October 1, 2026 to December 31, 2029, under the Voice and Action LGBTQ2IA+ 2026-2029 Program of the Diversity and Social Inclusion Service / Approve draft agreements to this effect
entries.5d86054bf361f4703d446117eb9f563eca412fef: The City of Montreal has allocated an annual budget of $1M to support community organizations working with LGBTQ2IA+ communities. This measure is part of municipal commitments to combat discrimination and promote inclusion, in accordance with the Montreal Charter of Rights and Responsibilities. Despite advances in recognition and rights, LGBTQ2IA+ people continue to face various forms of discrimination, harassment, violence and exclusion in several spheres of their lives.
entries.cca8b6f3df921afe18fdd3001777bc23bfe7f438: Contract with Salvex Inc. to repair basketball grounds at Jarry Park - Total expenditure of $703,053.74 including taxes - Public Call for Bids 26-6047 (3 sum)
entries.c99e86d2a3ff00ff9822ac6de03d110b6aead95b: The two basketball fields in Jarry Park, located in the borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Park-Extension, are among the most frequented facilities in this area. Their popularity is due to their strategic location, the quality of their layout and their high attendance by residents of the area as well as by players from different sectors of the city. The last intervention on these basketball fields dates back to 2015, when the lighting system had been replaced.
entries.820aac9f7f411e3054d04b29e02ef5585029925f: Grant a contract to Défensement ProQuip inc., for turnkey snow removal services for the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough, for a period of five winter seasons - Total expenditure of $22,042,432.13, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 26-21528 (5 sum)
entries.57808237a624126d231acf002969b7066b312a1b: The Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne (SCAEC) is responsible for the integrated planning of snow clearing operations on pavements and sidewalks, the launching of tenders and the award of related contracts. On August 5, 2026, the SCAEC launched a call for tender No. 26-21528 for turnkey snow removal services for the Plateau-Mont-Royal district. A notice was published on the Government of Quebec's electronic tendering system (SEAO) as well as in the daily Le Devoir.
entries.c16b05863448362488e3ac61035d96b8279e6899: On June 18, 2026, the Conseil d'agglomeration approved the draft exhibition agreement between the City of Montréal and Supply and Demand Inc. for the presentation of "Sensory L-odyssey" from December 5, 2026 to October 11, 2027 at the Biosphere. However, Supply and Demand Inc. informed the Biosphere on June 22, 2026 of recent significant organizational changes within the company, which was therefore no longer able to undertake this mandate in the parameters understood and wished to revise the financial terms of the agreement or significantly reduce the duration or scope of the project.
entries.ce0286026cb2010a1549280810207d75547df1ad: Offer to the borough of Sud-Ouest to take over acquisitions of land, cadastral operations and any alienations, agreements or steps required for carrying out related projects of the Complexe Turcot, in accordance with section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montréal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4)
entries.e1a80b4c53c6db3f41664c406c593695b5847a57: The reconstruction of the Turcot interchange carried out by the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable du Québec (MTMD) has led to significant changes in the surrounding areas of work in the South-West District. The Urbanism and Mobility Service (SUM) has been mandated to carry out projects related to this work with a view to requalifying this sector and reducing the nuisances associated with the highway. The Gadbois Pole projects, including the approaches to Highway 15 (A15), are thus the subject of collaborative agreements with the MTMD.
entries.df20bdbce86f5d3c433c16a03f611dfbedec65ba: Authorize the submission of two applications for funding to the Department of Transport and Sustainable Mobility under Project Call 2027-2028 of the Urban Active Transportation Development Financial Assistance Program for projects on Champlain Street and Saint-Jacques Street, and two other applications for financial assistance to the Active Transportation Infrastructure Financial Assistance Program (Véloce III) for projects on Guy Street and Laurier Street for the development or redevelopment of new cycle lanes or sidewalks, where required
entries.3cd8384dbe17f66a9739724ca0bb0f7b9a0aff40: As part of the Sustainable Mobility Policy 2030 and in line with the objectives of the Government of Quebec's 2030 Green Economy Plan, the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable (MTMD) seeks to develop alternative modes of transportation for cars, including bicycles and walking, in order to encourage the people of Québec, the ultimate clientele of the program, to opt for these more healthy, economical, ecological and safe means. The Program d'aide financière au développement des transports actifs dans les parcours urbains (TAPU) and the Program d'aide financière aux infrastructures de transport actives (Véloce III) are intended as accompanying tools for municipalities that aim at helping them take or continue a sharp turn in the supply of active transportation infrastructure in Quebec. The financial assistance provided by the Ministry through these programs can cover 50% of eligible expenses up to a maximum amount.
entries.c997c0d51f98b8d75caa930127f4dcf53356f77c: To adopt a resolution authorizing the partial use of amounts accumulated in the local "water and sewer" financial reserve, intended to fill the operating deficit, up to $2,100,000, necessary to enable the Water Service to meet future expenditures by the end of the year related to the smooth operation of operations.
entries.10b206ed236394485d85abb24f566d583b90355a: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water to the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean up wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety, as well as protect the environment, today and for future generations. In accordance with the Policy on the Management of Reserves of Funds, the Local Water and Sewer Financial Reserve provides a financial lever for the Water Service to support the needs of local water and sewer systems. Funds from this reserve can be used, among other things, to fund non-recurring expenses and one-time interventions required to maintain these assets in good condition and reduce the risk of failure and ensure continuity of services to the population.
entries.7e6f8016fed16c6e1ca6818525ec5372f2eae7d8: Under section 126.2 of the Municipal Jurisdictions Act (hereinafter referred to as the "MCA") and section 19 (11.1) of the Act respecting the exercise of certain powers in certain agglomerations, the Montréal agglomeration has powers to promote local and regional development in its territory. In order to exercise these powers, the City may enter into agreements with the departments or agencies of the Government of Quebec and, where appropriate, with other partners concerning its role and responsibilities, including the implementation of regional priorities and the adaptation of government activities to regional particularities. For these purposes, the City shall administer the sums entrusted to it under those agreements and have the powers necessary to carry out them.
entries.412d0488c22c1f90601341032166424ea5e26404: On October 20, 2017, the City of Montreal (the City) acquired, by deed No. 23,449,516, the site of the former Blue Bonnets racetrack (the Hippodrome), located in the borough of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (the Arrondissement), from the Société nationale du Cheval de course (SONACC) and the Government of Quebec. This site constitutes the last vacant land of such a size in the central areas of Montréal. It is currently undergoing a planning process led by the Urban Planning and Mobility Service (UMS), in collaboration with the Arrondissement and the Real Estate Strategy and Housing Service (SSIH).
entries.b70facb40c1c08d42eba8777d595b24f727bdb59: Notice of Motion and Tabling - Regulations for the Closure of an alley northeast of 18th Avenue between Ontario Street East and De Montigny Street, in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, for transfer to riparian owners
