entries.e77afd45165edb85446b793c1afd94d21a877a11: The Service de la stratégie immobilier et de l'habitation (SSIH) has received an application from a citizen to acquire the portion of the lane that is riparian to his property. Analysis of this application reveals that the alley originally known as Lots 1,260,852, 1,260,856 and 1,260,863, all of which are in the cadastre of Quebec and shown as an indication on the attached C and P plans, is entirely occupied by all the residents, numbering seventeen (17) and can be assigned. The necessary steps have been taken, with a view to the transfer of this lane, under administrative framework number C-OG-GPI-D-17-002 "Devolution of lanes to riparian owners – Terms and conditions", pursuant to the provisions of sections 179 to 185 of Schedule C to the Charter of the City of Montreal (Enframement).
entries.25df22771f4dfe4b794b4773c27e6264611f2a38: Adoption - Regulations authorizing a borrowing of $951,000,000 for the financing of work under the Water and Sewer Secondary System Renewal Program
entries.0db5bb1c950325003cff92b0601940f00d9b1540: Nearly 20 years ago, the City of Montreal committed to an ambitious infrastructure rehabilitation and repair program aimed at eliminating the infrastructure deficit and ensuring the sustainability of water systems. This program aims to improve the level of service provided to citizens by reducing service interruptions and emergency interventions resulting from outdated systems and network failures. The program also aimed to reduce the volume of leaks, thereby reducing the costs of maintaining networks, producing and distributing drinking water, and collecting and purifying wastewater.
entries.0289ad728e5f7df9ac66306f5290b196741b3a1e: Adoption - Regulations Amending the Montreal Heritage Board Regulations (02-136)
entries.7e1bd5bb116536fa183ce9ecdf846cd2e177ebae: The Conseil du patrimoine de Montréal (CPM), the Comité Jacques-Viger (CJV) and the Comité consultatif en reconnaissance (CCR) are advisory bodies of the municipal council whose mission is to provide independent advice in order to inform the City's decisions on certain matters. Created in 2002 by the adoption of the Regulation respecting the Conseil du patrimoine de Montréal (02-136), the CPM is the city's consultative body with respect to heritage matters and its mandate is to formulate opinions and make comments and recommendations in order to improve the understanding, conservation and presentation of heritage within the framework of the plans, projects and policies submitted to it, in accordance with the provisions of its constitution. Established in 2012 by the adoption of the Regulations concerning the Comité Jacques-Viger (12-022), the CJV is the city's advisory body with regard to planning, urban planning, architecture, design and landscape architecture.
entries.5038cbc01d09927cf7b1dfc35d1d4df8c58104c1: Adoption - Regulations Amending the Subsidy to Amend the Electrical Service Connection of Certain Vessels Regulations (S-6.01)
entries.008f8902b95def7a20575f0e962f6ee21441af60: Adoption - Regulations Amending the City's Rules of Procedure on the Delegation of Authority of the City Council to District Councils (02-002)
entries.75764b95091fccbd3607a8f158959f177566dc36: The City Council adopted the Regulation Respecting Tourist Accommodation Facilities (25-007) to oversee the operation of tourist accommodation establishments in principal residence on the territory of the City of Montreal. To ensure its application, the City Council amended the City's Rules of Procedure on the delegation of powers from the City Council to the borough councils (02-002) so as to entrust the District of Plateau-Mont-Royal with the application of Regulation 25-007 throughout Montréal. Subsequently, the City Council passed Resolution CM26 0721 to initiate the process of transferring this delegation to the borough of Ville-Marie.
entries.b2c4d719d598963d3eaa59ae2bffadc0f5015ab6: Adoption - Regulations Amending the Self-Service Parking Regulations (16-054)
entries.ed5f4fe744678e3efd964aba682afbe4f444dbb5: Since August 2016, the City of Montreal has put in place a regulatory framework for self-service vehicle parking (SLV) through the Self-Service Vehicle Parking Regulations (16-054) (CM16 0990). These regulations set out the requirements to be met for universal parking permits for SLVs. These universal licences are necessary for car sharing service providers to offer their full SLV service on the streets of Montreal.
entries.87819eca8acb932a77d36ed00c2461ce89f16e13: Adoption - Regulations authorizing a loan of $46,375,000 to finance the implementation of the Urban Forest Plan
entries.cbe3c94d3146e20f61fcb8f89e81f6da1b11477e: Since 2012, the City of Montreal has been carrying out plantations as part of the Canopee Plan, now integrated into the Urban Forest Plan (UFP). The City of Montréal has adopted various strategies or action plans to increase the presence of trees in its territory; Climate Plan 2020-2030 aims at reducing vulnerability to heat waves and reducing the area of islets of heat. The flagship action of the Climate Plan "Planning, maintaining and protecting 500,000 trees in areas vulnerable to heat waves" is an example of a measure put in place to respond to them.
entries.5fe468623b5878d06d017d401f46cebfd76019c3: Adopt, without change, pursuant to section 145.45 of the Planning and Town Planning Act (QLRR, chapter A-19.1), a resolution authorizing the construction of a mixed 10-storey building at the intersection of Jean-Talon Streets East and Buies Streets in the borough of Saint-Léonard, on Lots Nos. 1 124 222 and 1 122 578 of the cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montreal, in zones Cm-2320 and H-1910
entries.c793e27bfc94162aae2da4abef6e9a85c01326c4: An application is made under the new authority granted to municipalities for authorization of certain derogatory real estate projects, to authorize the construction of a mixed (residential and commercial) building with modulations to its volumetricity, but the highest part would reach ten (10) floors, on Jean-Talon Street East, in the territory of the Jean-Talon East USP. The enabling authority under section 93 of the Act to amend various housing legislation (S.Q. 2024, Chapter 2), since February 21, 2024, which provided for the possibility of adopting a resolution authorizing certain housing projects despite the urban planning regulations in force, in an accelerated manner, has been incorporated into the Planning and Urban Development Act (QLRA, chapter A-19.1), sections 145.45 to 145.49 of the latter since June 11, 2026.
entries.0955a4eefb34605eed861794b10e33427535f072: Name "Étienne-Côté crossing" means the pedestrian crossing connecting Decarie Boulevard with Ouimet Street, southeast of Morin Street, and consisting of Lot No. 2 190 749 du cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montréal, in the borough of Saint-Laurent
entries.119f2f52c82ca2f873584e3a02fcd790ae9b0d1d: The borough of Saint-Laurent wishes to perpetuate the memory of the Laurentian painter Étienne Côté, who died in 2022. The unnamed pedestrian passage linking Decarie Boulevard and Ouimet Street, in the heart of the cultural district of the borough, represents a local opportunity to welcome the name of artist Étienne Côté.
entries.5694d37a5d7db4a43c1900ab5cc1fbe6dd59c13b: Abolish and repeal the Montreal Urban Community Union Retirement Agreement
entries.97d75d6540861e0a2d941b15224c299aa33d68f2: As a result of the municipal reorganization that came into effect on January 1, 2002, the City of Montréal succeeded the Urban Community of Montreal (the "CUM") in all its rights and obligations. As such, it became the employer, as well as the promoter and administrator of the pension plans and pension agreements then established by the CUM. The Convention for the Retirement of Unionized Employees of the Urban Community of Montreal (the "Convention") took effect on January 1, 1992 and targeted certain blue-collar, white-collar and professional participants in the Pension Plan for Unionized Employees of the Urban Community of Montreal (the "Approved Plan").
entries.ccee27d7ce54962f882d0b15477c3aa0ec63f4be: Appoint Morad Bkhait and Thierry Petit-Phat as members of the Intercultural Council of Montreal for a first three-year term, beginning in September 2026 / Renewing Mohamed Noredine Mimoun's term as a member for a second three-year term, beginning in September 2026
entries.eff31f43b79fcb9263ef589f58ab3d8b1f091e65: The Montreal Council, the Montreal Intercultural Council and the Conseil jeunesse de Montréal Regulations (19-051) govern the operation of the ICD. These regulations provide that the ICD is composed of 15 members, including one person serving as Chair and two persons serving on the Vice-Chair (section 3). When there are departures or mandate purposes, vacancies must be filled.
entries.0fd58c8dd053cbf66581746648581ce45efe1ab2: Motion of the Official Opposition - Motion - To hold a public consultation of the Office de consultation publique de Montréal (OCPM) on the open water bathing project in Lachine

entries.4e3af29ab4b4cb378fcf7d6ce527fb343c6a6825: Conclude a framework agreement with Aqua Data Inc. for the provision of water meters from 50 to 300 millimetres without mechanical parts for the City's drinking water distribution system, lasting 24 months - Estimated amount of the agreement $341,721.77, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 26,21479 (1 sum)
entries.cb0d22846c43115c1c0ebbff9107e110cc314c7e: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater in order to protect public health, safety and the environment, today and for future generations. The Water Systems Directorate is responsible for the distribution of quality drinking water and the collection of wastewater, carrying out projects to upgrade and develop network assets, while ensuring their operation and maintenance. Since July 2012, the Water Consumption Measurement Section (WMO) has been installing water meters in industrial, commercial and institutional buildings (ICI), as well as in certain residential buildings.

entries.bd0e708ec91657d2ee5702e2199a7217ff6598ff: On May 15, 2025, the City of Montreal's agglomeration council approved a lease agreement for the rental of premises with an area of 21,925 square feet on the 10th floor of the building located at 1611 Crémazie Boulevard East, to relocate the Property Assessment Directorate of the Finance Service. entries.3db710672273dc73f7e9ec9829a650582fc015c8: Purchased by the City of Montreal (City) on December 8, 2020 for possible redevelopment, the building located at 7255 Saint-Urbain Street, in Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension borough ("the Building"), is currently leased to Mr. Nimalan Masilamany (the "Location") who has been operating a car mechanics workshop there since 2004. entries.cd9eb41df9803b37e58794237fea23295a9588a6: Provide $250,000 in financial support to École Polytechnique de Montréal, exclusively to support the five-year research program of the Mobility Chair (2026-2030) / Approve the draft convention for this purpose / Authorize a $50,000 budget transfer from the Directorate General to the Urban Planning and Mobility Service for the year 2026
entries.d1a089b81f9bacb0d8167a9212aedaf663123f7f: The Mobility Chair, led since its creation in 2010 by Professor Catherine Morency (Polytechnique Montréal), is a place dedicated to research, experimentation and methodological development to evaluate the contribution of transport projects, policies and plans to sustainable development. At the heart of her mission are the development of indicators of sustainable mobility, anticipation of their impacts, and training of highly qualified personnel in transport and mobility. Catherine Morency provides the definition and coordination of the research program and supervises the research team as well as students.

(CG26 0337) and regularize expenditures for these non-capitalizable works
entries.7f56236431987fbe4e8e010e904480cbafcb472e: Following the validation of the file by the Accounting and Financial Information Directorate, it appears that the expenditures incurred do not meet the criteria for recognition of tangible capital assets set out in Chapter SP 3150 of the Public Sector Accounting Standards and must be recorded on the results in the appropriate nature of expenditure. Indeed, the City's official documentation describes the Cross du mont-royal as a monumental cross erected for commemorative purposes, becoming an emblematic symbol of Montreal. entries.f2616034c0d4b5a93470143a5aec13e33b3d6af2: In 2023, the Major Parks, Mount Royal and Sports Service was responsible for the system of large parks, as well as corporate sports facilities. entries.823d741928026916a285bfc3e01ccbe4ceb1aa58: The maintenance of the City of Montreal's regional parks is provided through service contracts awarded to external suppliers, including for snow removal operations. entries.8adfdcd973ea56912154473817453b9fe6cd0d7a: Since 2012, the Service Espace pour la Vie, grandes parcs et Mont-Royal (SEPVGPMR) has been conducting interventions to combat the impacts of the ash grove. entries.2f679ce039ba5a4aa18bb452505c9e5c0328531e: The Société de transport de Montréal (STM) has undertaken a major renovation program for the Berri-UQAM station to ensure its sustainability and modernization, including the rehabilitation of its roof and upgrading of its infrastructure. entries.14d776f250dbe844ac81282aad2ee079b74dda19: Provide financial support totalling $760,033 to various organizations for the period from October 1, 2026 to March 31, 2028 under the Administrative Agreement on the Management of the Fonds québécois d'initiatives sociales - Alliances pour la solidarité (Ville-MTESS 2024-2029) / Approve draft agreements to this effect

entries.11f8cf4fd336b295c8ea70fcce452073dc56092c: The Ville de Montréal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montreal population, manage stormwater and clean up wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety while protecting the environment, today and for future generations. Québec municipalities are facing the ageing of their water infrastructure, a situation that can result in, among other things, failures, service interruptions and, in some cases, damage to essential infrastructures, both public and private. This creates major challenges in terms of continuity of services, safe drinking water supply and sustainable management of municipal assets.

entries.6669bf08ffef839bd8f84fdac53c8e80c652af7b: The Government of Quebec recently introduced the Small and Medium Enterprises Emergency Assistance Program (SMEAP) - U.S. Tariffs to support companies directly or indirectly affected by U.S. tariff measures. entries.035d3940faf801766b42dff02a5f8e90c0124a69: The Government of Quebec announced the creation of the Small and Medium Enterprises Emergency Assistance Program (SMEAP) – U.S. Tariffs to support companies directly or indirectly affected by U.S. tariff measures. entries.73fe9c50d7f26b51f2f08428aaacc8ce395a4010: Following the Declaration of Reciprocity concerning the new partnership between the Government of Quebec and local governments, concluded in 2023 and implemented in particular by the 2025 roadmaps, the Government of Québec renewed the Fonds régionalité et ruralité (FRR) for a new period beginning on April 1, 2025 and concluding on March 31, 2028. In this context, the FRR was renewed, with a revised structure to better respond to territorial realities. It is now divided into five components: Strand 1 – Regional radiation; Strand 2 – Territorial development; Strand 3 – Vitalisation; Strand 4 – Cooperation and municipal governance; Strand 5 – Local businesses.

In accordance with the Policy on the Management of Reserves of Funds, the general financial reserve for water is constituted: 1. amounts that the central municipality allocates annually 2. interest generated by the capital allocated to the reserve General reserve funds may be used to deal with unforeseen events of the Water Service and to finance non-recurring expenses. entries.a8a0dfd1d923463fac377238adbc652c289f5186: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) as a federal police force has a wide range of mandates and responsibilities related to organized crime. entries.6560a7f82055519629e1daacf5448f31d3c87221: In coming into force on June 26, 2013, subsection 2.0.1 of section 573 of the Cities and Cities Act (hereinafter referred to as "the VCA") granted municipalities the discretion "...to refuse any submission by a contractor or supplier that, in the two (2) years preceding the bid opening date, has been subject to an unsatisfactory performance assessment." This provision gives municipalities broad discretion as to whether or not to use a performance evaluation process and whether or not to consider an unsatisfactory performance evaluation when awarding a contract. On the recommendation of the Contract Review Board, by resolution CM13 1028 of September 24, 2013, the City Council requested that a performance evaluation system be put in place as soon as possible to adequately assess the performance and quality of work performed by contractors and products offered by suppliers.

entries.ae476272feb78a8ca3c6c621e20b8fcfa123b56d: Under the legislation applicable to the City of Montréal, the treasurer must file two comparative statements. The first, compares the revenues and actual expenses for the current fiscal year with those for the previous fiscal year for the period ending June and the second, compares the revenues and expenses of the municipality that are expected to be realized for the current fiscal year, at the time of preparation of the statement and based on the information available to the treasurer, with those provided for in the budget for that fiscal year (Act C-19 Cities and Towns Act; section 105.4). The projection of revenues and expenses for the twelve months of the current fiscal year was established on June 30, 2026 by the managers of the various business units of the City on the basis of the results for the first six months of fiscal year 2026.

entries.cff0cca935e099130c8b431f7b43755434d54b39: The Quartier des arts du cirque (QUAC) project aims to consolidate a local commercial artery on rue Jarry Est in the Saint-Michel district of Villeray-Saint-Michel-Parc-Extension. Through a three-stage entrepreneurial journey (workshops, creation of a container micro-commerce, and continuation of the entrepreneurial initiative in a mutualized premises), QUAC supports young people and entrepreneurs from immigration to their first business. Jarry Street East in Saint-Michel is one of Montreal's few commercial streets without real dynamism: few local shops, no local grocery stores, vacant premises and an unattractive street.

SOVERDI receives financial support under the Urban Forest Plan, a program managed by the Service Space pour la vie, grands parcs et Mont-Royal (SEPVGPMR) to achieve the objectives of the Climate Plan 2020 2030 and the Nature and Sports Plan.

entries.0e98f14e61e5dd0fbe89afa017b48dd9c2374da7: The Coopérative de solidarité Polliflora (Polliflora) is a non-profit organization whose primary mission is to maintain and promote the creation of an environment conducive to beekeeping through planting and storage of plants for urban farming purposes. In recent years, Polliflora has occupied a plot of land on the former site of the hippodrome. The borough of Côte-des-Neiges - Notre-Dame-de-Grâce (the Arrondissement) has mandated the Service de la Stratégie immobilier et de l'habitation (SSIH) to negotiate an extension of lease for an additional period of 2 years, in order to allow Polliflora to continue its activities.

entries.a9cd01c17e81bf8191f64c99e67b92059565a2b8: Since 2024, representatives of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM), the City and Hydro-Québec have engaged in discussions concerning work for the redevelopment of Hochelaga Street and for the construction of the new Hochelaga transformer post at Hydro-Québec in the district of Mercier–Hochelaga- Maisonneuve. entries.427de59d05eede849328ba98838c996211feb813: Conclude a framework agreement with Reliure Travaction (1991) inc. for 24-month document binding services to Montreal libraries - Estimated amount of the agreement: $633,814.06 including taxes - Public Call for Bids 26-21381 (1 sum)
entries.0e5e364003e52abd174b5072d3bac5affcc3fdb0: The purpose of this file is to enter into a supply framework agreement with Reliure Travaction (1991) inc. in order to meet the binding needs of Montreal libraries. These services strengthen and repair books and periodicals in order to extend their useful life and ensure that they are made available to the public in an adequate condition. The last supply framework agreement for bookbinding services for Montreal libraries, concluded with Les Reliures Caron & Létourneau ltée following the Public Call for Bids 23-19993, ended on October 19, 2025.
entries.c8213dcad86b9281d28eba64d7b66cb410ed6461: To conclude a framework agreement with Infrarouge Kelvin Inc., for professional thermography services, inspection of partial discharges of medium voltage cables and verification of the low voltage components of the underground structures of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal, lasting 36 months - Estimated amount of the agreement: $523,596.15, including taxes - Public tender S-2354 (2 som.) / To approve the draft service agreement to this effect
entries.92f63f3cce203f7a1313eeb1dfee8216d157c9cf: As part of its work to maintain and manage the city's underground duct system, the Commission des services électriques de Montréal must, prior to any request for access from its employees or external contractors, conduct thermographs and inspections of partial discharges for medium voltage cables as well as verification of low voltage components in accordance with the access standards set by Hydro-Québec, in order to ensure safe access to its structures. These thermographic readings and partial discharges must be performed by certified specialists and specialized equipment that the Commission des services électriques de Montréal does not possess which obliges it to employ an outside firm specializing in this type of service. The call for tenders was published in the SEAO electronic system as well as in Le Devoir newspaper on April 1, 2026.

entries.b39642efa4bafacce38540bee52c09e96ede976d: Grant an OTC contract to Telus in connection with the project to bury cable networks on Notre-Dame Street West between 6th and 20th Avenue, Lachine District - Total expenditure of $119,762.20 including taxes
entries.48c609f812eb6b7d5feeb85e8ace283e72fdbe45: Since January 1, 2000, the Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM) has been entrusted with the management of agreements concerning certain terms and conditions for cable networks between the City of Montreal and users with aerial cables in street poles. To this end, it has developed a plan that takes into account the budget estimates and the capacity to implement its partners. The Notre-Dame Street West project targets the section between 6th and 20th Avenue, in the Lachine borough, which is approximately 1,100 metres long and provides for the removal of 42 posts.
entries.dfd0dd440038426a7e8d5ade5a8ade91e010011c: Provide $3,300,000 in financial support to the Société du Musée d'archéologie et d'histoire de Montréal Pointe-à-Callière for the renewal of exhibitions and equipment, as well as the preservation of remains in 2026, 2027 and 2028 / Approve draft convention to this effect
entries.d7a6cd400323d83561a633e4fe5ccdff41ae5fb1: Since 1992, when the Pointe-à-Callière Museum opened, the Société du Musée has rented from the City of Montreal buildings in which part of the museum is housed: 150 St. Paul Street West, the Ancienne-Douane and 350 Place Royale, the Éperon Building, in addition to the undergrounds that connect the Museum's spaces, as well as 335 Place d'Youville (Caserne No.1). The Pointe-à-Callière Museum is one of the cultural facilities whose responsibility for management rests with the City Council under the Charter of the City of Montréal. To this end, an annual grant is paid by the City to this non-profit organization, according to a partnership agreement that has been renewed many times since 1992.
entries.c8b473d2e32f8c2d0440a8958e29e5bd7e9aae14: Exercising the option of the second 12-month extension and authorizing an additional expenditure of $1,148,505.88, including taxes, for the supply of cast aluminium parts for urban furniture in the City of Montreal under the framework agreement with Monmet Ltd. (CM24,0049), thereby increasing the total amount of the agreement to $3,346,999.88, including taxes
entries.0f6fc5d0ab59b5604f6cae184ab0bf51ac19feb9: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (SMRA) is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as to provide a variety of specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services, in an environmentally responsible manner and in a safe environment. In order to maintain its urban furniture fleet and carry out new facilities, the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (SMRA) has entered into a framework agreement with Monmet Ltd. for the supply of cast aluminium parts, which is essential for urban furniture in the City of Montreal.

entries.a402fa682e972b48dbc838d76d607a35a7f6193a: Conclude a framework agreement with Orange Traffic Inc., for the supply of traffic light structural equipment (Lot 1), lasting 24 months with a 12-month extension option - Estimated amount of the agreement: $1,486,848.65 including taxes - Public tender 25-21235 (2 sum)
entries.beac50f1bbc97e8f95dc072f6da39acaef4c9ca0: In its usual practices, the City of Montreal maintains an inventory of traffic light equipment in order to meet maintenance, modification and installation of new systems. To ensure optimal management of these requirements, continuous acquisitions of equipment are required, thereby maintaining an inventory of essential equipment and meeting project timelines. To this end, the Innovation and Travel Management Division (IOM) regularly solicits the market by entering into framework agreements to ensure consistency and ease of supply while building profitable economic stocks.
entries.e19b1668061c580094df08fff22175697646f518: Approve the proposed lease by which the City of Montreal leases to the National Research Council of Canada, for a period of two years, effective September 1, 2026, premises at 2300 Alfred-Nobel Street in the borough of Saint-Laurent, with a total area of 50.16 square metres, for office space purposes, for a total rent of $59,520, excluding taxes
entries.976c99a7b7c299d9a7d3e5d1ad3987a1e24eaf67: The City of Montreal (City) owns two rental buildings located in the Technopark of the borough of Saint-Laurent (Technoparc Montréal), namely, the Business Centres located at 7140 Albert-Einstein Street and 2300 Alfred-Nobel Boulevard. These business centres offer office space for small start-up companies operating in the technology and scientific research sectors. The Real Estate Rental Division of the Real Estate Strategy and Housing Service (SSIH) is responsible for renting the available spaces of these buildings and managing leases.
entries.7b66ebb5a01f934b5fb9e25d98d4700753e77bde: Authorize an additional expenditure of $1,221,409.32 including taxes, for contingencies and implications under the contract awarded to AECOM Consultants Inc., for professional design services for plans and specifications and monitoring of works for the renovation of the Jardins ouest du Jardin botanique de Montréal (CM24 0406), increasing the total expenditure to $6,595,610.32, including taxes
entries.17376922fa09ef3357dcaea4225e23ad2f9b0a1b: The renovation of the Jardins Ouest du Jardin botanique de Montréal is intended to improve accessibility and inclusiveness and enhance their heritage character. The project includes the redevelopment of six thematic gardens, the development of a new space for children and families, the narrowing of the West Belt Road, as well as the rehabilitation of sewerage lines by shelving. It also aims at preserving landscaped and built heritage, integrating the principles of universal accessibility and inclusion, taking into account existing constraints and creating a coherent and safe immersive route for visitors.
entries.b8655dc20d427af500ec56b31696285d1b3a04dc: Grant an OTC contract to Transvrac Montréal-Laval Inc., for snow transportation services in the arrondissements of Montréal-Nord and Plateau-Mont-Royal, for a period of one winter season, including a 12-month extension option - Total expenditure of $3,463,376.77, including taxes / Approve draft service agreement to this effect
entries.7fdebbc1452641ed2e54db074f0eedd74ac512bc: Since January 2016, the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne (SCAEC) has been responsible for the integrated planning of snow removal operations throughout the City of Montreal. As part of its responsibilities, SCAEC wishes to enter into a brokerage services agreement with Transvrac Montréal-Laval inc. (Transvrac) in order to ensure the transportation of snow in the districts of Montréal-Nord and Plateau-Mont-Royal.
entries.4b9c87e4e220b8943dcb023a4789f3c0593d0872: Contract with Centre Investigation & Sécurité Canada inc., for the services of curate clerks at snow disposal sites, for a two-year period, including two winter season extension options - Total expenditure of $605,576.19, taxes included - Public tender 26-21454 (7 som.)
entries.cafb28316358ac45c372f89c434f263ca93a659a: On June 10, 2026, the SCAEC launched Call for Bids No. 26-21454 for services of curate clerks in snow disposal sites (LEN). A notice was published on the Government of Quebec's electronic tendering system (SEAO) and in the daily Le Devoir.
entries.e25c2ff60fd2615ae481353640b6a84e740c8f4b: Contract with CMS Entrepreneurs Générales Inc. to refurbish and secure the Parc-La Fontaine Avenue Trail - Total expenditure of $4,011,678.85 including taxes - Public tender 25-6025 (6 som.)
entries.5d67619923ede35abfe2590787311c7dacbc41af: Located in the heart of the Plateau-Mont-Royal district, La Fontaine Park is an iconic park in Montreal, frequented by both residents of the area and visitors from all over Montreal. In order to ensure its sustainability and meet the challenges associated with its evolution, the City of Montréal has undertaken a thorough reflection on its future, which led to the adoption of the La Fontaine Park Management Plan in 2018. Since this adoption, several development and redevelopment projects have been carried out or are being planned.
entries.ced85d3bddcc90dbfecf204d1f317045cb0cd5c3: Award a contract to 9519-4668 Québec inc. (Goldiator towing) for snow removal services in the borough of Montréal-Nord, for a period of three winter seasons, including an option to extend a winter season - Total expenditure of $678,915.88, including taxes - Public tender 26-21465 (8 som.)
entries.5eee955f0f65cd8f205d89a39e01277eb6af272c: Contract with Fraco Products Ltd. for the manufacture and delivery of custom crowd control barriers for the Quartier des spectacles - Total expenditure of $185,904.23, including taxes - Public tender 26-21405 (3 som.)
entries.cf1be66c989419b07e2d73cc7fc7c90a257b17ae: The Quartier des spectacles – Secteur de la Place des Arts project is a major initiative aimed at strengthening Montréal's central role as a cultural metropolis. It focuses on three main areas: the development of public spaces that promote user-friendliness and accessibility; the redevelopment of streets to improve travel flow and user safety; the reconstruction of underground infrastructure to ensure the sustainability and modernization of essential networks.Strategic objectives Consolidate the sector's cultural vocation by providing suitable venues for artistic and festive events; Position the Quartier des spectacles as an international destination, capable of hosting large-scale events; Create an attractive and inclusive urban environment, conducive to the cohabitation of residents, visitors and cultural actors.
entries.abc8c2915fbd26837d57465ee2887a3959e84946: Approve two agreements between the Minister of Municipal Affairs, the Chief Electoral Officer of Quebec and the City of Montreal to carry out two pilot projects in any by-election that may take place before the general election of 2029, allowing the inclusion of photographs of candidates on ballot papers and the presentation of a web profile of candidates
entries.cc815169d4b9b1aceaf9cbb6a88a98cbcda1025d: The 2025 general election filled the 103 elected positions of the City of Montreal for a period of four years. Between two general elections, an elective position may become vacant for various reasons. If the vacancy of an elected person is found more than one year before a general election, the Municipal Elections and Referendums Act (MRL Chapter E-2.2) provides for the filling of the position by means of a by-election.
entries.3259af495d6e8ea722d1fc6171ca7be73b096b6d: Grant an OTC contract to CCxA for the professional services required for the return of the artistic facility 18 Gay shades, including an exhibition licence, as part of the Sainte-Catherine East project in the Village, for a period of 10 years - Total expenditure of $984,996.39, including taxes / Approve the Professional Services Agreement to this effect
entries.3c2eb00802ff5572615967dce8818773289fc4f6: On April 1, 2026, the SCAEC launched Call for Bids No. 26-21383 for services to operate the snow disposal site (LEN) Langelier located in the Saint-Léonard district. A notice was published on the Government of Quebec's electronic tendering system (SEAO) and in the daily Le Devoir.
entries.10eaabc45aca735032cc151e201ee334755a9df0: The Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne (SCAEC) is responsible for the integrated planning of snow removal operations on pavements and sidewalks, the launching of tenders and the award of related contracts. On June 1, 2026, SCAEC launched Call for Bids No. 26-21431 for turnkey snow clearing services for the boroughs of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Thankse, Lachine, Outremont, Plateau-Mont-Royal and Sud-Ouest. A notice was published on the Government of Quebec's electronic tender system (SEAO) as well as in the daily Le Devoir.
entries.262e5ecad66170bf572b8c119ae0e79b89951aaa: Contract with J.A. Larue inc., for the supply of two mechanized nest-of-blow padding machines - Total expenditure of $781,460.93, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 26-21476 (3 som.)
entries.5ff8dcd115b5be73606d8c688babfa236ccb1f86: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (SMRA) is to ensure the availability and reliability of specialized vehicles and equipment required to support the operations of the boroughs and central services of the City of Montreal, while providing solutions tailored to the operational needs of the territory. For several years, the City of Montréal has been implementing various strategies aimed at optimizing pavement repair operations and reducing response times related to potholes. In this context, a mechanized locking project has been implemented to improve the efficiency of collating operations and the general condition of pavements.
entries.180ad7a711d4508cfcb0df6dcd5dd029cb84e62a: Grant a contract to Globocam (Montreal) Inc., for the supply of four 6 x 4 trucks with insulated and heated tilting asphalt box - Total expenditure of $1,751,902.13 including taxes - Public Call for Bids 26-21464 (2 som.)
entries.104034fd37738e04496c986ad33e441a92028924: To authorize a budgetary transfer of $6,599,000 net of rebates and grants from the Ten-Year Capital Program of the Culture, Sports and Recreation Service to the borough of Saint-Léonard for the year 2026, to complete the development of the soccer site with a permanent inflatable structure at Hébert Park, as well as a transfer of authorized appropriations for the borough for a total of $6,691,074.76 net of rebates required for the continuation of the project
entries.feea5f387f01a690e5876effc65b6e217d01a822: As the decision summary is to be submitted to the Municipal Council on August 24, 2026, rather than in June 2026, the borough of Saint-Léonard was required to pay invoices from the general contractor responsible for the work before that deadline. This situation requires us to revise the cost apportionment and therefore recalculate the balance to be transferred to the borough of Saint-Léonard. Accordingly, this addendum amends the following elements of the decision summary: 1.
entries.06f1d471faa7f8817983ff2bfb855af5b61d9f3b: Increase the allocation of the borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Park-Extension, through the environmental liability reserve, in the amount of $168,472.14, net taxes, to cover environmental rehabilitation work as part of the development of George Vernot Park, Lot No. 792, and the cost of professional services for environmental monitoring as a result of redevelopment
entries.d6d67382e304c697d44bec7f6d42d0f485e86ea0: By resolution CA26 140173, adopted at its meeting on July 7, 2026, the Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension District Council recommends that the City Council increase the allocation of the borough of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc- Extension, through the environmental liability reserve, for an amount of $168,472.14 net taxes, to cover all environmental rehabilitation work in connection with the development of George Vernot Park, Lot No. 792, as well as the costs of professional services for environmental monitoring following the renovation work. The purpose of this summary is therefore to forward the file to the City Council.
entries.d97bad78e966ec8e0f88c4f69502f2b206958219: Remove from the public domain street (public square) Lot 6 141 365 from the cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montreal, with a maximum area of 899 square meters, located at the south-east intersection of Sherbrooke Street East and Langelier Boulevard, in the arrondissement of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, to pay it into the public domain as a local park, as part of a project to develop this space
entries.a7ff2caeddd75a73e6406b3ccd6dbd072beb6671: By resolution CA26 27 0191, adopted at its ordinary session of June 29, 2026, the Mercier-Hochelaga-Maisonneuve borough council recommended that the municipal council remove from the public domain street (public square) lot 6,141 365 from the cadastre du Québec, located at the southeast intersection of Sherbrooke Street East and Langelier Boulevard, and transfer it to the public domain as a local park, as part of a project to develop this space. The purpose of this summary is therefore to forward the file to the executive committee.
entries.f06c15a544470a2047cf644d994302133302bf5d: Approve the extension of business hours at Plateau-Mont-Royal during commercial promotions from September 17 to 27, 2026
entries.38df87e2c677e5ca88f5b076aa025adb211f3bf3: VALIDATION Intervenor et sense de l'intervention Other intervenor et sens de l'intervention Stakeholders Reading: RESPONSIBLE DU DOSSIER Benita DEGBOE File Analyst - - Tel : Telecop. : - EXECUTIVE SUMMARY DECISION IDENTIFICATION File #:1267896007 Unit administrative Arrondissement Le Plateau-Mont-Royal , Direction du responsable : développement du territoire et des études techniques , Division de l'urbanisme_du patrimoine et des services aux entreprises Level of decision-making Proposed municipal council: - Re: Recommendation to the municipal council to extend business hours at Plateau-Mont-Royal during commercial promotions in the fall of 2026 CONTEXT CONTENT On September 21, 2017, the Act increasing the autonomy and powers of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec came into force. This Act gives the City, among other things, certain powers related to the application of the Act on hours and days of admission to commercial establishments.
entries.d98b6004b81248bcfde21fe78ccf53626d3db43c: Increase the staffing of the Building Management and Planning Service, through the Environmental Liabilities Reserve, for $67,482.28 net taxes ($73,901.89 including taxes), for the professional fees of Les Services EXP inc., relating to the monitoring of soil and contaminated water on site 051761 located at 3550 Saint-Patrick Street, Southwest District
entries.a274cf6cc6878116d455955c08ed08212ca568ca: Since December 2024, the City of Montreal has owned the site located at 3550 Saint-Patrick Street, formerly operated by Suncor for oil activities carried out between 1915 and 2000. The land contains contaminated soil and water that exceed regulatory criteria. Following the acquisition of Suncor's land, the City must follow up to meet its environmental obligations, document the evolution of contamination and maintain management measures to control environmental risks.
entries.7dd3a5a387ce7bbc184f9d626d417612f1d1e76f: Accept the offer of services of the borough of Montréal-Nord to take over the design, coordination and implementation of the renovation work for the carriageway section in front of 5542 Léger Boulevard, part of the administrative arterial network of the City located on the territory of the borough, in accordance with section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4)
entries.53c168565a7841072c22e667ce278ee1b8465e1a: The Road Infrastructure Service (SIRR) is responsible for the rehabilitation and maintenance of the assets of the arterial road network of the City of Montreal (RAAV), which is the jurisdiction of the City's Council under the Charter of the City (section 87, paragraph 6, and section 105). Knowing that the street on which an intervention is to take place falls within the jurisdiction of the City's Council, the Arrondissement de Montréal-Nord has offered to carry out the work there pursuant to section 85, paragraph 2, of the Charter of the City of Montreal, which states that "A borough council may, on such terms as it determines, provide the City's Council with a service connected with a jurisdiction falling within its jurisdiction; the resolution of the borough council takes effect from the date of adoption by the City's Council of a resolution accepting the provision of services".
entries.939652daa80433c29832fd12cfbf3da1f5ab94ef: Approve amendments to the resolution establishing the Order of Montreal
entries.aed7fc1cb88fa87e6e98bb58fcb3438384fefe20: Amendments have been made to the resolution establishing the Order of Montreal (the Order), which serves a variety of purposes, including: providing terminology clarifications to avoid ambiguity; making certain adjustments to the process; clarifying the definition of criteria; simplifying the text; and making editorial adjustments. This approach is intended to update the resolution establishing the Order of Montreal so that it adequately reflects the evolution of practices, issues and realities observed since its last revision in 2018.
entries.2400c9ab1a7908e3c2dcf0f9061e13c5b85b9a87: To approve, with reservation, the Planning of Space Needs 2026 of the Montreal School Services Centre
entries.ddf91681eef7693ccccb618db750aef647635ca0: The Centre de services scolaire de Montréal (CSSDM) transmitted its Space Needs Planning (PBE) to the City of Montreal (Ville) on July 14, 2026. Pursuant to sections 272.6 and 272.7 of the Public Education Act (PIA), the City must approve or refuse the content of PBE within 45 days, no later than August 28, 2026. The purpose of the PBE process is to provide a framework for the exchange of information and positioning on school building requirements between school service centres (SSCs) and municipalities in order to plan land transfers free of charge.
entries.9bd2eb61163f6d1e0e18ea8615b92fdf6a275f59: Accept the offers of services offered by the councils of boroughs of Anjou, Outremont, Villeray–Saint-Michel–Park-Extension and South-West, to assume responsibility for coordinating and carrying out street development work forming part of the administrative arterial road network of the City of Montréal for the year 2026, in accordance with section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4)
entries.459b0d1c6f694cd7a4f5430742b105839dffc866: The City of Montreal's Urban Planning and Mobility Service (SUM) is responsible for the planning and development of the city's arterial road network (RAAV), which falls under the jurisdiction of the City Council under the City Charter (Art. 87(6) and Art. 105). Knowing that the streets on which they wish to intervene fall within the jurisdiction of the City Council, boroughs have offered to carry out the work there pursuant to section 85 of the City of Montréal Charter, which states that "A borough council may, subject to the conditions it determines, provide the City Council with a service linked to a jurisdiction falling within its jurisdiction; the resolution of the borough council shall take effect from the date of adoption by the City Council of a resolution accepting the provision of services." The acceptance of borough offers of services, in respect of redevelopment projects to be carried out in 2026, constitutes the subject matter of this file.
entries.d111b5b8f38efd40f7b07b9a4385905a11a3bdde: Increase the allocation of the Urban Planning and Mobility Service from the environmental liability of contaminated soils in the amount of $70,980.65 net taxes to conduct soil characterization studies related to the Highway 15 Urban Woodlot Project on the land of acquisition lots 1,573,778, 1,573,998, 1,573,970, 5,663,854, 6,247,589, 5,663,856, 2,357,108, 2,357,109, 2,357,110, 2,357,111, 1,573,778, and 1,573,997 of the cadastre of Quebec, Registration Division of Montreal

entries.4fbe3fc83e9bb0dee2753e43b38b1c1b5ff91ca0: To extend, until September 22, 2031, the declaration of competence of the council of the City with respect to the exercise of the powers relating to the performance assessment of contractors and suppliers provided for in the Act respecting contracts for municipal bodies (RLRQ, c. C-65.01), with the exception of the power to refuse any submission by a contractor or supplier which, during the two years preceding the date on which tenders were opened, has been subject to an unsatisfactory performance evaluation, to the extent that such submission is deemed to be the lowest compliant, in accordance with section 85.5 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4)
entries.fa9d57deb29d77dc3b0d955093fe5d28fad582e7: In 2013, on the recommendation of the Contract Review Board, the City Council requested that a performance appraisal system be put in place as soon as possible to adequately assess the performance and quality of work performed by contractors and products offered by suppliers. Subsequently, as of 2015, pursuant to section 85.5 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (the Charter), the City Council has declared itself competent, with respect to all boroughs, with respect to the exercise of powers related to the performance evaluation of contractors and suppliers provided for in subsection 2.0.1 of section 573 of the Cities and Cities Act, except for the power to refuse any submission by a contractor or supplier which, during the two (2) years preceding the date of opening of tenders, has been subject to an unsatisfactory performance evaluation, to the extent that such a bid is deemed to be the lowest compliant bidder.
entries.1b062c365a2467b11ce719b8ffd3405b3d1efa65: To extend, until September 22, 2031, the declaration of jurisdiction of the council of the City with respect to the adoption and application of the Regulations respecting contractual management, in accordance with section 85.5 of the Charter of the City of Montréal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4)
entries.0d2de20e96e6fd3fdf442c2524e1315a09cdf752: Accept the offer of service of the Conseil d'arrondissement de Montréal-Nord to assume responsibility for the design and implementation of the work of construction of donkeybacks on streets forming part of the administrative arterial road network of the City for the year 2026, in accordance with section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4)
entries.fb20967f681731df7b1e8585befea7312078da37: The City of Montreal's Urban Planning and Mobility Service (SUM) is responsible for the planning and development of the city's arterial road network (RAAV), which falls under the jurisdiction of the City Council under the City Charter (Art. 87(6) and Art. 105). Knowing that the streets on which it wishes to intervene fall within the jurisdiction of the City Council, the borough of Montréal-Nord has offered to carry out the work there pursuant to section 85 of the City of Montreal Charter, which states that "A borough council may, subject to such conditions as it determines, provide the City Council with a service related to a jurisdiction falling within its jurisdiction; the resolution of the borough council shall take effect from the date of adoption by the City Council of a resolution accepting the provision of services." The acceptance of the borough's offer of service, in respect of redevelopment projects (addition of donkey back) to be carried out in 2026, constitutes the subject matter of this file.

entries.6664b130d3417813a2485ab13ccf838e6a960561: Notice of Motion and Filing - Regulations Amending the Subsidy to Amend the Electrical Service Connection of Certain Vessels Regulations (S-6.01)
entries.eca1f46c315da92a2bb5eff904450a93d593e700: Notice of Motion and Tabling - Regulations Amending the City's Rules of Procedure on the Delegation of Authority from the City Council to District Councils (02-002)
entries.c6f7e63fed936079d784cdf78c80459096888510: Notice of Motion and Filing - Regulations Amending the Self-Service Parking Regulations (16-054)
entries.86701bbdcb0a2e784277d690b4e6907e043427d4: Notice of Motion and Tabling - Regulations Respecting Identification as a Historical Event of the Signing of the Treaty of Great Peace of Montreal
entries.6a5744ef9af272527573453c1e23453a1e7c71dc: As part of the 325th anniversary of the signing of the Treaty of the Great Peace of Montreal, the City of Montréal wishes to undertake various actions to mark this major historic event. Several municipal departments propose initiatives to contribute to this commemoration. In this context, the Heritage Division wishes to initiate an approach to officially identify the signature of the Treaty of 1701 as a historical event, which would give it heritage status under the Cultural Heritage Act (CPA).
entries.f4800011a3b77c31504d88a2b8a4117f05dafbed: Notice of Motion and Tabling - Laurier Palace Fire Historical Identification Regulations
entries.c12f6ad5a44370e87f06e0a78026d6ec591ab51e: As part of the 100th anniversary of the fire that ravaged the Laurier Palace in the Hochelaga neighbourhood on January 9, 1927, the City of Montreal would like to take various actions to mark this major historic event. In this context, several municipal services are proposing initiatives to contribute to this commemoration. In this context, the Heritage Division wishes to initiate an initiative to formally identify this tragic fire as a historical event, which would give it heritage status under the Cultural Heritage Act (CPA).
entries.a0a2fb4b070016d6fba3a9a09c96821a601311e1: Notice of Motion and Filing - Regulations authorizing a loan of $46,375,000 to finance the implementation of the Urban Forest Plan
entries.f0589b3efcaf60951a136bab0b9dc7adf4297b4e: Adoption - Regulations respecting the closure of a part of the alley to the southwest of 89th Avenue, between Rue Eugène-Couvrette and Boulevard Perras, in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, for transfer to riparian owners
entries.05b998659ab32796b23fde617399abc495e7150b: The Service de la stratégie immobilier (SSI) has received an application from a citizen to acquire the riparian lane at its property, located southwest of 89th Avenue, between Rue Eugène- Couvrette and Boulevard Perras, in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux- Trembles. Analysis of this application reveals that the portion of the alley shown as indicative on plans B, C and P annexed, is entirely occupied by all the riparian owners. The necessary steps have been taken to transfer this part of the alley, now known, according to plan Q-143 Rivière-des-Prairies, as being lots 4,522,523 to 4,522,548 inclusive, 6,395,913 to 6,395,916 inclusive and 6,685,500, all of which are from the cadastre du Québec, the real estate electoral district of Montréal.
entries.80f0ef26fdd10f2f59797d536cb20a6ff485fa00: Adoption - Regulations authorizing a loan of $177,837,000 for the financing of construction, repair and improvement of sports and aquatic equipment
entries.4d4a54d223db1e278f2ae3334e99a616f30a8828: The City of Montreal has developed planning tools that provide a common vision and direction for the development of physical activity and sports practices such as: The Montréal Aquatic Intervention Plan adopted by the City Council in April 2013; The Sport and Physical Activity Policy adopted by the City Council in November 2014. As part of the Capital Program 2026-2035 adopted by the City Council, the Service de la culture, des sportes et des loisirs plans to invest in the number invested 38370 - Sports Facilities Development Projects brings together the Gadbois Recreational Sports Centre project and the Montreal-North Aquatic and Sports Complex project.
entries.df887bc874df4f619e1db081d8c0c965fdc4fae6: Montreal is facing an acute housing crisis. In this context, the proliferation of illegal short-term tourist rentals helps to remove units from the residential rental stock. In order to respond to this pressure, the City of Montréal has already adopted a tight framework, including a ban on short-term tourism rentals outside authorized periods.
entries.82a209ef6938155b59690e6b8b7589a8954aea46: Adopt a draft resolution, pursuant to section 145.45 of the Planning and Town Planning Act (QLRR Chapter A-19.1), authorizing the construction of a mixed 10-storey building at the intersection of Jean-Talon Street East and Buies Street in the borough of Saint-Léonard, on lots Nos. 1 124 222 and 1 122 578 of the cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montréal / Held a public consultation
entries.f282a637ea615dcee5b4aee1891872e7a2c5359f: Adoption, without change, of Regulations Amending the Housing Safety, Maintenance and Security Regulations (03-096)
entries.011ff0e831d8b19cf5679fcb1a914e8e5460b0fe: Name "place Chez-Marguerite" the new public square located at the corner of Rue Charleroi and Avenue L'Archevêque, in the arrondissement of Montréal-Nord
entries.ff0f1195296c6662d6c8398547946748e6106e64: On 29 September 2025, following a proposal by the Consultative Committee on the Toponymy of Montreal-Nord, the borough council adopted a resolution asking the municipal council to appoint "place Chez-Marguerite" as the new square set up in 2025 on Rue de Charleroi, at the intersection of Avenue L-Archêque. This proposal aims to recognize the local involvement and dynamism of a businesswoman from Montréal-Nord, Marguerite Dugal-Ricard (1907-1981).
entries.b912badc9a9a530d6e6d3ff01d9f7b25ee2dcf63: Rename "arena des Patineuses" the Saint-Louis Arena, located at 5633 Saint-Dominique Street, in the Plateau-Mont-Royal district
entries.c37bf41ed6c424f50cf7b424a85673b35c8157c1: Early in 2026, the Plateau-Mont-Royal district contacted the Heritage Division to change the common name of the Saint-Louis Arena, a municipal building located at 5633 Saint-Dominique Street, built in 1981 and closed for modernization work since 2024. The district wanted to take advantage of the reopening planned in the fall of 2026 to announce a new name for the Arena, a name that highlights the presence of women in ice sports.
entries.497fd9308cb43ef798eefa4d9ebc333a7ac1283f: Name "Espace Thirteen" the place of creation and diffusion located at 13, Avenue Strathyre, in the district of LaSalle
entries.8cfeb5eaaed2c05025601d8ec305d1531710bd7b: The LaSalle district is currently developing the site of the former LaSalle Town Hall, located at 13 Strathyre Avenue, as a cultural hub, particularly because of its proximity to the Fleming Mill, the historic emblem of the district. Work is under way and progress is being made in accordance with the established timetable. To date, the construction site has achieved a rate of progress of about 80%.
entries.33e8094c28e6c45c0acfa90469e9a8a038f8aca9: Name "Sisters du Bon-Conseil Park" located east of Basile Routhier Street, between Gouin Boulevard East and Park Avenue Stanley, in the district of Ahuntsic-Cartierville
entries.7f2b5bbbc64fdcc55ab9312cc1e5b48a6bb9eff2: Since 2017, the district of Ahuntsic-Cartierville and the Heritage Division have been working to clarify toponymy in the vicinity of the Viau Bridge. As part of this file, it is hoped that Basile Routhier Park, whose name is common, will be named "Sisters du Bon-Conseil Park".
entries.b1db2fa5195a4d09e57872bd19fb605c2f51171e: Name "Place des Pointerolles" the new square in the right-of-way of Colonial Avenue, between Elmire and Demers streets, in the Plateau-Mont-Royal district
entries.6b090714602ebb4596061f1dde180d3ff508950e: In early 2026, the Plateau-Mont-Royal district contacted the Heritage Division to initiate an initiative to appoint a new school square in front of the Saint-Enfant-Jésus school on Colonial Avenue between Elmire and Demers streets. The square is located on the roadway in the right-of-way of the Colonial Avenue.
entries.61872a1336aebd2cb8453929b72b7dbbb5d3fc51: Appoint Julie-Pascale Provost, Mayor of the borough of Lachine, as the City's representative at the office of trustees of the Société d'archéologie et de numismatices de Montréal (Museum of the Château Ramezay)
entries.278c43bf0ef353781dea6a2ad31ff03fa944d73e: In 1862, the Société d'archéologie et de numismatiques de Montréal was founded and mandated to promote numismatics and "antiquarian" research, as well as the creation of a collection of coins, medals and antiques. It was also interested in the conservation and presentation of Montreal's heritage. In 1893, on the verge of being sold by public auction by the Quebec government, Château Ramezay was threatened with demolition.
entries.9fd19232cde402e702d09e11fbca9cf9fd738046: Appoint Maude Théroux-Séguin, Mayor of the borough of Ahuntsic-Cartierville, as an observer member on the board of directors of the Conseil du système alimentaire Montréal, for a period of three years, until July 24, 2029
entries.fe7d2d4a8b289538f3df0abef5b61823743a1fbf: The Conseil du système alimentaire Montréal (SAM) is a regional network comprising several food partners (production, processing, distribution, consumption and post-consumption). Its mission is to provide strong regional leadership in the field of food by mobilizing stakeholders, advising decision makers and supporting structuring initiatives. Created in 2018, the Conseil SAM (CSAM) is the decision-making body of the SAM and brings together members from various backgrounds (economic, academic, institutional, philanthropic, community, etc.).
entries.6f94956387647caf906da8c274940c41785d78c0: Appoint Sarah-Maude Cossette, Kenza Chahlouni and Marie-Ève Voghel Robert as a member of the Conseil des Montréaliennes for a first or second three-year term beginning in August and September 2026 / Appointing Meryem Benslimane as Vice-President of the Conseil des Montréaliennes for a two-year term beginning in August 2026
entries.fec3878cd7c58c1868c7d14e0fe56db5c808338e: The Montreal Council, the Intercultural Council of Montreal and the Conseil jeunesse de Montréal (19-051) regulate the functioning of the Conseil des Montréaliennes (CM), in particular the number of members constituting the Council and their qualifications. These regulations provide that the Council is composed of 15 members, including one person serving on the Chair and two persons serving on the Vice-Chair (Article 3). When there are departures or terms of reference, vacancies must be filled within 6 months.
entries.477bcd548bf59a16adad767af0f420c4efba935a: Motion of the Official Opposition - Motion to demonstrate the City of Montreal's solidarity with the Palestinian people and civilian victims of the conflict in West Asia, commonly known as the Middle East
entries.712ec8a970f6b14ee0f84324895893660f76140e: Motion of the Official Opposition - For the conservation of the tunneler "Lisette" in order to support the future development of the public transport network of the metropolitan region
entries.f1e9e30d4f2d08f183709c8e96a1d4a61ae690b8: Motion of the Official Opposition - For the installation of photo radars in front of each primary school to improve the safety of children near schools
entries.30798a342d7d32b7b2fe7e7b1c014bd554351064: Provide $742,500 in financial support to Father's House, to enhance the Rent Assistance Bank and support 150 additional tenant households at risk of eviction / Approve draft convention for this purpose
entries.a88319871206b052be68cf84cf0b33e09d657ece: Montreal is facing a continuing crisis of affordability of housing, including sustained increases in rents and increasing pressure on low- and middle-income tenant households, which particularly weakens vulnerable people, who spend a significant proportion of their income on housing and have little financial room for manoeuvre in the event of unforeseen conditions. In this context, delays in payment and risks of eviction are increasing.
entries.ebe01846012ddbd0d51a24444d59dbce7a52f6dd: Provide $540,000 in financial support from the Operating Budget of the Real Estate and Housing Strategy Service to the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal, for the renovation of housing units intended for vulnerable clients / Approve draft agreement to this effect
entries.389392beea62a619ab5e4efb58bb8caa43b7ddc8: The purpose of this decision-making document is to approve a contribution agreement between the City and the Société d'habitation et de développement de Montréal (SHDM) in order to accelerate the re-entry into the market of 45 housing units owned by SHDM, with the aim of providing housing for homeless or at risk of becoming homeless. The financial contribution of up to $540,000 would enable SHDM to mobilize internal resources and mandate external contractors so that these 45 housing units are rehabilitated by the end of August 2026.
entries.1c3fe2888019b7c7bcfa7beb499df6b1de22805b: Provide $150,000 in financial support to Cyclo-club Lachine, for Les Mardis Cycliques de Lachine event for the years 2026-2028 / Approve draft convention for this purpose / Authorize a budget transfer in 2026 to the amount of $15,000 from general administration contingent expenditures to the budget of the Department of Culture, Sports and Recreation / Authorize a recurring adjustment to the budget base of the Department of Culture, Sport and Recreation to the amount of $15,000 for the years 2027 and 2028
entries.718d3b5a36547ebd70287adfdbba81f3a01554ca: On December 19, 2025, Cyclo-Club Lachine submitted a request for support to the City of $50,000 for the 2026 edition of Les Mardis Cycliques de Lachine. Cyclo-Club Lachine's mission is to promote the borough of Lachine and the City of Montreal by organizing one of the most prestigious cycling events in eastern North America for nearly 45 years. This non-profit organization was formed on April 20, 1976 under the Quebec Companies Act, Part 3 (QLRQ, c.
entries.8f07e380cc914c9b975f29c45d64c002956d3928: On December 9, 2025, Beach Volleyball Événements submitted an application for financial support to the City of Montreal for the years 2026 ($250,000), 2027 ($265,000) and 2028 ($280,000). The event in 2025, by Beach Volleyball Évènements, was a great success at Jean-Drapeau Park. In 2025, the City provided $25,000 in support through the program to support international, national and metropolitan sporting events.
entries.b8d13da782b1193cd77973c23a1046e5f6f2c2bb: Provide additional financial support of $2,850,000 to GPCQM Events, for the holding of the Grand Prix Cycliste de Montréal in 2026, 2027 and 2028 / Provide support in goods and services valued at $1,410,000 for 2027 and $1,420,000 for 2028 / Authorize the extension of the agreement until 2028 / Authorize a budgetary transfer in 2026 to the amount of $250,000 from general administration contingent expenditures to the budget of the Culture, Sports and Recreation Service / Authorize a recurring adjustment to the budget base of the Culture, Sports and Recreation Service in the amount of $250,000 for the years 2027 and 2028 / Approve draft addendum 1 to this effect
entries.b70eff94249aeb4c73b73ce7c5aa7ff41805e899: Provide additional financial support of $700,000 to the Action Sports Association, $200,000 in 2026 and $250,000 per year in 2027 and 2028, for the holding of the Jackalope Festival in 2026, 2027 and 2028 / Authorize the extension of the agreement until 2028 / Authorize a budgetary transfer in 2026 to the amount of $200,000 from general administration contingent expenditures to the budget of the Culture, Sport and Recreation Service / Authorize a recurring adjustment to the budget base of the Culture, Sports and Recreation Service to the amount of $200,000 for the years 2027 and 2028 / Approve the draft addendum to this effect
entries.740df03fbdf3196ccd31d48da1b85c2236b49a96: On December 8, 2025, following a deficit edition, the Action Sports Association sent an adjustment request for a recurrent annual financial support of $500,000 from 2026 to 2028 in order to ensure the sustainability, growth and outreach of the event. The purpose of this application is to approve an addendum to the contribution agreement between the SAA and the City, which will amend the term of the agreement by extending it until 2028, increasing the financial support to $250,000 per year, as well as the terms of the agreement and the terms of payments.
entries.aebc9fafc7803545f8ede77dbd54f0c76713d853: Contract with Marco Cournoyer inspections inc. (Fire Protection MCI), for the inspection and maintenance of alarm and fire protection systems for buildings at the Jean-R.-Marcotte wastewater treatment plant, for a period of 36 months, including a 24-month extension option - Total expenditure of $1,889,887.25, taxes included - Public tender 26-21389 (4 som.)
entries.f72f29f9def2c5d3bad318ae3d11c6112a112258: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment, now and for future generations. The Department of Wastewater Treatment (DEEU) is responsible for the operation and maintenance of several alarm and fire protection systems designed to ensure personal safety, asset protection and business continuity. These systems, distributed across fifteen (15) buildings of the Jean-R.-Marcotte Wastewater Treatment Plant (Station), require rigorous supervision and regular interventions.
entries.b0d9929501a07a460176308e198adca702ca77e0: Exercising the option of the first 12-month extension / Authorize an additional expenditure of $3,400,298.84, including taxes, for the maintenance services of equipment and natural environments in regional parks under three contracts awarded to SOGEP Inc. (CG23,0129), thus increasing the total contract amount to $14,961,805.77, including taxes
entries.7dbb609df9557c3f97cd54aac997c065ac920cb0: The maintenance of the regional parks (nature parks) in the network of the City of Montreal's major parks is provided by external service contracts covering, among other things, general maintenance, equipment maintenance and horticultural work in natural environments. These contracts are necessary to ensure the safety of users, the quality of the facilities and the maintenance of assets in a territory of more than 1,700 hectares of natural spaces. Available free of charge to the public, the regional parks host more than one million visits annually.

entries.82350472c82f6fa3f53ecf14a98561fa755136d9: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montréal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. As part of its operations, the Jean-R.- Marcotte (Station) wastewater treatment plant generates a variety of residues, including those from decommissioning, commercial waste, residual waste from various works, as well as sand particles recovered from decantors' feed canals. These materials must be sent to a technical landfill (LET) authorized by the Department of the Environment, Climate Change Control, Wildlife and Parks (MELCCFP) for final disposition in accordance with existing regulations.
entries.987b450d6120dd82ed0ebc48be16df6316686004: Exercising the option of the first 12-month extension / Authorize an additional expenditure of $202,036.26, including taxes, for Biosphere household maintenance services under the contract awarded to Proprecan Inc.
