entries.b38dc58fa8e5c78a146867e59281f2987c2c1cdb: Created in 2008, the Montreal Library Renovation, Expansion and Construction Program (the RAC Program) supports the consolidation and development of the Montréal Library Network. This program is eligible for funding under the Montreal Cultural Development Agreement between the Ministère de la Culture et des Communications du Québec (MCCQ) and the City of Montreal. Funding is allocated as follows: 40% - CMCQ; 60% - Service de la culture.
entries.1febd0b6fd118fd7b451cbe1f3924a3049ef4ee1: Award a contract to Fer-Pal Construction Ltd., for the rehabilitation of secondary water pipes by blouses and roads in various streets of the Plateau-Mont-Royal and Rosemont arrondissements–La Petite-Patrie - Total expenditure of $13,372,179.16, including taxes - Public tender 524104 (2 som.)
entries.51632a8b831970ac6a4a9df973159e916bf535e0: The rehabilitation of water pipes by the sheathing technique is proposed by the Directorate of Asset Management (DGA) of the Water Service (SE). They are part of the strategy for water management of efficient infrastructures and are part of interventions that contribute to improving collective infrastructure and the quality of life of citizens. This untrenched sheathing technique represents many advantages compared with more traditional methods of excavation reconstruction, notably: · Rapidity in carrying out the work; · Reduction of disturbance on surrounding infrastructures; · Rapidity of site reclamation; · Reduction of the disposal of soil and excavating materials.
entries.61566419eaf2a15de360dbc2bb114d4e4a3603a2: Grant an OTC contract to Bibliotheca Canada Inc. for the provision and installation of an automated document sorting and return system in the library and cultural space of the Espace du Coeur-Nomade - Total expenditure of $216,897.81, including taxes (single supplier)
entries.97eae2defbf1f2a3e949d10b869fdc46e5e2f4d6: The Espace du Coeur-Nomade project, serving the Montréal-Nord and Ahuntsic-Cartierville arrondissements at 3170 Henri-Bourassa Boulevard East, is being carried out as part of the program of renovation, expansion and construction of libraries (RAC Program) and the program of support for municipal cultural facilities. It consists of building a library as well as cultural and community spaces. Designed by the firms Affleck de la Riva architectes, Coarchitecture, ARUP and Martin Roy & Associés, the project is under way.
entries.cdc824f59833df52d19909f1ddaef3d85fc1039f: Contract with Beluga Services Municipaux Inc., for the operation of the Ray-Lawson snow disposal site in the district of Anjou, for a period of five years - Total expenditure of $13,121,205.70, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 26,21295 (2 sum)
entries.833ad17ff3f8e8fc3ef76be2d3536fb378d67a7f: On February 4, 2026, the SCAEC launched Call for Bids No. 26-21295 for services to operate the snow disposal site (LEN) Ray-Lawson, located in the Anjou borough. A notice was published on the Government of Quebec's electronic tendering system (SEAO) and in the daily Le Devoir.
entries.65d048ff85da28e556403fbc04b67637e1bc89b8: Approve the proposed modification of the lease by which the City rents to Collectif d'animation urbaine L'Autre Montréal, for a period of three years, effective July 1, 2026, a space on the third floor of the building located at 3680 Jeanne-Mance Street in the Plateau-Mont-Royal borough, with an area of 1,318.36 square feet, for administrative purposes, for a total rent of $31,254.60, excluding taxes. The total amount of the real estate subsidy is estimated at $67,631.88
entries.7b457838235eccf4677444065742d913ce665f5b: Located at 3680 Jeanne-Mance Street, the Strathearn Centre is a sociocultural building. It houses several organizations such as Montréal Intercultural Arts, Ex aequo, Atelier d'Artisanat Centre-ville inc. and many others. From November 1, 2006 to June 30, 2017, the City of Montreal (City) leased to the organization Collectif d'animation urbaine L-Autre Montréal (L'Autre Montréal) room 331 d'a surface area of 1,506.95 sq. ft.
entries.86407610cedb75b0e3a8f434c0024b9a333c2cca: Grant an OTC contract to the Friends of the Botanical Garden of Montreal to be a point of sale for the Passport Space for Life for a period of three years - Total expenditure of $1,160,000, including taxes
entries.3cec1599d4a4be2922babfe2875d4fe359ce0fa9: The largest natural science complex in Canada, Space for Life, which includes the Biodôme, Biosphere, Insectarium, Botanical Garden and Planetarium, occupies a central place in citizen mobilization to preserve biodiversity and the environment. From this perspective, the service is working to increase accessibility of its facilities, including through initiatives promoting inclusion, diversity of audiences and reducing economic barriers. Since October 2021, Space for Life has been offering an annual Passport offering unlimited access to the five museums for a full year at an advantageous rate.
entries.1289b2845f73b5e4f8fef01ca8198f54ce62e31f: Provide a professional services contract and licence between the City and the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal for the application of the Flood Risk Assessment Method and its management - Total expenditure of $194,812
entries.8fc80b22e719d6085f6a01e05830898391452ac6: Spring floods are a recurring problem in Montreal, particularly for the reconstituted boroughs and towns located near Lake des Deux-Montagnes, the Prairie River and Lake Saint-Louis. To ensure the resilience of the territory to flooding, the city must continue to put in place permanent means to mitigate the risk. The City has obtained a grant from the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing (MAMH) for the application of the flood risk assessment and management method (MERIGE).
entries.5815acd6b98d094ea320d983315fcc9d4be73b5f: Grant an OTC contract to the Société des Amis du Biodôme de Montréal to be a point of sale of the Passport Space for Life for a period of three years - Total expenditure $1,600,000, including taxes / Approve draft convention to this effect
entries.5a765bacc5462ca4ce54536bda4880ab585196eb: The mandate of the Asset Management Directorate of the Water Service is, among other things, to identify and prioritize the renewal of water and secondary sewer infrastructure in the territory of the City of Montreal. This work is part of the strategy of water management for efficient infrastructure and is one of the interventions that contribute to improving collective infrastructure and the quality of life of citizens.

entries.9fa65de3fb7242eda56c53f9cdd573fc3835a2ee: Built in 1964, the former Baldwin pool, located at Baldwin Park, reached its end of service in 2019. In 2019, a contract for professional services was awarded for its renovation and expansion project. However, in 2021, soil studies revealed the presence of an old burial site under the pool, making the site unsustainable.
entries.a95923430e68edef619f513ed48fc05f32e40f7b: In 1994, the City entered into an agreement with the Société du Musée d'archéologie et d'histoire de Montréal Pointe-à-Callière (the Société), enabling it to operate the Museum and providing an annual grant to this non-profit organization. Since then, agreements have been concluded on an annual or triennial basis based on discussions between the Museum and the City. The last three-year agreement ended on December 31, 2025.

entries.08b16a9a305a0d4abe63895da3fb5c1022e86957: Approve the City's intervention in an act of amendment to an emphyteosis between Santé Québec (the Institut de Cardiology de Montréal) and Centre de la Petite Enfance Cardio-Puces, in order to consent to the extension of the term provided for emphyteosis and the use of the land identified as Lot 2 787 367 of the cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montreal, for the purpose of expanding a daycare, notwithstanding the restriction on use in favour of the City contained in the act published under number 1 223 896, which allowed the use for medical center purposes only
entries.e95f940ccf0c7e8544e6e47e72e1246ed0c207b2: On October 15, 1951, the City of Montreal (City) donated to the B.C.G. Clinic in Montreal, now the Marie-Enfant Hospital, a land for the construction of an anti-tuberculosis centre. The act of donation stipulated a return clause that if the land were to be used for purposes other than an anti-tuberculosis centre for childhood, the land would become the property of the City. On August 24, 1956, the terms "purposes of an anti-tuberculosis centre" were changed to "Medical Centre".
entries.08b57ba7fe28e91e503b31295d673a0c8291dc0b: Approve the proposed three-year cooperation agreement between the City of Montréal and Ouranos Inc., effective June 16, 2026, for a total amount of $517,387.50, including taxes, and a contribution in kind of $300,000
entries.0063d53c28071223388bfb6e285db010e314aaa2: This dossier concerns the renewal of the partnership between the City of Montreal and Ouranos in order to sustain the development of the City on the basis of current and future scientific data. In June 2017, the City of Montreal signed a 3-year membership agreement with Ouranos, a consortium on regional climatology and adaptation to climate change. Ouranos is a non-profit organization created in 2001 whose mission is to help Quebec society better adapt to climate change by rigorously building on scientific knowledge and best practices.

C-11.4)
entries.7790cfe0e29919e08efbc410112ddf5a53184283: Rutherford Park is located at the foot of Mount Royal, south of Avenue des Pins, between McTavish Street and Dr. Penfield Avenue. The sports ground was developed in 2017 as a result of renovation work on the same reservoir.

entries.9fae33492db1fda0fa6a9d9bbac51ee2c975aa6b: The Planning and Development Division of the Urban Planning and Mobility Service (SUM) is the applicant unit responsible for a strategic building acquisition program in priority areas. This program also extends to the entire Montreal area when specific needs are identified. In 2021, the city centre and the Borough of Montréal-Nord agreed to coordinate their efforts to increase municipal land control in this district, particularly for local purposes, such as the development of new parks.
entries.433b70fb1b8ceeb0e2f71796bf1882637a6a8158: Approve the extension of hours of admission to commercial establishments at special events, including commercial promotions, for the 2026 summer season of the Société de développement commerciale Avenue du Mont-Royal, the Société de développement commerciale Laurier Ouest, the Association des gens d'affaires du Mile-End and the Société de Développement du Boulevard Saint-Laurent
entries.4a93a9002590f2389e889c9c86922a37945c93f4: On September 21, 2017, the Act increasing the autonomy and powers of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec was enacted. This Act introduces new provisions under the Hours and Days of Admission to Commercial Establishments Act that now allow the City of Montreal to authorize different legal hours of admission to commercial establishments at special events. Previously, applications for authorization to extend hours of admission to commercial establishments were submitted by merchant associations to the Ministry of Economy and Innovation.
entries.183b8936590f45b61e422597624d5eeef70f07fe: Authorize a budgetary transfer for the year 2026 of $200,000 from Villeray–Saint-Michel–Park-Extension, $130,000 from the borough of Saint-Laurent and $70,000 from the borough of LaSalle to the Service de la concertation des arrondissements et de l'expérience citoyenne, as part of their integration into the soil management site of the Pointe-Saint-Charles Business Park (PEPSC)
entries.60ec852a5ac311163b56e4ccd5b1f984f8251677: As part of its activities, the City generates excavation soils that must be characterized in order to determine their level of contamination and thus treat them accordingly. In this regard, on February 11, 2021, the Directorate-General formally mandated the Department of borough consultation and citizen experience to develop a project for an integrated treatment site. Accordingly, the creation of the PEPSC site has enabled these needs to be met and has come to provide participating boroughs (Ville-Marie, Sud-Ouest, Verdun, Mercier-Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Ahuntsic, Lachine, Rosemont - La Petite-Patrie, Le Plateau-Mont-Royal, Côte-des-Neiges - Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Outremont and Saint-Léonard) with a range of services allowing optimal and standardized disposal of their excavation soils.

entries.7315be2636b79914f0f2a82d7eb9f300191532a7: The Service des infrastructures du réseau route (SIRR) is responsible for the rehabilitation and maintenance of the assets of the administrative arterial network of the City of Montreal (RAAV), which falls under the jurisdiction of the Council of the City under the Charter of the City of Montréal (Art. 87(6) and Art. 105). Knowing that the streets on which they wish to intervene fall within the jurisdiction of the Council of the City, boroughs have offered to carry out the work there pursuant to section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montréal, which states that "a Conseil d'arrondissement may, subject to the conditions it determines, provide the Council of the City with a service connected to a jurisdiction falling within its jurisdiction; the resolution of the District Council takes effect from the adoption by the City Council of a resolution accepting the provision of services." In recent years, investments in the maintenance of the road network have significantly improved the condition of the streets of the arterial network.

entries.62e159e1ff9ead829866d041e09e5c996396535a: The hippodrome's redevelopment project represents an unprecedented opportunity to address the housing crisis as it will eventually accommodate 10,000 social and affordable out-of-market housing. However, in order to achieve this goal, it requires significant investments in infrastructure and public facilities and particular governance. In 2023, determined to accelerate the development of the project, the City of Montreal and the Government of Quebec announced the creation of the GALOPH Working Group: Acceleration Group for the Optimization of the Hippodrome Project, composed of partners from business, community, residential real estate and private and institutional financing sectors.

C-11.4)

In recent years, investments in the maintenance of the road network have significantly improved the condition of the assets of the arterial network. Knowing that the sections of streets covered by the planned interventions fall within the jurisdiction of the City Council, the arrondissement of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve offers its services to carry out work pursuant to section 85 of the Charter of the City of Montréal which states: "A borough council may, on such terms as it determines, provide the City Council with a service linked to a jurisdiction falling within the competence of the City; the resolution of the borough council takes effect from the adoption by the City Council of a resolution accepting the provision of services."

entries.99adf3bea4179824c1ccb4044c6fd65f46657271: On July 9, 2020, the Superior Court of Quebec declared unconstitutional, invalid and inoperative the suspension of indexation of pensioners' pensions as of December 31, 2013, since January 1, 2017, as provided for in the Act to Promote the Financial Health and Sustainability of Municipal Defined Benefit Pension Plans (MRSP Act). The other provisions of this Act remain valid. The Quebec Court of Appeal upheld this judgment on May 10, 2023, and the Supreme Court of Canada dismissed applications for leave to appeal on April 11, 2024.

entries.24327682663d77539037e2edd8cadab4edc65462: The Act respecting ethics and ethics in municipal matters (RLRQ, chapter E-15.1.0.1) (the Act) requires the council of a municipality to adopt, by regulation, a Code of Ethics and Ethics for Cabinet Personnel (the Code) (section 15.1 of the Act). Section 15.2 requires that the Code be revised after each general election and that the council adopt, no later than May 1 following the election, this revised Code, which replaces the one in force, with or without amendment.
entries.eac951786ea2b46192fc69c262b9c9d8f55d4efe: Adoption - Code of Ethics and Conduct for City Council and District Council Members
entries.47b900b3b55e1b1d8438adbc7c6e3946c70c34d6: The Commission de la Présidence du Conseil held 2 working sessions dedicated to the study of the Code of Ethics and Conduct for the members of the City Council and the borough councils on 11 February and 9 March 2026. This work, undertaken in accordance with the legal obligation to proceed with the adoption of a revised Code of Ethics after the election of November 2, 2025, is aimed at recommending the adoption of a revised Code of Ethics to the municipal council before May 1, 2026. As part of its work, the Commission de la Présidente du Conseil was able to benefit from the assistance and professional services of Me André Comeau, an ethics adviser to elected persons as well as members of Montreal's cabinet staff, who submitted his comments and recommendations as part of this mandatory review process.
entries.1a2ab8c1514327c23e669f7ea12804e1d046351b: Adoption - Regulations authorizing a loan of $18,500,000 to finance the restoration of municipal heritage buildings under the Montreal Cultural Development Agreement
entries.6bbba7486cedf4c4568d3a0eb7396ca983b661bc: Following the approval of the most recent Agreement on Cultural Development in Montreal (EDCM) by the conseil d'agglomeration in October 2024 (CG24 0555), the Urban Planning and Mobility Service (SUM) is now required to pass the necessary borrowing regulations for the implementation of planning projects under the Municipal Heritage Buildings Development Program. The agreement between the Ville de Montréal and the Ministère de la Culture et des Communications (MCC) constitutes a financial vehicle and a remarkable lever for the development of Montréal in its role as a cultural metropolis of Quebec. This is concretely implemented through the Municipal Heritage Buildings Development Program, which is funded by this agreement.

The City may register a notice of deterioration in the event that a building has become obsolete or degrades if the corrective work has not been completed within the time limit specified by the competent authority. Inscribed in the Land Registry, the notice of deterioration is related to the building.

entries.0ffb15dd8da279b99ecaa66463d1b48017f11712: The Plan d'action Vision Zero 2025-2027 pursues the objective of achieving zero deaths and serious injuries on the Montreal road network by 2040. Background to the Addendum With regard to the new eligibility criteria for the financial assistance program for institutions located in an area affected by major works, an amendment was requested to the duration of eligible work as defined in section 1 of that regulation.
entries.2a00c791df8e0bdc1f46013c31e6e5be1cccd498: Tabling of the Executive Committee's response to the recommendations of the Permanent Commission on the Inspector General entitled "Study of the 2024 Annual Report of the Office of the Inspector General of the City of Montreal"
entries.302556b5d19d9d6971b50f30916b944c7c7f78e5: The permanent commissions of the council are public consultation bodies established by the municipal council and the conseil d'agglomeration. In accordance with the Act respecting cities and cities and the Charter of the City of Montreal, their mission is to inform the decision-making of elected persons at the municipal and agglomeration levels and to encourage the participation of citizens in public interest debates. The Standing Commission on the Inspector General submitted a report containing 11 recommendations to the municipal council on May 12, 2025 and the conseil d'agglomeration on May 15, 2025 in its document entitled "Etude du rapport annuel 2024 du bureau de l'inspecteur général de la Ville de Montréal".
entries.2348034e61def0a4dbc3a9907d2a64fc978a3f9b: Presentation of the 2025 activity report of each of the following advisory committees: Jacques-Viger Committee, Montreal Heritage Council and Advisory Committee in Recognition
entries.a34b0504d23e21368d75a755522751c952011b5e: Pursuant to section 21 of the Jacques-Viger Committee Regulations (12-022), the committee shall report on its activities to the municipal council by filing its activity report 2025. Pursuant to section 18 of the Montreal Heritage Board Regulations (02-136), the board shall report on its activities to the municipal council by tabling its activity report 2025. In accordance with section 28 of the Advisory Committee on Recognition Regulations (22-044), the committee shall report on its activities to the municipal council by submitting its activity report 2025.
entries.3883be1de1617ee6083a4252fd48064a5435646a: Filing of the 2025 annual drinking water quality assessment for 17 distribution systems served by drinking water production plants in Atwater, Charles-J.-Des Baillets, Lachine, Dorval, Pointe-Claire and Pierrefonds as required under the Drinking Water Quality Regulations (Q-2, r. 40)
entries.e708264cbf3aacc4411ec35c290388bdc0e85410: The City of Montreal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water to the Montreal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. Reporting to the Water Service, the Drinking Water Directorate (DEP) provides drinking water to all residents of the Montréal area from six (6) drinking water production plants: Atwater, Charles-J.-Des Baillets, Lachine, Dorval, Pointe-Claire and Pierrefonds. Section 53.3 of the Department of the Environment, Combating Climate Change, Fauna and Parks (MELCCFP) Regulations requires that a water distribution system produce an annual assessment of the quality of drinking water produced for human consumption.
entries.1914dd26d0198a22af71441f5f321ec224474762: Tabling of Treasurer Activity Report for Fiscal Year 2025 pursuant to section 513 of the Municipal Elections and Referendums Act
entries.bf6ea526bf004c366933c5923d62dfe86052b5e6: Tabling of the 2025 Annual Report on the Montreal Water Strategy's Annual Report 2025-2034
entries.cf8759eeb2d5b8abf7ee66192d3414f2f3fac15c: This dossier is part of the implementation of the Montreal Water Strategy 2025-2034, adopted on June 4, 2025 by the Executive Committee following a broad public consultation. The Strategy pursues an overall objective: that all Montrealers have access to quality drinking water as well as healthy riparian and aquatic ecosystems, which they can safely benefit from. It also seeks to ensure that its infrastructure is adapted and that nature is used to meet the challenges imposed by climate change.
entries.b5ed79aeb6e8f197f9626d8df09562618b2edf77: Tabling of the Annual Activity Report of the City's Audit Committee for the period from January 1 to December 31, 2025
entries.ab36ba7996fcf9b0ffcdcebb859a5278a301e1d3: The audit committee of the City of Montreal shall consist of not more than 10 members appointed by the agglomeration council, on the proposal of the Mayor of the City of Montréal. Section 3 of the Charter of the Committee provides that among the members of the committee: •two (2) must be members of the agglomeration council representing the reconstituted municipalities; •at least three (3) must be members of the municipal council, previously designated by that council; •at least three (3) must be independent members, among whom the agglomeration council designates the chairman. Section 31 of the Charter of the Committee provides that no later than March 31 of each year, the chair of the committee shall report to the city council and the agglomeration council on the activities of the committee, comments and recommendations resulting from its work.
entries.8d6418ae3ba0bccfb8eff9bbb29e27ddeabee4dc: Tabling of the Commission's report on the Inspector General entitled "Study of the mid-year 2025 report of the Office of the Inspector General of the City of Montreal"

entries.d2a88fa636590bfcfb4a7988761e1ae1899241b1: Exercise the option of the first 12-month extension and authorize an additional expenditure of $175,071.19, including taxes, for the supply of Kebony wood for specialized workshops, under the framework agreement with North On Sixty (CM24,0689), thus increasing the total amount of the framework agreement to $797,867.77, including taxes
entries.81bd31461854db9fb4e18f1d31a70ebaf7c47b5a: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (SMRA) is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as to provide a variety of specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services in an environmentally responsible manner and in a safe environment. The carpentry team, which is an integral part of the SMRA, is responsible for the manufacture and supply of urban furniture replacement parts. As part of its raw material procurement planning, SMRA has identified the need to acquire a type of wood essence: Kebony wood.
entries.ad07e3efa508ac7e4082734b3268951234a9804d: Grant a contract to Pavages Métropolitain inc., for road works in the boroughs of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, Côte-des-Neiges– Notre-Dame-de-Grâce, Ahuntsic-Cartierville, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie, Saint-Léonard and Ville-Marie (PCPR, PCPR+ and PRRP 2026) - Total expenditure of $10,589,009.13, including taxes - Call for tender 527002 (7 sum)
entries.d7a31c5cb169336f94de91297ee18897a37833a3: Conclude a framework agreement with Groupe Geninov inc., for professional work monitoring services during modifications to the underground network of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal for a period of 36 months - Estimated amount of the agreement: $843,286.67 including taxes - Public tender S-2349 (5 som) / Approve draft agreement to this effect
entries.0be0df7cf050dc6acbe74089222b90d708cad797: The mission of the Commission des services électriques de Montréal (CSEM) is to plan, build, maintain, operate and administer underground duct networks. To accomplish this mission, interventions by the CSEM in the public domain of the City are required. Activities to carry out these interventions are carried out by teams of employees internal to the CSEM or performed by external suppliers under contract with the CSEM.
entries.4603e7d49efcb594fbf2b565b5af672723711e08: Approve the proposed lease by which the City leases to the Women's Community Entre Elles, for a period of 24 months, effective February 1, 2026, room 4, located at 251, Avenue des Pins Ouest (Cité-des-Hospitalières), with an area of 77 square feet, for office purposes, and community activities for newcomer women, for a total rent of $2,453.22, excluding sales taxes and the amount of the real estate subsidy is $15,495
entries.b0b2e6de45b29ffa770f2bac27057d525df0f375: In 2017, the City of Montreal (Ville) acquired from the Religious Hospitallers of Saint-Joseph la Cité-des-Hospitalières (Cité), located at 201 to 251-A, avenue des Pins Ouest (l'Immeuble). The City, as owner of this heritage site, has the responsibility to protect this environment and its cultural and landscape heritage. The City's protection efforts and the project to enhance the site must comply with the following five principles, enshrined in the act of sale: The preservation of the spirit of the place; Respect for the values of the Religious and their spiritual mission; Protection and sustainability of the built and natural heritage; Consistency with the history of the site; Openness to the community and the response to its needs.
entries.abea90b4f2b7c908cb452f5b7439888e1127f74e: Authorize the assignment of the contract for professional services awarded to Anne Lagacé (CM26 0075) to 9560-8303 Québec inc. for the remainder of the agreement, under the same conditions / Approve the draft convention to this effect
entries.a888a1620520ba25da97dae7f1fb9302d44a283e: On 26 January 2026, the municipal council approved the award of a contract to Anne Lagacé for the design, construction, assembly and dismantling of the installations of the luminous artistic exhibition "Resonances", an external work for the illumination of the Jardin des Premières-Nations in the context of the 2026 edition of the event Jardins de lumière, whose opening is scheduled on 28 August 2026 (CM26 0075). Anne Lagacé, who signed the initial agreement in her own name, wishes to assign it to the new corporation of which she is a shareholder.
entries.e2d8c46f22d89c9a9075a4c0c3f225882b989911: Termination of the contract awarded to Veille sur toi inc., for the acquisition of 12 objects for the Welcome Baby Project (CM25 0765), by December 31, 2026 / Authorize a $711,280 budget transfer from unanticipated local authority contingent expenditures to the Human Resources and Communications Service
entries.757e7abf8c2514849398db30e6698d6fef6ce2de: In June 2025, following Public Call for Bids No. 25-20874, the City of Montreal awarded a contract for the acquisition of twelve (12) items for the Baby Welcome box, for a period of three (3) years, with two (2) extension options of twelve (12) months each. The total expenditure associated with this contract was $7,476,249.38, including taxes. However, as part of the budget process, it was decided not to renew the Baby Welcome project, with an objective of optimizing spending and refocusing activities.
entries.a60b8b1347b6b0f481710ad022cecc9449a449b6: Exercising the option of the first 12-month extension and authorizing an additional expenditure of $87,406.05, including taxes, for maintenance services in the historic gardens of the Cité-des-Hospitalières, located at 251, Avenue des Pins Ouest, under the contract awarded to Jardin de lumière (Richard Archambault) (CM23 0146), thus increasing the total contract amount to $331,778.25, including taxes
entries.0e4eb49fa159fa2a63cf6d7900d3d9abd6ca035f: In 2022, the Supply Service issued a public tender No. 22-19635 for a service to maintain the historic gardens of the Cité-des-Hospitalières, located at 251 Avenue des Pins Ouest. The maintenance of the gardens of this building is normally carried out by a private company. This file is intended to exercise the first year of option, from November 16, 2025 to November 15, 2026.
entries.1c8ee8c8c7c08848695d6223037f8d8a843c1654: Exercising the option of the second 12-month extension, without additional expense, for the cleaning services of sumps, sump drains, sewers, sewage pipes and valve chambers in the floodable sections of the borough of Pierrefonds-Roxboro, as part of the framework agreement with 9363-9888 Québec inc. (Saniva) (CM23 0404 (Lot 2))
entries.8335fd7009d289e0f9ea098edd26102eb2a7ab01: The Ville de Montréal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montreal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment today and for future generations. The Water Systems Directorate is responsible for the distribution of quality drinking water and the collection of wastewater by carrying out projects to upgrade and develop network assets, while ensuring their operation and maintenance. The purpose of this file is to renew framework agreements with 9363-9888 Québec inc. (Saniva) for lots 1 and 2, relating to the boroughs of L'Île-Bizard–Sainte-Geneviève (Lot 1) and Pierrefonds-Roxboro (Lot 2), in order to address emergency situations caused by flooding.
entries.6b5153e38297dee8a9dc42e1d5533daf2ba845a1: Exercise the option of the second 12-month extension and authorize an additional expenditure of $2,121,767.30, including taxes, for the supply and delivery of crushed stones under the framework agreement with Amrize Canada Inc. (formerly Lafarge Canada Inc.) (CM23,0433), thus increasing the total amount of the agreement to $7,795,265.44, including taxes
entries.b28b10496417c8efb784916acb81c55057408ec7: In 2023, the Supply Service launched a public tender for the supply and delivery on request of a variety of premixed, net crushed stone with two twelve-month extension options. The contract, in the amount of $3,621,544 including taxes (agreement: $3,149,168.70 + quantity variation $472,375.31), granted to Lafarge Canada Inc. (now Amrize Canada Inc.) has been in effect since April 24, 2023, for a period of twenty-four (24) months. In December 2025, consumption on the framework agreement was $3,948,248.06, including taxes, or 83.97 per cent of the contract awarded.
entries.345486544ea66f1e34eb577c7c28cad0f2dffeec: Approve the Arrears Payment Agreement with Hydro-Québec, for the period from January 1, 2014 to December 31, 2025, in respect of several rental records located in the right-of-way belonging to Hydro-Québec, used by citizens of the City of Montreal for cycle paths, parks and community gardens, for an amount of $125,167.62, including taxes
entries.837f0f067b8d78c83a4d99698f27eeae8bd81413: For several years, the City of Montreal (City) has rented land from Hydro-Québec located in rights-of-way used by citizens of the City for bicycle paths, parks and community gardens. Between 2014 and 2025, a disagreement persisted between representatives of the Real Estate Strategy Service (SSI) and those of Hydro-Québec (HQ) regarding the rate to be paid by the City for the occupation of these lands. Hydro-Québec initially requested arrears of approximately $1.9 million, based on the market value of the occupations.
entries.a106d15c9f2c08b0c7f15938a2a27c343fea37ac: In 2017, the City of Montreal (Ville) acquired from the Religious Hospitallers of Saint-Joseph la Cité-des-Hospitalières (Cité), located at 201 to 251-A, avenue des Pins Ouest (l'Immeuble). The City, as owner of this heritage site, has a responsibility to protect this environment and its cultural and landscape heritage. The City's protection efforts and the project to enhance the site must comply with the following five principles, enshrined in the act of sale: The preservation of the spirit of the place; Respect for the values of the Religious and their spiritual mission; Protection and sustainability of the built and natural heritage; Consistency with the history of the site; Openness to the community and the response to its needs.
entries.d4d40126ab14820473133e77bf10c6568bba0139: Ratify the agreement between the City and the Department of Environment and Climate Change, Wildlife and Parks for a grant by the Ministry of $16,409,137.60 under Component 2 of OASIS / Authorize an additional revenue and expenditure budget of $689,268 to the City Branch's operating budget / Confirm that the City and its partners, in accordance with the OASIS normative framework, are committed to paying 20% of eligible expenditures, any non-eligible expenses and any cost overruns associated with carrying out the project
entries.b462310405a0dab942a86e749d607db92f36d7d3: The OASIS program of the Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) is implemented to support the municipal community and Aboriginal communities in strengthening their resilience to heat waves and intense precipitation accentuated by climate change. The program is part of axis 3 "Strengthening Québec's resilience to the impacts of climate change" of the implementation plan stemming from the Government of Quebec's 2030 Green Economy Plan (PEV 2030).
entries.7fc6c2a3335a8034935447ea3aa097588265f1a6: Approve the draft local loan agreement between the City and Club de lutte Inter-Concordia for the rental, free of charge, of an administrative office and a training room at the Claude-Robillard sports complex from 2026 to 2027, as part of the Policy of Support for Organizations Working in Corporate Sports Facilities
entries.b13d09c97df4890b26ef2136d28458e44495401b: Since 1996, the City of Montreal has supported, in financial contributions as well as goods and services, non-profit organizations for their service in sport and physical activity to the Montreal population annually. In order to incorporate the new recommendations of the Auditor General's 2023 report and changes in the legislative framework, the Sport Facilities Management Division revised its Policy of Support for Organizations Working in Corporate Sports Facilities (Policy) (CE24 0552). This policy of support is intended to provide the Sport Facilities Management Division with clear and objective guidance in order to properly guide the support of organizations working in corporate sports facilities.
entries.f02d918877c8097486d5eedbbd0b9cc265e2848e: Approve the proposed lease by which the City leases to the Société du musée d'archéologie et d'histoire de Montréal Pointe-à-Callière, for a period of three years, effective January 1, 2026, a premises located at 335 Place d'Youville, with an area of 551 square metres, for museum purposes, for a total rent of $5,535, excluding taxes. The amount of the real estate subsidy for the total duration of the proposed lease is $162,423.78
entries.99c2674103321ea76f711e30adfa469c0c0a8a23: The Société du musée d'archéologie et d'histoire de Montréal Pointe-à-Callière's mission is to "make Montreal known and loved yesterday and today through activities of dissemination, education, conservation and research in the place of Montréal's archaeological and historical heritage; and to establish links with relevant regional, national and international networks that will benefit the public." The museum rents spaces from the City of Montreal at 335, Place d'Youville, in the former Fire Department No. 1, and wishes to extend its lease, which has expired since December 31, 2025. The Service de la culture (SC) mandated the Real Estate Strategy Service (SSI), on January 19, 2026, to accompany it in negotiating the new lease between the parties. The lease was negotiated by agreement.
entries.04fc2c403a4b24d41e0348b38b18ef2041edf0b7: In 2017, the City of Montreal (City) acquired, from the Religious Hospitallers of Saint-Joseph (Religieux), the Cité-des-Hospitalières (Cité), located at 201 to 251-A, avenue des Pins Ouest (L'Immeuble). The City, as owner of this heritage site, has the responsibility to protect this environment and its cultural and landscape heritage. The City's protection efforts and the project to enhance the site must comply with the following five principles, inscribed in the act of sale: The preservation of the spirit of the place; Respect for the values of the religious and their spiritual mission; Protection and perpetuity of the built and natural heritage; Consistency with the history of the site; Openness to the community and the response to its needs.
entries.b0771e65d3fe5c3fe1e153839a582518d21b92f6: Approve the proposed lease by which the City leases to Marie-Dominique Bonmariage and Rachel Jordan, for a period of 24 months, effective February 1, 2026, room 3, located at 251A, Avenue des Pins Ouest (Cité-des-Hospitalières), with an area of 98 square feet, for office purposes, workshops and conferences in herbal facilities, for a total rent of $4,762.80, excluding sales taxes
entries.8837ebfa7c7b289f067633a6001adc324808b89e: Approve the proposed lease of premises 157 and 164, located at 251, Avenue des Pins Ouest (Cité-des-Hospitalières), with a total area of 612 square feet, for research, creation and theatre projects, in Sibyllines, Petrus and Creation, for 24 months, effective February 1, 2026, for a total rent of $29,223.12, excluding sales taxes
entries.4da6474b4205736458cf584c62d9b961155168c1: Approve the proposed lease by which the City leases to Milton-Parc Recreational Association, for a period of 24 months, effective February 1, 2026, Premises 1, located at 251A, Avenue des Pins Ouest (Cité-des-Hospitalières), with an area of 121 square feet, for office purposes for community activities, for a total rent of $6,370.68, excluding sales taxes
entries.245308260769e82d255d0e355c5fa9d01b0c6f90: Conclude framework agreements with Cintas Canada Ltd. and Universal Security Equipment Inc., for the supply and delivery of workwear, for a period of 36 months, including two 12-month extension options - Estimated amount of agreements: $2,046,042.02, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25-21173 (5 sum)
entries.9d9aa9010ffe5b058dd94cb9a12aa215fc174df5: The purpose of this file is to conclude three framework agreements for the supply and delivery of workwear, required for the operational needs of blue collars and white collars as part of their work. These framework agreements will be made available to all business units in the City of Montreal. In August 2020, the contract for the supply and delivery of polos was awarded on an out-of-court basis, in accordance with documents attached to price application 20-18217, to the lowest compliant bidder, namely Groupe Trium inc., for an estimated total amount of $70,860.01, including taxes.
entries.edabcd85d5329288f6082c89de87a7ab6338abf0: Conclude framework agreements with USD Global Inc. and Orbis Canada Ltd., for the provision of 36-month residual collection tools, including two 12-month extension options - Estimated amount of agreements: $3,484,025.17, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25,21241 (2 sum)
entries.547e0ed5b511e364a8644267fb3b10232b437839: Since January 1, 2015, pursuant to section 85.5 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4), the municipal council of the City of Montréal has jurisdiction with respect to the removal, transport and deposit of residual materials (CM14 1126; CM24 1122). The Collection, Transportation and Processing Division of the Residual Material Management Directorate and Infrastructures of the Environmental Service is responsible for planning and having contracts, or framework agreements, awarded for the provision of residual material collection tools.
entries.e65bf39dfbf18171a7aeb57c784effb7e7fc6517: Conclude framework agreements with Tacel Ltd. (lots 1 and 3) and Eco-Compteur Inc. (lot 2) for the provision of traffic light equipment, for a period of 24 months with a 12-month extension option - Estimated amount of agreements: $2,593,558.91 including taxes - Public tender 25-21195 (3 sum)
entries.9ffcb77830e0d34cd512d88340d0bc225ae8c917: Supported by its Urban Planning and Mobility Plan (PUM), the Urban Planning and Mobility Service (SUM) has set ambitious targets for redevelopment of the territory and street-sharing throughout the City of Montreal. This approach is part of a renewed concept of street sharing, putting safe, efficient and sustainable urban transportation at the heart of the ecological transition. In this context of public space transformation, urban mobility management is becoming a major challenge.
entries.208707ccea80e20c3a0b833dc92ce970e03a006c: Grant a contract to Les Pavages Céka inc., for the replacement of lead water connections and roads in various streets of the arrondissements of Côte-des-Neiges–Notre-Dame-de-Grâce and Outremont - Total expenditure of $4,819,574.85, including taxes - Public tender 524202 (7 som)
entries.bd98854d707288ddb3bf6b9ddeeae2d9f65bfa40: The City of Montreal, through the Asset Management Directorate (ADM) of the Water Service (WS), wishes to carry out replacement work on leaded water connections in accordance with Directive S-DRE-SE-D-2021-03. This work is part of the municipal strategy for efficient infrastructure and contributes to improving the quality of life of citizens. The specific objective of this work is to replace current leaded water connections.
entries.4b0189cbf802574e1ccd58790082a5b49f9cfa26: Contract with Les Entrepreneurs Bucaro inc., for road works in the Plateau-Mont-Royal, Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, Anjou and Montréal-Nord districts - Total expenditure of $9,380,867.81, including taxes - Public tender 527003 (6 soum)
entries.7c0874a7f4b7c804fad2b6032ff45dd62f2a7bd9: Grant a contract to Englobe Corp., for the professional services of testing sidewalks in the administrative arterial road network of the City of Montreal in 2026 - Total expenditure of $668,253.50, including taxes - Public tender 25-21216 (2 soum)
entries.102e381abe35fdf69b468d58b68e0d9f1fbff72d: The City of Montreal's Road Infrastructure Service (SIRR) continues its mission to plan for the maintenance of the assets of the City's administrative arterial network (RAAV) in order to maintain its established level of service throughout the life cycle. The investments allocated to maintaining the arterial road network demonstrate the City of Montréal's commitment to improve both the comfort and safety of road users and the quality of life of citizens, as well as the efficiency of movement of people and goods. In order to properly establish investment needs, the City of Montréal is continuing to implement best asset management practices and thus ensure effective and efficient management of its municipal infrastructure in general and its road assets in particular.
entries.712686330b818a6fc956197cbfcb74fd028bc75f: Grant a contract to FER-PAL Construction Ltd., for the rehabilitation of secondary water pipes by brooming and roadway in various streets of the boroughs of Ahuntsic-Cartierville and Villeray–Saint-Michel–Park-Extension - Total expenditure of $11,103,483.78, taxes included - Public tender 524106 (3 soum)
entries.5829714a741ddcff81410dfb2783923273cf42b0: The rehabilitation of water pipes by the sheathing technique is proposed by the Directorate of Asset Management (DGA) of the Water Service (SE). These are part of the strategy for water management of efficient infrastructures and are part of the interventions that contribute to the improvement of collective infrastructure and the quality of life of citizens.This untrenched sheathing technique represents many advantages compared with more traditional methods of excavation reconstruction, notably: · speed in carrying out the work; · reduction of disturbances on surrounding infrastructures; · speed of site restoration; · reduction of the disposition of soil and excavation materials.
entries.0b35013bfe1997532328944df4868dd9e318b602: Award a contract to Les Services EXP inc., for professional design and construction audit services of the Plateau-Mont-Royal District Service Court, for a three-year period, including a 12-month extension option - Total expenditure of $1,386,606.55, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25-21129 (3 sum)
entries.12bab9bcc266a1e2314e48cee0fa80ceccfc9b19: The Le Plateau-Mont-Royal (CSPMR) service court redevelopment project is a priority project of the City of Montreal's Service Course Program, which aims to upgrade and improve the performance of buildings as well as optimize the operation of service courses. Phase 1 of the project (lots 1 and 2, deconstruction and decontamination) was completed in 2024. A design-construction contract (CC) was awarded in June 2025 (CM25 0764) to Pomerleau Inc. for the completion of phase 2 (lot 3) of the project, namely the construction of the new service yard.
entries.ddf58ea7833e208aeef20b58f8b490dc7655caef: Award a contract to St-Denis Thompson Inc. for the development of a sports park between Saint-Patrick, Hadley, Roberval and Cabot Streets (Gadbois Station Sector 3) - Total expenditure of $12,171,494.28 including taxes - Public Call for Bids 522801 (11 bidders) / Increase the operating budget of the urban planning and mobility department through the Environmental Liabilities by an additional $3,504,606.80 net
entries.91f5fb6e3d0cbe194f48568cbae7ddc7e0a9f5c1: As a result of the work of the Turcot interchange by the Ministère des Transports et de la Mobilité durable (MTMD), the City of Montreal and this ministry signed a collaboration agreement that designates the City to carry out the project to develop the Gadbois Pole in order to compensate for the nuisances and impact of this major transportation project in the area. The aim of the Gadbois Pole project is to create a significant space for the neighbourhood, including by building recreational spaces and sports grounds, greening the surroundings of the Gadbois Centre. Mobility and accessibility are considered in the project with the creation or improvement of cycling and pedestrian links as well as parking areas.
entries.fbcea1974fe06d33c29ecea935a71542331f200e: Contract with Procova Inc. to construct the Irma-LeVasseur Park Pavilion in Outremont District - Total expenditure of $1,735,892.55, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 512802 (14 sum)
entries.f859f239b4fedf95d1abae9469274ff416c59b6f: As part of the implementation of the MIL Montréal project, the City is currently completing the development of the new Irma-LeVasseur Neighbourhood Park. This park is one of four hectares of new public spaces developed as part of the redevelopment of the former Outremont Yard Station in partnership with the Université de Montréal. With an area of 18 500 m2, the park is located south of Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux Avenue between Dollard Avenue to the west and Wiseman Avenue to the east.
entries.21bfb89cef56b876795d848befcdf2e113734e5d: Grant two contracts to Accessories Tools Limited and Maintenance J.R. Villeneuve inc., for the seasonal rental of vacuum-type street broom on chassis with a capacity of 5.6 cubic metres, without operator and with maintenance for a period of three years - Total expenditure: $3,762,181.61, including taxes - Public tender 25-21257 (2 sum)
entries.45a7426ede1479dc9e9910ab55c309a1c9062325: Grant an OTC contract to the Canadian National Railway Company for work on the repair of the railway bridge over Wellington Street, between the streets of the Congregation and Sucrerie, in the South West District, including work by the Commission des Services électriques de Montréal / Authorize an expense of $11,497.50, including taxes, for the impact of the City's internal services - Total expenditure of $9,253,975.58, including taxes
entries.88a3f44130db7082f91baf4086464fc3ccc474bc: The CN / Wellington Railway Bridge, built in 1961, allows Wellington Street to pass under the tracks of the Canadian National Railway Company (CN), between De la Congrégation and De la Sucrerie streets, in Le Sud-Ouest borough (see attached location plan). Two orders of the Canadian Transportation Commission frame this work (see attached orders): - Order No. 100303 (1960): Authorizes the City of Montreal to build the bridge - Order No. 122813 (1966): Clarify the division of maintenance responsibilities: - City of Montréal: responsible for concrete components (pillars, abutments, retaining walls), approaches, rolling surfaces, drainage, sidewalks, lighting, pumping station and handrails. - CN: responsible for the steel part (establish), track, ballast and associated drainage system. Over the years, the bridge has been degraded due to freezing and thawing cycles, deglazing salts, general wear and tear.
entries.529ab9a582b56b9748422c394411453665a6e9b8: Grant an OTC contract to Transvrac Montréal-Laval inc., for the rental of trucks with operators for the transportation of excavated soils from Pointe Saint-Charles Company Park and the works floor storage base, and for the transportation of snowmelt residues from snow disposal sites, excavated soils and various bulk materials in different boroughs for a one-year period - Total expenditure of $1,829,028.05, including taxes / Approve draft agreement to this effect
entries.851496d360270201af927e68a343fc1f5274924d: SPEC excavated soils: The Boroughs and Citizen Experience Consultation Service (SCAEC) is responsible for operating and managing the excavated soil management site at Pointe Saint-Charles Enterprise Park (PEPSC) located at 1221 Carrie-Derick Street in Montreal. In the fall of 2020, the City acquired equipment from the EPPSC field to develop a pilot site to develop this activity and establish a business model that would enable, among other things, the development of low-contaminated soils. Since July 19, 2021, the site has been operational and hosts excavated soils from 15 boroughs and several central projects.
entries.beb5536a7530fced48f2e21e5bb2c90004cfa4ee: Grant an OTC contract to Productions Figure 55 inc., for professional services for the production, production and post-production of an immersive 360 dome film for the Montreal Planetarium - Total expenditure of $562,758.70 including taxes / Approve draft agreement to this effect
entries.8c2d76c3d2f31ae8e0441df8998f452fb4125c7e: By combining science, art and emotion, the Montreal Planetarium embodies the desire of Space for Life – Canada's largest museum complex in nature sciences – to offer unprecedented, strong and meaningful scientific experiences. In doing so, it pushes the boundaries of museum institutions dedicated to science and shapes new approaches to help bring people closer to nature. With its immersive exhibitions and shows, the Planetarium invites visitors to explore the Universe to discover and better understand fascinating astronomical phenomena.
entries.bc524362955dc9fc890088a7b8b898757bc3b77a: Grant an OTC contract to Lucion Media Inc., for professional services in the design and realization of multimedia artistic interventions for the event "Gardens of Light 2026" - Total expenditure of $103,546.49, including taxes
entries.95432b244ce5824aace3781eb5cddad0f58dff11: Provide $3,071,550 in financial support to the Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain (SOVERDI) to support the greening and strengthening of the Montreal canopy on private and institutional sites, for the period from March 24 to December 31, 2026 / Approve the draft convention to this effect / Authorize a budgetary transfer to PDI 2026 of $3,071,550 in local jurisdiction from the Branch to the Service des grands parcs, du Mont-Royal et des sports as part of the Urban Forest Plan
entries.3ee268bdccc53414e5c2fd89df227e879d1ac840: The Société de verdissement du Montréal métropolitain (SOVERDI) is a not-for-profit organization whose mission is to green the Montreal landscape by planting the right tree in the right place. Its action aims to significantly increase the urban forest in order to improve the health and quality of life of citizens.ne.s. SOVERDI supervises the member organizations of the Urban Forest Alliance in carrying out their greening projects.
entries.6cd2a799a9f19b6a201f717ed566bb95e00971ef: Provide $450,000 in financial support to the Plant Biology Research Institute, for a three-year period ending December 31, 2028, to support its mission for the years 2026, 2027 and 2028 / Approve the draft convention to this effect
entries.4ed523b1795bd434ac38e08899867f9548e322ec: Provide $525,000 in financial support to the Musée des Hospitalières de l'Hôtel-Dieu de Montréal for its operation and maintenance of its activities for the period 2026-2028 / Approve draft convention to this effect
entries.e5558df54ea8fdfa3e7c76e481be15d077bca439: The Museum of Hospitallers of the Hôtel-Dieu de Montréal is a depository OBNL of a unique heritage that presents history: 1. from the origins of Montreal and its foundation by Jeanne Mance to the equal of Paul de Chomedey, Sieur de Maisonneuve; 2. from the Fondation de l'Hôtel-Dieu by Jeanne Mance, first lay nurse in Canada; 3. from the Hospitallers of Saint Joseph in their mission of caring for the sick; 4. from the evolution of care and health sciences. The Museum tells the story of women, lay and religious, who have made a remarkable contribution to the establishment of Montreal through all the care they have given to the citizens who built the city, but also through their involvement in urban development at the foot of Mount Royal. As a unique witness to the history of medical knowledge, the collections presented and preserved at the Museum recount knowledge related both to medicinal plants and to the evolution of surgical tools while testifying on the human side of care as well as to the attention and empathy offered to patients.
entries.f4d9dd42799755bc25ff70fa6ca9da324ec02a76: Authorize an additional $3,400,000, including taxes, for the development of sustainable mobility corridors (traffic lights, civil and electrical works and cycle paths) in the boroughs of Ville-Marie and Mercier– Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, under the contract awarded to Bruneau Électrique inc. (CM25 0295), thereby increasing the total contract amount to $11,399,999.99, including taxes
entries.92e6a2c5411dbb9766511d26f8f877d89029eff7: On May 16, 2025, the City awarded Contract No. 521901 (CM25 0295, Decision File No. 1258848001) to Bruneau Électrique inc. This contract constitutes a framework agreement for the construction of sustainable mobility corridors, including cycle paths, civil and electrical works, as well as the installation and adjustment of traffic lights. The interventions concern the boroughs of Ville-Marie and Mercier– Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, specifically Hochelaga Street, between Frontenac Street and Desjardins Avenue, as well as Rue du Havre, between Hochelaga Street and Ontario Street.
entries.65f14a91b8c489f9bfaac5929aa42777adad52ae: Since 2014, the City of Montreal has made available to its citizens a fleet of bicycles in free sharing. These bikes, although operated by BIXI Montréal, remain the property of the City of Montreal. In 2024, operator BIXI Montréal concluded another record season with 13.9 million trips for a cumulative total of more than 75 million trips since 2009.
entries.51674a418e6348031c996623f28eb1dd6a36f311: Remediation of sewer pipes through the sheathing technique is proposed by the Asset Management Directorate (AMD) of the Water Service (SE). They are part of the strategy for water management of efficient infrastructure and are part of interventions that contribute to the improvement of collective infrastructure and the quality of life of citizens. This trench-free sheathing technique represents many advantages, compared with more traditional methods of reconstruction of sewage pipes by excavation, including: · Significant reduction in costs of execution compared to reconstruction by excavation; · Rapidity in carrying out the work; · Reduction of disturbances on surrounding infrastructure; · Timeliness of site restoration; · Reduction of the disposition of soil and excavation materials; · Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions compared to reconstruction by excavation; · Maintenance of traffic during construction.
entries.fec3d9179893a352f343bf10de4f7beb2bda3db1: Approve the draft addendum 1 amending the financial contribution agreement between UTILE Polytechnique and the City (CM25 0574) / Approve the draft subordination and non-intervention agreement between the Fédération des Caisses Desjardins du Québec, UTILE Polytechnique and the City of Montreal
entries.429b36f0513f6534bd3b28b6452bf959af83efe0: Approve the draft agreement with the Minister of the Environment, Climate Change Control, Wildlife and Parks for a grant of $13,500,000 for the implementation of a program to assist in the rehabilitation of contaminated land located on the territory of the City of Montreal / Authorize an additional budget of equivalent revenues and expenditures
entries.2c09a10d8619315dd5093b41efb41eabeea7436e: In 2018, a $75 million agreement was signed between the Minister of Sustainable Development, Environment and Climate Change Control and the City of Montreal. This agreement resulted in the implementation of a program to rehabilitate land on Montréal territory facing contamination problems in soil and/or groundwater. The agreement was the subject of several amendments, including one fifth that increased the initial envelope by $6.4 million.

C-11.4), to take over the tendering process, the award of the contract, the implementation and supervision of the construction of two bus stops on Saint-Patrick Street, at intersections of Eadie Street and Avenue de l'Église
entries.2657814eb4095a241bda30bd42dc6ec45f630015: As part of its approach to the modernization and optimization of the bus network, the Société de transport de Montréal (STM) is implementing a redevelopment of its network aimed at improving customer experience, increasing accessibility to public transportation and better meeting current and projected mobility needs in Montreal. This intervention provides for the development of two new bus stops on Saint-Patrick Street in the South-West borough of Eadie and the Church intersections. The implementation of these stops will help improve service to the sector and improve the conditions under which transit users can move.

entries.6f3a0f85d6e30f937a6e03590d71fdd1f904568c: Frédéric-Back Park is under the jurisdiction of the conseil d'agglomeration in accordance with the Schedule to the Montréal Agglomeration Order. The greenhouse project in this park, as proposed in its present form, was approved by the conseil d'agglomeration on February 19, 2026. The borough Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension (VSP) is the unit responsible for the development of this project.
entries.796b793e11228255e41d6cae6f5c0a8c5cbba337: Authorize a budgetary transfer of $1,879,500 net from the local road reserve to the urban planning and mobility department's operating budget 2026 for funding studies planned as part of the redevelopment of the Van Horne Viaduct and its surroundings
entries.f78f5f21bc8ffb7244eb04ab468a688f102fce05: As part of its mission to plan and guide the realization of an attractive, inclusive and resilient Montreal, the Urban Planning and Mobility Service (UMS) is responsible for implementing several major urban and mobility projects, including the replacement of the Rosemont - Van Horne viaduct. Built in 1971, the Rosemont – Van Horne viaduct allows 22,000 people a day to cross the Canadian Pacific Railways by connecting the boroughs of Rosemont–La-Petite-Patrie and Plateau-Mont-Royal. This structure has been subjected over the years to significant demands and is now in an advanced state of deterioration and is expected to reach its useful end around 2030.
entries.cbd91083439296e1721f7bb493cb7d9135c6e551: Authorize the submission of the application for the project "Development of the new electrical box intended to supply charging terminals for electric vehicles and self-service electric bicycle station" at the Municipal Merit Award 2026 Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing, in the category Municipality and Sustainable Development
entries.2b98581550e72ab2500955b46017992d575ab081: Authorize the application for the "59 Saint-Pierre" project for the Municipal Merit Award 2026 of the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing, in the category Municipality and Sustainable Development
entries.74fc2bbcb42d510d236123071b3f4695d4e75a7c: The Ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation (MAMH) recognizes, through the Municipal Merit Awards, the remarkable contribution of municipalities, organizations, groups and individuals who, through their dynamism and commitment, actively participate in the development of their community. Each two years, these awards also highlight initiatives that are motivating and innovative and inspire Quebec as a whole. The City of Montreal wishes to submit the candidacy of the 59 Saint-Pierre project in the municipality and sustainable development category, which rewards municipal projects that improve the quality of life of residents while integrating economic, social and environmental dimensions of sustainable development.
entries.92b5cf3dc4c8f61b36b033845f4e7406d8b299cf: Authorize the submission of the application for the project "Modernisation et décarburation des pratiques du concret à la Ville" at the Municipal Merit Award 2026 of the Ministry of Municipal Affairs and Housing, in the category Municipal Relève

entries.a63c45df8f79f73569a78dd3e64a69fe1c5331b4: The Jardin botanique de Montréal is one of the five scientific museum institutions in the City of Montreal, alongside Biodôme, Biosphere, Insectarium and Planetarium. Together they form Space for Life, the largest natural science complex in Canada. Through its conservation, research, education and dissemination activities, Space for Life accompanies the population towards a harmonious relationship with nature and encourages everyone to act to protect biodiversity and accelerate the socio-ecological transition.

entries.b192421d741b57e19a5b2ca8c79208e3a0ecce3a: On March 25, 2025, the Act to enact the Municipal Bodies Contracts Act and to amend various provisions, primarily for the purpose of reducing the administrative burden on municipal bodies , was assented to. As its name indicates, this Act enacts the Municipal Bodies Contracts Act (QLR, c. C-65.01) (hereinafter referred to as the "COMA"), which provides primarily for a review of the rules governing the award of certain contracts by municipal bodies.

entries.ba7878c71e9be34ae7be8b5756517a69ba573c67: Commitment to rigorous and responsible management of public finances The Administration wishes to adjust the administrative structure of the City to continue to optimize its resources and activities. In adopting Budget 2026, the Administration confirmed its intention to pursue its optimization efforts, in particular with a view to refocusing on the priority services offered to citizens and reducing central services by 1,000 posts over the next four years. A savings of $16 million is also provided for in Budget 2026.
entries.0de027d18df52bcf02adb20bfdc3d2dfd96d4b35: Adoption, without change, of Regulations Amending the Regulations to Improve Supply of Social, Affordable and Family Housing (20-041)
entries.7a101e04857b7dca9ea53225643c0432896cf356: Appointing Jean-François Sabourin, currently an alternate member, as a regular member to continue his first term of office ending on September 17, 2027, Nelly Charpentier, as an alternate member for a first term of three years, beginning on March 25, 2026 / Approve the renewal of Philippe Lupien's term of office as a regular member for a second non-renewable term of three years beginning on April 18, 2026
entries.1f3628886f7b431e92f08400cc48da2c30e51007: The Conseil du patrimoine de Montréal (CPM) is the City's advisory body on heritage matters. An important part of its mandate is to provide advice and recommendations in order to promote understanding, conservation and presentation of heritage within the framework of plans, projects and policies submitted to it. Under the Montreal Heritage Board Regulations (02-136), the CPM consists of nine (9) members, including one President and two (2) Vice-Presidents, as well as two (2) to five (5) alternate members.
entries.1d0015ee65bfd8db0b0b955e1778004925c35cd5: Appoint Audrey Girard, urbanist, as a member of the Jacques-Viger Committee for a first three-year renewable term, beginning on 23 March 2026
entries.b7410154338b98f8a955d69be5531a9305b64bcd: The Jacques-Viger Committee is the City of Montreal's advisory body on planning, urban planning, architecture, design and landscape architecture. It provides advice and comments and recommendations with a view to improving the quality of plans, projects and policies submitted to it, in accordance with the Jacques-Viger Committee Regulations (12-022), and gives its opinion to the City Council on any proposed amendments to the urban plan and any draft regulations adopted under section 89 (paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 5) of the Charter of the City of Montréal.
entries.67c7abfe5863fd22f6c176186106c26cf3a96166: Appoint Kevin Martinez and Iles Ousmer, as members of the Conseil jeunesse de Montréal, for a second three-year term beginning in March 2026
entries.6ef56b0815db587a045cd362cd1c0907b2df80d7: The Regulation respecting the Council of Montrealers, the Intercultural Council of Montreal and the Conseil jeunesse de Montréal (CjM) (19-051) governs the operation of the CjM. These regulations provide that the CjM is composed of 15 members, including one person serving on the Chair and two persons serving on the Vice-Chair (section 3). When there are departures or mandate purposes, vacancies must be filled.
entries.f040693a1542604f0c99fef6c28cf87d882f1d0d: Appoint Chahi (Sharkie) Tarakjian to the Commission on Culture, Heritage and Sport and appoint Michèle Tremblay to the Commission on Water, Environment, Sustainable Development and Large Parks

entries.3e0aac36a64032dc370a94782d40dc28c309b6eb: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshops Service (SMRA) is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as to provide a variety of specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services, in an environmentally responsible manner and in a safe environment. As part of its 2026 rolling stock acquisition planning, SMRA has identified the need to acquire eleven (11) motorcycles to meet the operational requirements of the City of Montreal Police Service (SPVM). This requirement led to the launch of Public Call for Bids No. 25-21193.

entries.a6e8cb3d8988cc2c56da2a10ac0c201a337e0d71: In July 2025, the public tender 25-21077 was published on the Electronic Tendering System (ESAA), as well as in the Journal de Montréal , for the supply of genuine Freightliner brand parts intended for use in municipal mechanical workshops. These parts are essential to the maintenance and repair of heavy vehicles in the city's motor vehicle fleet. They are exclusively available from authorized dealers of the brand.
entries.5397b12441d751783eb698edbfce6bdeedc57fc7: Exercising the option of the first 12-month extension and authorizing an additional expenditure of $233,974.40, including taxes, for the short-term rental of two carry-on trucks with a nominal height of 55 feet or more, without operator and with maintenance, under the framework agreement with La Compagnie de Leasing d'Autos Enterprise Canada (CG25 0173), thus increasing the total amount of the framework agreement to $474,646.50, including taxes
entries.f4ef786917331ff812b0702fcbda0e94de464dea: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (WMS) is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as to provide a variety of specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services, in an environmentally responsible and safe environment.
