(CM25,0774), thereby increasing the total contract amount from $2,728,892.08 to $3,148,550.83 including taxes
entries.0a4bcb9536e11fd69008aa3626349e6a5a95aa74: Grant an OTC contract to La Messe Basse for the realization and installation of the immersive and interactive museum experience Contact77 at Planétarium de Montréal - Total expenditure of $919,799.88 including taxes / Approve draft service agreement for this purpose
entries.2cf49ba5962373ccc43a9b9ec0496b7ec5318f67: Conclude a framework agreement with Infrastructel inc. for professional work monitoring services during modifications to the Montreal Electrical Services Commission's underground network, for a period of 36 months - Estimated amount of the agreement: $849,808.97, including taxes - Public tender S-2346 (5 Som.) / Approve draft agreement to this effect
entries.9ac5320686c4572e00d958649d4a6cefacb87379: Approve the draft agreement between the City of Montreal and the Société de transport de Montréal to authorize work for the construction of the Irma-LeVasseur Park Pavilion and the installation of a masonry flooring at Wiseman Mechanical Ventilation Station in Outremont District, as part of the implementation of the urban project MIL Montréal
entries.34af719c6c1e8a9512e9167388f0963da21cfe83: As part of the implementation of the MIL Montréal project, in April 2025 the City undertook the development of the new Irma-LeVasseur Neighbourhood Park. This park is one of four hectares of new public spaces developed as part of the redevelopment of the former Outremont Yard Station, which was built in partnership with the Université de Montréal. With an area of 18,500 m2, the park will be located south of Thérèse-Lavoie-Roux Avenue between Dollard Avenue to the west and Wiseman Avenue to the east.
entries.2558cc14f46899381c67c582021a6cb2a9af60d4: Approve the proposed amendment to the lease by which the City leases to Cytec Canada Inc., for an additional two years beginning March 1, 2026, premises 103, 105 and 111 located at 7140 Albert Street-Einstein, with an area of 609 square feet, for office space purposes, for a rent of $48,000, excluding taxes
entries.17b0ff0e53901492f86989f41957107762cd656f: The City owns two rental buildings located in the Technoparc of the borough of Saint-Laurent, namely, the Business Centres at 7140 Albert-Einstein Street and 2300 Alfred-Nobel Boulevard. The Business Centres offer office space for small start-up companies working in the technology and scientific research sectors. The Rental Division of the Real Estate Strategy Service (SSI) is responsible for renting available spaces in these buildings and managing leases.
entries.1a349b6451fa6a6ac1bf3ba756849b2223dc8f69: Approve the proposed lease by which the City of Montreal leases to Marion-Prune Paycha, for a period of 24 months, effective February 1, 2026, room 152, located at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest (Cité-des-Hospitalières), with an area of 141 square feet, for office purposes and exhibition and distribution of photographic work, for a total rent of $6,281.52, excluding taxes
entries.6688008405fd624e782a51bbe386dae1acd04c3b: Approve the proposed lease by which the City of Montreal leases to Startop, for a period of 24 months beginning February 1, 2026, room 387, located at 251, Avenue des Pins Ouest (Cité-des-Hospitalières), with an area of 653 square feet, for office purposes, coworking, workshops and conferences to women entrepreneurs, for a total rent of $34,380.36, excluding taxes
entries.e717eb7d25c7d321416a84903a36d1e0c08537f8: Approve the proposed lease by which the City leases to the Association québécoise des connecteurs et des artisanes du livre, for a period of 24 months beginning February 1, 2026, room 388, located at 251, avenue des Pins Ouest (Cité-des-Hospitalières), with an area of 562 square feet, for initiation workshops, volume repairs, conferences and offices, for a total rent of $16,472.28, excluding taxes. The amount of the real estate subsidy is $8,581.74
entries.bddbf2350ab7805b7d00234c8c03b3cbb5f4e6a1: In 2017, the City of Montreal (City) acquired the Religious Hospitallers of Saint-Joseph, the Cité-des-Hospitalières (Cité), located at 201 to 251-A, avenue des Pins Ouest (L'Immeuble). The City, as owner of this heritage site, has a responsibility to protect this environment and its cultural and landscape heritage. The City's protection efforts and the project to enhance the site must comply with the following five principles, enshrined in the act of sale: The preservation of the spirit of the place; Respect for the values of the Religious and their spiritual mission; Protection and sustainability of the built and natural heritage; Consistency with the history of the site; Openness to the community and the response to its needs.
entries.e7f552df1a7a2d9ca89508b66991e82270df9d4f: Provide $300,000 in financial support to the Bureau du cinéma et de la télévision du Québec for its plan for the promotion, outreach and attractiveness of the Montréal audiovisual industry 2025-2028 / Approve a draft convention to this effect
entries.255a14d590e7d080078cceeae41a52fd3d3deb14: The Bureau du cinéma et de la télévision du Québec (BCTQ) is an industrial cluster recognized by the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal. Its mission is to contribute to the development and competitiveness of Quebec's audiovisual sector. The BCTQ promotes metropolis as a must-see destination of international calibre for all segments of the audiovisual production industry, including filming, visual effects, animation and post-production.
entries.ee33fa427eeed9a7287d92f9d7aac3264af11956: Provide $100,000 in financial support and $57,765 in technical support to the National Institute of Scientific Research (INRS), for a three-year research project entitled "Enhancing the resilience of municipalities to climate change through the integration of green solutions and engineering" / Approve draft convention to this effect
entries.e96167b7c716df318fd1fa2029d3c8913a2d0cf5: The research project "Enhancing the resilience of municipalities to climate change through the integration of green and engineering solutions", initiated and managed by the National Institute for Scientific Research (INRS), has as its main objective to quantify and then optimize the benefits of stormwater management infrastructure in order to increase the resilience of municipalities to climate change. It focuses on three main themes: 1. quantification of processes associated with green infrastructure related to adaptation to climate change, through various experimental monitoring in situ and in controlled environments; 2. optimization of benefits through model development and integration into dynamic infrastructure control; 3. development of decision support tools based on the life cycle of green infrastructure.
entries.9a9834cf3dcb94c545952bf3f6fe9de40d23472b: Provide $100,000 in financial support and $75,000 in technical support to the Marine Mammal Research and Education Group for the exhibition "Discovering the social life of bluvets at the Biodôme", for a period of three years / Approve the draft convention to this effect
entries.b8cc1d84661e74aa26e3f620c60afa0e1b54b0e5: The beluga is an umbrella species at the top of the food chain, highlighting the biological as well as physical and geological uniqueness of the St. Lawrence estuary. The beluga of the St. Lawrence estuary is a threatened species.
entries.1e94c0cde8956ba367287ce32fad5191d713f4f3: Approve the draft act by which the City acquires from the Société de développement et de valorisation du Parc olympic, a property known as the Planetarium de Montréal, consisting of Lot 5,647,842 of the cadastre du Québec, Registration Division of Montreal, located in the Olympic Park, in the arrondissement of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve
entries.e09f93b15254e9e577e5c4d71079c52b6778a9e5: On 15 March 2011, the Régie des installations olympices (R.I.O.), which has since become the Société de développement et de mise en valeur du Parc olymique (Société), and the City of Montreal (Ville) concluded an agreement of usufruct (Convention) to authorize the City to build a new museum dedicated to education and dissemination of information in the field of astronomy (Planétarium) on the property of the RIO described in the Convention, in the district of Mercier-Hochelaga-Maisonneuve, northwest of the Cinéma StarCité Montréal, west of Centre Pierre-Charbonneau, south of the practice ground of the Stade de soccer Saputo and contiguous with the Biodôme. The Convention provides, inter alia: - the waiver of the R.I.O. to the benefit of accession so that the constructions and works carried out by the City on the building may be wholly owned by the City; - the execution of a cadastral operation once the Planetarium has been constructed to permit the creation of a lot comprising the constructions and works carried out by the City (Propriété); - the City; - the transfer to the sale.
entries.718e7f1f2477752f4ab4e4ec70fbaeda04b07c6d: Approve the draft lease by which the City rents to Naos jeunesse: creativity in action!, for a period of 24 months, beginning on February 1, 2026, premises 451 and 460, located at 251 Avenue des Pins Ouest (Cité-des-Hospitalières), with an area of 431 square feet, for office purposes, community services, and educational workshops for young girls, for a total rent of $20,416.44, excluding sales taxes
entries.5315d387902a0a4a58ce8077bc866feb359f7cdf: In 2017, the City of Montreal (City) acquired the Religious Hospitallers of Saint-Joseph, the Cité-des-Hospitalières (Cité), located at 201 to 251-A, avenue des Pins Ouest (L'Immeuble). The City, as owner of this heritage site, has the responsibility to protect this environment and its cultural and landscape heritage. The City's protection efforts and the project to enhance the site must comply with the following five principles, enshrined in the act of sale: The preservation of the spirit of the place; Respect for the values of the Religious and their spiritual mission; Protection and sustainability of the built and natural heritage; Consistency with the history of the site; Openness to the community and the response to its needs.
entries.06fe2faa82d639d818991072c354ac4a23b9b8ba: Repeal resolution CM25 1239 / Approve the draft act by which the City of Montreal sells to the Société québécoise des infrastructures, for assembly to its main building and storage, vacant land known and designated as set-aside lots 6 700 464, 6 700 466, 6 700 468 and 6 700 456 as well as lots 1,260 692, 1,260 693, 1,260 694 and 1,260 733 of the cadastre du Québec, electoral district of Montréal, in the borough of Rivière-des-Prairies– Pointe-aux-Trembles, with an area of 4,352 square metres, for an amount of $1,171,123, plus applicable taxes
entries.226262b427fd364e35773bf3926deca95dd20160: Authorize the filing of an application to obtain access to the transitional measure of the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change Control, Wildlife and Parks (MELCCFP) for the flood protection structure, namely the dyke at 5th Avenue Nord, in the district of Pierrefonds-Roxboro
entries.4f136366d2e77626a99d708dac9bc4137ab5126a: In June 2025, the Ministry of Environment, Climate Change Control, Wildlife and Parks (MELCCFP) announced the adoption of a modernized water regulatory framework. The Flood Protection Works Regulations (ROPI), which form part of this new framework, require municipalities to provide preliminary information on the location of their protection structures to the Department before March 1, 2026, and a municipality may file an application for access to the transitional measure prior to that date.
entries.02267cf1d7d29fab2bb93a0bcdaec2fe3b03525c: Authorize the application of the Ville de Montréal's Environmental Service to the Municipal Merit of the Ministère des Affaires municipales et de l'Habitation du Québec for the Saint-Laurent Organic Materials Processing Centre project
entries.f83e1e4f66db2b4799b5d4dd3f4270ac0f5d1d97: In 2025, the completion of the deployment of organic material collection for all Montrealers, as well as the first year of operation of the St. Lawrence Centre for Organic Material Processing (CTMO), represented two major advances towards the Montréal zero waste target by 2030. Beyond its operational role, CTMO is a structuring project that combines innovation, sustainability and education to strengthen community resilience.
entries.5f6033454d6c4057f1ff9be4ee2765bf27150f60: Adopt a resolution approving the extension of the admission hours of the commercial establishment Séduction de la S.I.D.A.C. Plaza Saint-Hubert as part of the Nuit Blanche du Festival Montréal en lumières event, during the night of February 28 to March 1, 2026
entries.24c27c92906e99499fa2d597edb0f8a00443b0aa: To extend the declaration of jurisdiction of the Council of the City, for a period of five years beginning on March 22, 2026, with respect to the adoption of regulations relating to the parking on the local road network of self-service vehicles having no specifically reserved parking on the street and the issuance of permits for the parking of such vehicles as well as certain maintenance activities (laying, removal, maintenance, replacement) related to charging stations, in accordance with section 85.5 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (RLRQ, c. C-11.4)
entries.986dfc855c24faa7a440de8625b13df701687069: Prior to the City Council's first declaration of jurisdiction in 2016 with respect to self-service carsharing vehicles (VLS), universal parking permits for these vehicles were issued by the boroughs under different terms and conditions. The city council's declaration of jurisdiction allowed the city centre to adopt the Self-Service Car Parking Regulations (16-054), harmonizing parking regulations and the issuance of permits across the territory. These regulations specify, among other things, the areas in which VLS parking is permitted, mainly in residential street parking areas (SRRR).
entries.f3fcfb5c9361a668a263b0379137adde9638e5c5: Authorize the district of Mercier–Hochelaga-Maisonneuve to carry out work to transform the former Maisonneuve Market, located at 4375 Ontario Street East, in the classified heritage site of the Ancienne-Cité-de-Maisonneuve, lot 1 878 407 du cadastre du Québec, electoral division of Montreal, pursuant to section 64 and chapter VI.1 of the Cultural Heritage Act
entries.d377d25c889eb9f96dab4ac9eb1d8aa97b96cadd: The former Maisonneuve market was built in 1912. It occupies a dominant position in the Hochelaga-Maisonneuve district. Designed in the "city beautiful" style, popular at the time, the building retained a public vocation, but ceased its market activities in 1962.
entries.3016164434716a16c246207592903054f7e1933b: Approve the draft financing agreement between the City of Montreal and the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal as part of the restoration of the riverbank of the Prairies in the borough of Montréal-Nord
entries.52472cbfc000e3934dbe01e3007195d41cf04c48: As part of the project to restore and stabilize the banks of the borough of Montréal-Nord, at its meeting on December 15, 2025, the City Council authorized the application for financial support from the borough to the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal (CMM). It is now appropriate to approve the financing agreement between the City of Montreal and the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal and authorize the Deputy Clerk of the City of Montreal to sign it.
entries.4b937ceaeda439c7be1a5a35f166d561f1fb09dd: Notice of Motion and Filing - Regulations authorizing Videotron to permanently occupy the public domain for the purpose of installing a telecommunications tower in Victor-P.-Gray Park
entries.d55547fd53ddd7dac3cefa9649ee1d6ab8edcf02: Notice of Motion and Tabling - Regulations Establishing the Nocturnal Vitality Business Assistance Program
entries.04783fb0fbe730bf757298a7a00a7a3164f5d72c: Notice of Motion and Filing - Regulations Amending the City Council Contract Management Regulations (18-038)
entries.3f844b9253c4a742d56209a740d704b0cec7ad80: Notice of Motion and Tabling - Services Regulations
entries.1fc3a0731be13e11851a33af92a17e75575e98d5: Adoption - Regulations Amending Regulation 2486 adopted by the former City of Lachine in respect only of the residual portion of the alley south of Sherbrooke Street, between 6th Avenue and 7th Avenue, Lachine borough, for transfer to riparian owners
entries.2b1c698630ec0eab70ebae15e8318373d8e7a195: Adoption - Regulations authorizing a loan of $98,000,000 to finance the work of Phase Two of the Underground Infrastructure Reconstruction and Redevelopment Project on Avenue des Pins
entries.1130a635623ebf1e0351dfe23696dc1f3c249938: The area of the former Royal Victoria Hospital The area of the former Royal Victoria Hospital is the subject of concerted planning between the City of Montreal, the Société québécoise des infrastructures and McGill University. This historic area within the Mount Royal Heritage Site provides for the requalification of the various pavilions to house institutional and residential functions, as well as the expansion of Mount Royal Park and the creation of a new entrance to access it. The site will eventually accommodate nearly 6,000 new users, requiring significant improvements in safety and accessibility, particularly for active and collective mobility.
entries.ce86c0e620d43e0355503afa382749f5c36a399b: Notice of Motion, Tabling and Adoption of Proposed Regulations entitled "Regulations Amending the Regulations to Improve the Supply of Social, Affordable and Family Housing (20-041)" / Public Consultation / Delegation of Authority to Clerk
entries.54eefd89966fd8ef73a02eee454c6ba6d5617266: Regulation 20-041 to improve the supply of social, affordable and family housing, known as the Mixed Metropolis (MMR) Regulations, came into effect on April 1, 2021. Since that date, funding programs and residential real estate markets have evolved so that enforcement has become more complex and it is therefore planned to replace it with a new incentive approach.
entries.aad67919f5fc237c7b9eba6831693536119d1fe8: Appoint Émilie Bouchard as a member of the Conseil interculturelle de Montréal for a second three-year term beginning February 2026
entries.fc07a9257b52db0ec8a57361b067ca6abe6e15d0: Name Gabrielle Rousseau-Bélanger, Councillor of the City of Pointe-aux-Trembles District of Rivière-des-Prairies–Pointe-aux-Trembles, as an observer member of the Montreal Food System Council (Montréal Food System Council) for a period of three years, until February 11, 2029
entries.d13730103064d8d3b0963c08a7c7c2063226631e: The Montreal Food System (SAM) is a regional network consisting of several food partners (production, processing, distribution, consumption and post-consumption). Its mission is to ensure strong regional leadership in food by mobilizing stakeholders, advising decision makers and supporting structuring initiatives. Created in 2018, the SAM Council (CSAM) is the decision-making body of the SAM and brings together members from diverse backgrounds (economic, academic, institutional, philanthropic, community, etc.).
entries.41a699ececbe14761c1bb480d80fd307ef6d0afe: Motion of the Official Opposition - For a City that respects science in its public decisions
entries.593da05d720724f980043959d26db90020aa8a92: Motion of the Official Opposition - 10th anniversary of the submission of the Charbonneau Commission's final report: reaffirmation of the principles of transparency and integrity
entries.cb27e98a30d6d9c2b7556cf6b97787af2fcf4e1a: Motion of the Official Opposition - Preserving and strengthening the strategic role of the Office of Commissioners
entries.5a814e4407b1ba340bdf085fe41ef217137ca79d: Exercising the option of the first 12-month extension and authorizing an additional expenditure of $671,469.74, including taxes, of $671,469.74 for printing and distribution of information notices to the population in neighbourhoods and districts where work will soon be undertaken, under the contract awarded to Printemploi (CG24,0062), thus increasing the total amount of the contract to $1,953,656.23, including taxes
entries.b6052b5084578271312702df0b9fc9d0d4f967b2: The Human Resources and Communications Service is expected to provide information to the population of neighbourhoods and districts where work will be undertaken in the near future; this information relates to the nature and duration of work, obstacles to traffic, temporary closure of water supply, etc. The transmission of this essential information is carried out in particular by distributing letters upstream, works notices, letters granting (for lead file) and invitation cards for public information sessions.
entries.85150725c011ac1bb90bf7c4d7d7251e5902f661: Exercising the 12-month extension option and authorizing an additional expenditure of $10,000,000, including taxes, for the provision of desktop computers, laptops, servers and electronic tablets and accessories under the framework agreement with the Government Acquisition Centre (CG24 0198), thereby increasing the total contract amount to $30,500,000, including taxes
entries.ec294027cb7d7d7d41df10eef2055da74bf77799: Exercise the 12-month extension option and authorize an additional expenditure of $252,424.49, including taxes, for laser printing services, insertion, shipment and supply of stationery for municipal court notices under the contract awarded to 9169-9835 Québec inc. (Publications 9417) (CE24 0132), thus increasing the total contract amount to $744,575.95, including taxes
entries.67270076a9711402d366d2fb98dc7535078f0064: Following the closure of the City of Montréal's printing plant, in 2015 the municipal court launched a public tender to identify a company that will be able to print, insert, ship and provide the stationery necessary to continue to send its various notices to the defendants. Contracts were awarded to Publications 9417 for the period 2016-2026. The current contract expires on March 7, 2026.
entries.3f24042d9ee2fd3ca436e19704d74809e143dde1: Exercise the option of the first 12-month extension and authorize an additional expenditure of $1,264,392.63, including taxes, for professional and technical services in biology for various projects under the agreement with Stantec Consultants Ltd. (CG24,0202), thereby increasing the total contract amount to $3,732,831.15, including taxes
entries.e34d8ad92aff7593c2edfdcf667b3a1c3a6428d8: The Great Parks, Mount Royal and Sports Service (SMPMRS) entered into a framework agreement with Stantec Consultants Ltd. on April 18, 2024, for a total of $2,468,438.52 including taxes for professional and technical services in biology. These services permit the conduct of studies conducted over the past 30 years by the SGPMRS to acquire biological knowledge essential to the management of natural environments and the realization of projects. This contract expires on April 18, 2026.
entries.64c6798cfe5d36518d1c5de0b6ac5303ef2cf8b6: Exercising the five-year extension option and authorizing an additional expenditure of $5,157,101.77, including taxes, for maintenance and support services of Ariel Pension Management Software, under the contract awarded to Telus Health (CANADA) Ltd, (CG21,0069), thereby increasing the total contract amount to $9,824,111, including taxes
entries.0fd108b4d014cb7c4ee2335700a609850de86f43: The City of Montreal (the "City") introduced a pension administration system in 2011 following a public tender (CE11 0326). The Montréal Pension Plan Office (the "BRRM") uses the Ariel software package from Telus Health (CANADA) Ltd (formerly Morneau Shepell Ltd) to administer the City's pension plans. Following the implementation of the Ariel system in 2012, the City invested in updating the software package to reflect legislative changes as well as amendments to the provisions of the various Montreal pension plans resulting from agreements between the City and the various unions and associations.
entries.d9ca57f83c0bcb15799e12847ffda6d3948bb38b: Grant an OTC contract to Nature-Action Québec Inc. for the technical services of manual control against invasive alien plant species in large parks, for a period of three years - Total expenditure of $1,730,971.08
entries.04659409319bed67b7695fb161f28b517b506598: Invasive Alien Plant Species (IEEVs) threaten the ecological integrity of large parks, compromising biodiversity and ecological services. To preserve these natural assets and reduce future costs associated with the degradation of natural environments, the Great Parks, Mount Royal and Sports Service (SMPMRS) conducts targeted manual interventions that limit impacts on species of conservation interest and promote natural restoration processes, particularly in forest environments.
entries.f033c6fe2274f4b655be524edca54c41375accda: Contract with Innotex Inc. for the supply of fire fighting clothing - Total expenditure of $1,260,873.34, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25-21238 (1 compliant sum)
entries.5bdd29b727779a5557063914914b8e2559c67a43: Combat clothing is an integral part of firefighters' and firefighters' personal protective equipment and equipment. In the Montreal Fire Safety Service (SIM), firefighters and firefighters as well as staff members have two combat clothes at their disposal. Thus, during routine post-fire washes or when sending one of their two combat clothes for their annual advanced inspection and cleaning, they have a suit available to them.
entries.4faed03ddb1bf21ae6d56abd777e9f24f1b1f7fe: Grant a contract to Tuyauterie Expert Inc., for the decarbonization work, and for the replacement of natural gas heating equipment with non-GHG equipment at Barrack 66, located at 4398 LaSalle Boulevard, in Verdun District - Total expenditure of $1,266,564.61, including taxes - Public Call for Bids IMM-15952 (7 sum)
entries.09e187661f28e030ddb3ba77c283eb70a094a645: As part of the Government of Quebec's 2030 Green Economy Implementation Plan (GEP), the Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) and the City of Montréal (Ville) signed a grant agreement on March 28, 2022 (Agreement) to enable the latter to implement certain measures of its Climate Plan 2020 - 2030 (Climate Plan) in response to the MOP. The agreement contributes, among other things, to supporting the financing of decarbonation projects for thirty-two (32) buildings identified by the Building Management and Planning Service (SGPI) as one of the largest emitters of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in municipal real estate (Parc), whose ultimate objective is to reduce emissions of approximately 7,000 tonnes CO2 eq., or about 25% of the GHG emissions of that park.
entries.0d8cb5482739457be8fc1f51f482295e970ad8f0: Grant a contract to Le Groupe M.E.A.S. inc. for the decarbonization and replacement of natural gas heating equipment with non-GHG equipment at Barracks 47, located at 2111 Saint-Zotique Street, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie borough - Total expenditure of $1,305,578.38, including taxes - Public tender IMM-15951 (7 som)
entries.cab74d4f8a4c04e83d66e2327856f1222968581d: As part of the Government of Quebec's 2030 Green Economy Implementation Plan (GEP), the Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) and the City of Montreal (Ville) signed a grant agreement on March 28, 2022 (Agreement) to enable the latter to implement certain measures of its Climate Plan 2020 - 2030 (Climate Plan) responding to the GEP. The Agreement is intended to support the financing of carbon-decarbonation projects for 32 buildings identified by the Building Management and Planning Service (SGPI) as one of the largest emitters of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in municipal real estate (Parc), whose long-term objective is to reduce emissions of approximately 7,000 tonnes CO2 eq., or about 25% of the GHG emissions of the said park. The Carbon Decarbonation Project 47 is part of Action 30 of the Climate Plan to transform 100% of the Park into an operational zero carbon park by 2030.
entries.5a65fcfe216d77ed2894b91f336c9303100456ed: Grant a contract of agreement to the Société du Parc Jean-Drapeau, for the period from January 1 to December 31, 2026, for the general coordination of the celebrations of the 50th anniversary of the Montreal Olympic Games in 2026 - Total expenditure of $125,000 / Approve the draft service agreement to this effect
entries.fa36a8f31e19c14415e1e8e12fc943aa4f092964: The year 2026 marks the 50th anniversary of the 1976 Olympic Games, which have profoundly characterized the City of Montreal, Quebec society and sport in Canada. Montréal wishes to mark the 50th anniversary of these Games throughout its territory. The Société du Parc Jean-Drapeau is a national and international leader in the field of sport, making a significant contribution to the influence and attractiveness of Montreal's metropolis.
entries.39670a9c2ceb686b79e346ca6a7a9a8075714872: Award a contract to Merkur Solutions Ltd., for expert development professional services HCL Domino and associated technologies, for a period of 24 months, including two 24-month extension options - Total expenditure of $326,712.96, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25-21192 (1 compliant sum)
entries.6b19ff593a38dbcc72de91ca6d3cfd487463ac71: Provide $500,000 in financial support to Mission Old Brewery, in the form of a mortgage-guaranteed financial contribution, for the construction of a building at 2801 rue de Rouen, in the borough of Ville-Marie / Approve the draft agreement to this effect
entries.a6e47b7ba851a470b870bdd66036fd89ab97375d: The City of Montreal is supporting, where possible, projects by filling, on an ad hoc basis, a lack of financial support. This is the case here for the social housing project Les Discréts de Rouen, carried out as part of the Initiative for the Rapid Creation of Housing – Project Component for which the City is contributing with additional financial assistance. The purpose of this summary is to approve an agreement to grant a financial contribution of up to $500,000 to the non-profit organization Mission Old Brewery (the Agency).
entries.05e8f5666056823b12647ae5a3bc04d73273ba8d: Conclude framework agreements with Sanexen Environmental Services Inc. and Loiselle Inc. for the City's 24-month contaminated soil management services, including two 12-month extension options - Estimated amount of agreements: $2,080,534.43, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25-21166 (4 sum)
entries.fd5642a775467760ee1be89b38473ae81d6402e6: The Ville de Montréal Water Service's mission is to provide drinking water for the Montreal community, manage stormwater and clean wastewater in order to ensure public health and safety and protect the environment, today and for future generations. The Water Systems Directorate is responsible for the distribution of quality drinking water and the collection of wastewater by carrying out projects to upgrade and develop network assets, while ensuring their operation and maintenance. The City of Montréal, as part of its municipal infrastructure maintenance and repair activities, must manage excavated contaminated soil in accordance with existing regulations.
entries.9a29ea9d397d87ce34d4cc0616493ba7d778c22e: Conclude framework agreements with Canadian Bearings Ltd. and Acklands-Grainger Inc. for the provision of 36-month personal protective equipment - Estimated amount of agreements: $964,946.32 including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25,21164 (5 sum)
entries.4bf78f79785d226a470cb2ffb4b132e6b22ea392: The purpose of this file is to conclude three framework agreements for the provision of personal protective equipment (PPE) upon request, primarily designed to ensure the protection and safety of employees of the City of Montreal in the performance of their duties. These framework agreements will be made available to all business units of the City of Montréal. Public tender 25-21164 has been published on the Electronic Tendering System (ESET) as well as in Le Devoir.
entries.fa4511bd4d13e630dc3a43e32c2ac6fbfdccf88e: Conclude framework agreements with Techno Feu inc., for the supply of spare parts for E-One fire trucks, lasting two years, including two extension options of 12 months each - Estimated amount of agreements: $2,580,490.08, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25-20983 (2 sum)
entries.ab5c31912f779b1bea3067f8b15d6f31ec2e939a: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (MRS) is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as to provide a variety of specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services, in an environmentally responsible manner and in a safe environment. As part of its planning, the Rolling Stock Service identified the need to create three (3) framework agreements for the provision of spare parts for E-One fire trucks, in order to meet the operational requirements of the City of Montreal for the Montreal Fire Safety Service (SIM), which led to the launch of the Public Call for Bids, No. 25-20983.
entries.82baea2927fec9a2b21ff05f480d9c7db52375c3: Conclude a framework agreement with Goodfellow Inc. for the supply of Sapin Douglas wood for the manufacture of urban furniture, lasting two years, including two extension options of 12 months each - Estimated amount of the agreement: $221,476.55, including taxes - Public tender 25-21205 (3 sum)
entries.b1129fc16e23a476f6a61383c83f540e24a03b20: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (SMRA) is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as to provide a variety of specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services, in an environmentally responsible manner and in a safe environment. The carpentry team, which is an integral part of SMRA, is responsible for the manufacture and supply of replacement parts for urban furniture. As part of its planning for the purchase of raw materials, SMRA had identified the need to acquire one (1) type of wood, i.e. Sapin Douglas wood.
entries.6eaafdd85e660551fbac32b7d91940c61a3c49e3: Conclude framework agreements with Videotron Ltd. and TELUS Communications Inc. for 60-month cellular data, support and professional services, including two 24-month extension options each - Estimated amount of agreements: $4,897,378, 86 including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25,21133 (4 sum)
entries.57dd028ddd7744c15a77754e1f3222b4cd2c55dc: Conclude a framework agreement with Groupe Conseil CHG inc. for three-year professional services in building structure engineering, including a 12-month extension option - Estimated amount of the agreement: $517,387.50, including taxes - Public Call for Bids 25-21074 (9 som)

The call for tenders was separated into 2 separate lots to allow firms active only in certain niches to submit a proposal. entries.cc33c5599b75167d4c2af05247f4105edee00257: Unilaterally terminate the contract awarded to AVI-SPL Canada Ltd. for the provision of audiovisual equipment for meeting rooms (CG25 0590)
entries.e1bb94b478c22948b286d6547d796488f54443ce: Approve draft Addendum 1 to the Financial Contribution Agreement between the City of Montreal, Friends of the Mountain and Centre de la montagne following the coming into force of the new provisions of Act 25 respecting access to documents of public bodies and protection of personal information
entries.0d2d55d9d0ff259983ca3371ca973aa3ac21e259: Following the coming into force of the new provisions of Act 25 relating to access to public records and protection of personal information, the Great Parks, Mount Royal and Sports Service wishes to clarify its expectations with respect to contractors involved in the sharing of personal information necessary for the fulfilment of its mandate. The attached addendum provides clarifications in this regard, which were not included in the contract document approved in 2023 and currently in effect.
entries.bb5750cff4ebfe766b8ae9b1c1475d4275095fc9: Exercise the 12-month extension option, without additional expense, for the City of Montreal's contribution to the work of the Industrial Chair in Drinking Water, as part of the agreement established with the Corporation of École Polytechnique de Montréal (CG22 0640)
entries.15f7135e98277b954602d30e4eae388ca597d979: Polytechnique Montréal's Industrial Chair in Drinking Water (CIEP) has existed since 1992. Its primary mission is to produce scientifically recognized results that can be used by industry and municipalities to improve the treatment and distribution of drinking water, while minimizing health risks. The City of Montreal has been participating in CIEP since 2005.
entries.b298fbe5418750b10fbd5a4be82c340d3c880acd: Grant a contract to the Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec for the provision of banking services, for a period of five years, including two three-year extension options - Total expenditure of $2,291,231.87, including taxes - Public tender 25-21116 (3 sum)
entries.06d3e77ef3863f97e674952cc4bd8a1f89bbb2ae: The City of Montreal wishes to retain the services of a primary provider to provide its banking services related to the collection, disbursement and management of its bank accounts. The contract awarded in 2018 (Appeal for tender #17-1584) initially consolidated banking services and merchant accounts. As financial institutions no longer provide market account services, this file deals only with banking services.
entries.484a2f5c7f9d286f28aae2f80dd921077f989dbb: To award a contract to Oslo Construction Inc. for decarbonization work, including the replacement of natural gas heating equipment with greenhouse gas-free equipment at barracks 31, located at 7041 Saint-Dominique Street, Rosemont–La Petite-Patrie District - Total expenditure of $1,935,440.42, taxes included - Public Call for Bids IMM-15965 (7 som)
entries.d17a4533542ed307a19aced43fe201f4bcab2439: As part of the Government of Quebec's 2030 Green Economy Implementation Plan (GEP), the Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) and the City of Montreal (Ville) signed a grant agreement on March 28, 2022 (the Agreement) to enable the latter to implement certain measures of its Climate Plan 2020 - 2030 (Climate Plan) that meet the objectives of the MOP. The Agreement contributes in particular to supporting the financing of carbon-decarbonation projects for thirty-two (32) buildings identified by the Building Management and Planning Service (EMPI) as one of the largest emitters of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in the municipal real estate park (Parc). The ultimate objective is to reduce emissions by approximately 7,000 tonnes eq.
entries.c3098fa6a64af4a445f960154ab1cdbbd3a7956e: Contract with Gagné & Roy Inc. for the replacement of seven roof basins at Pointe-Claire water filtration plant - Total expenditure of $1,939,714.48 including taxes - Public Call for Bids IMM-15980 (6 som)
entries.b3b9a71773b1ddc5672d9e2e1d26de1263f6d5f3: The Pointe-Claire drinking water production plant (3277), located at 243, chemin du Bord- du-Lac-Lakeshore, in the town of Pointe-Claire, was built in the late 1960s and provides drinking water for part of the population of the City of Montreal. Roofing basins No.4 to No.10 reached the end of their useful life and must be replaced.

entries.741447a8e4e31e00302c40a289884bb66775fc54: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (WMS) is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as to provide a variety of specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services in an environmentally responsible and secure environment. entries.c9592898b7e03a08f2670f50426fd8f462d2fb7e: In the current context of housing crisis and lack of space, the Diversity and Social Inclusion Service (SDIS) is working with several internal and external partners to find solutions and locations whose primary objective is to provide and sustain the provision of social and community services to people in vulnerable situations. entries.a29d99a720b5b06a17b36efdaf8052d15541e7ff: When the government terminated the AccèsLogis funding program in 2022, several new programs and initiatives to finance social and affordable housing (e.g. Quebec Affordable Housing Program, taxed funds) came into being. entries.034452d026f368541239e3484a8c05a83a0a1d37: Bill No. 40, An Act to reform municipal courts and improve the efficiency, accessibility and performance of the justice system, assented to on December 7, 2023 (RLRQ 2023, chapter 31), made a significant change in the structure, operation and jurisdiction of municipal courts in Quebec. Previously, judges of the municipal court of Montreal were paid directly by the City according to the remuneration guidelines set out in the Municipal Courts Act. The new law provided that, effective July 1, 2024, the remuneration of municipal judges throughout Quebec was borne by the Ministry of Justice in the form of advances to be reimbursed by municipalities where municipal judges sit.

entries.a6f07e4f4a53f8983a7e96ed49d602eb179f3473: As part of the budget process, the City of Montreal has an obligation to adopt the regulations required to impose the taxes set out in the budget for the fiscal year in question.

entries.b66001ffc38e4d22c2cdfe8c1dd3135d2275531f: In order to contribute to the financing of public transit, since 2010, the City of Montreal has imposed a property tax on non-residential parking lots in the territory of the city centre. In addition to funding for public transportation, the additional objective of extending the area of application of the tax to large outdoor parking lots is to encourage owners of the land concerned to reflect on the use of the territory they occupy. The tax is imposed under the powers provided for in sections 500.1 et seq. of the Cities and Cities Act.

entries.b45052347e09e8a86ddadba1806e7a9bc1626d92: Since 2023, volumetric pricing has been deployed to non-residential buildings throughout the City of Montreal. This rate is imposed on owners of non-residential buildings with water meters, and the rate varies according to water consumption.

entries.6aea1474a00422aa8984552f31b3ccf498a26b2f: The City of Montreal is competent to regulate the parking of vehicles in its territory, as it may determine the amount of fines based on the offences committed under the regulations provided for that purpose. The power to regulate parking is divided between the municipal council, on the arterial network, and the district councils, on the local network. In August 2022, the city council declared itself competent to regulate parking on the local network for a period of five years, in accordance with section 85.5 of the Charter of the City of Montréal, metropolis of Quebec (CM22 0978), in order to revise the amounts of fines for offences relating to parking on the territory of the City of Montréal.

entries.6b2d92b4a464a4e9eebdff220752150ebe92f03e: The rehabilitation of sewage pipes by the sheathing technique is proposed by the Asset Management Directorate (AMD) of the Water Service (SE). They are part of the strategy for water management of efficient infrastructure and are part of interventions that contribute to improving collective infrastructure and the quality of life of citizens.This untrenched sheathing technique represents many advantages, compared with more traditional methods of reconstruction of sewer pipes by excavation, notably: · Significant reduction in costs of execution compared to reconstruction by excavation; · Rapidity in carrying out the work; · Reduction of disturbance on surrounding infrastructures; · Timeliness of site reclamation; · Reduction of disposal of soil and excavation materials; · Reduction of greenhouse gas emissions compared to reconstruction by excavation; · Maintenance of traffic during construction.

entries.ea916b6fbed968412a9030c678889b6f24c7fc34: The day camps in Espace pour la vie are well known, are highly sought after by parents and enjoyed by hundreds of children who attend them each year. The stays offered at the Biodôme and the Botanical Garden/Insectarium, on topics related to botany, entomology, ornithology, astronomy, biology and ecology, make them excellent programmes for rapprochement with nature and development of scientific culture. entries.81a00a380c2cc621fa00c5b68c81bb51bd18ba6b: The Strategy "Montreal, Zero Waste 2030" (Strategy), adopted by the Agglomeration Council on August 27, 2020, aims at the ambitious goal of zero waste by 2030. entries.9044d4f786ec5ed8081fe6fe9e116129015412c3: The Union des municipalités du Québec (UMQ) implemented in 2013 in partnership at the time with the Simple Plan Foundation (currently SIRCO), the Municipal Employment Plan for Youth under the Protection of Youth in Quebec (PMEJPJ), and invited municipalities from all regions of Quebec to participate. To participate in this plan, the UMQ requested that a resolution be adopted to this effect by the municipal council of the municipality concerned. In 2021, the City Council renewed the plan for a five-year cycle (2021-2025) according to the following conditions: 1- Reserve a minimum of 25 student positions per year in a variety of employment sectors under this program. 2- That the selection and hiring of these young people be carried out centrally by the Human Resources Service in order to ensure the simplicity and consistency of the staffing process. 3- That at the end of the five-year period an evaluation be conducted to determine the renewal of the plan and if necessary revise the objective of the positions offered.

The Great Parks, Mount Royal and Sports Service (MPSRM) requires the services of a wildlife management firm to conduct field operations. entries.a45f11988ecd08997e87ffa0980fffcefae94ac1: On June 20, 2025, the OBNL AlterGo Événements submitted an application for three-year financial support to the City of Montreal for the organization of Défi sportif AlterGo (DSA) event from 2026 to 2028. entries.575537ab454129526d3b46098faa2fef2e1a37cc: Provide financial support totalling $285,000, to various organizations, for projects supported as part of the celebrations of the 50th anniversary of the 1976 Olympic Games / Approve draft agreements to this effect
entries.34e04c5d995452b8d13f84f3c6c7e4396cb66c9c: On 17 April 2025, the City Council adopted the normative framework for the call for projects to mark the 50th anniversary of the 1976 Olympic Games (OJ). This call for projects was based on the decision-making document presented and adopted on 17 April 2025, which set out the context for action. The overall coordination of these festivities, including the management of commemorative initiatives, was entrusted to the Société du parc Jean-Drapeau.
entries.7db805f3b610ae94ff7611b2f166a11e09e9d322: Approve the draft fifth amendment to the partnership agreement between Éco Entreprises Québec and the City, on the management and financing of activities related to recyclable materials as part of the implementation of the modernization of selective collection
entries.65302c1133f1109e2a8bf8402b3a77748531e740: The Regulations Respecting a System for Selective Collection of Certain Residual Material from the Act to Amend the Environmental Quality Act in Respect of Discretion and Selective Collection came into force on July 7, 2022 (hereinafter referred to as "the Regulations"). These Regulations provide for the modernization of the selective collection system using an Extended Producer Responsibility Approach (EPA) and transfers operational and financial responsibility for the management of recyclable materials (RMMs), from collection to recovery, to producers of these materials. In October 2022, Eco Entreprises Québec (ÉEQ) was designated as a Designated Management Organization (DMO) and represents producers.

entries.dfd0d5f0abaa11176857794e3f7d9bd0ddbb86e2: As part of the Government of Quebec's 2030 Green Economy Implementation Plan (GEP), the Ministère de l'Environnement et de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) and the City of Montreal (Ville) signed a grant agreement on March 28, 2022 (Agreement) to enable the latter to implement certain measures of its Climate Plan 2020 - 2030 (Climate Plan) in response to the MEP. The Agreement contributes in particular to supporting the financing of decarbonization projects for 32 buildings identified by the Building Management and Planning Service (SMPI) as one of the largest emitters of greenhouse gases (GHGs) in municipal real estate (Parc), whose ultimate objective is to reduce emissions of approximately 7,000 tonnes CO2 eq., or about 25% of the GHG emissions from that park. The Carbon Decarbonation Project 08 is part of Action 30 of the Climate Plan to transform 100% of the Park into an operational zero carbon park by 2030.

entries.d0815ed1687a3465873a43ae443e0f130ed852a3: The Active Transportation Fund (ATF) is a federal direct-on-demand financial assistance program. Eligible recipients, which include municipal and regional governments, public sector organizations, not-for-profit organizations, provincial and territorial governments and Aboriginal recipients, can apply for funding directly to Housing, Infrastructure and Communities Canada for eligible projects. Up to $500 million will be available for active transportation capital projects across Canada.

entries.345568707003c425b4beb5184ab56ad46824cda6: In particular, the Act to reform municipal courts and improve the efficiency, accessibility and performance of the justice system, adopted and assented to on December 7, 2023, introduced a significant change in the structure, operation and jurisdiction of municipal courts in Quebec. Previously, judges of the municipal court of Montreal were paid directly by the City according to the remuneration guidelines set out in the Municipal Courts Act. The Act, which seeks, among other things, to reform municipal courts and improve the effectiveness, accessibility and performance of the justice system, provides that since July 1, 2024, the remuneration of municipal judges throughout Québec is borne by the Ministry of Justice in the form of advances to be reimbursed by municipalities where municipal judges sit.

entries.c7959ffc7acc7a78435a0f089d874e47194186e5: On August 28, 2025, the Regulations Amending the Montréal Agglomeration Planning and Development Plan (RCG 14-029) (Schema) number RCG 14-029-8 was adopted by the Montréal Agglomeration Council and came into force on November 3, 2025 in accordance with the Act. Regulations RCG 14-029-8 make amendments to the Scheme in order to meet the Minister of Municipal Affairs' request and to ensure compliance with the new government direction in land use planning (OGAT Habitation), i.e.: Introduce the OGAT Habitation, entitled "Planning Living Environments for Access to Quality, Accessible and Affordable Housing for All Households", in the Scheme; Take housing diagnosis into account in content elements; Integrate the OGAT Habitation Strategic Indicator and targets identified in the housing diagnostic.

entries.eaf090dbca0ad98a2cd4271212bb84f8c8e5c0b7: In order to effectively support the mission of the City of Montreal Police Service (SPVM), it is essential to maintain an optimal level of operational performance and security. entries.12211ffc072f36ed380dc0dac28e032c992261f8: As part of the implementation of the Nightlife Policy and in conjunction with the Cultural Development Policy 2025-2030 and the City Centre Strategy, Action 1.1 provides for the designation of night vitality institutions that are conducive to cultural activities. entries.152c17d0f866afb2475497a2d86237c1fa9323f6: The Jean-R.-Marcotte (Station) wastewater treatment plant treats all wastewater and sanitation on the island of Montreal as well as rainwater from unit systems. In order to improve the quality of treated water and reduce microbiological contamination of St. Lawrence River waters, an ozone disinfection process will be added at the end of the existing treatment. The technological choice of ozonation as a method for disinfecting wastewater was made and public hearings were held in the spring of 2008.

entries.097e6992794089222504bcfb473ff8c2a5bdeea3: The Réseau de transport métropolitain (RTM), also known as "Exo", is administered by a board of directors (CA) composed of 15 members appointed as follows: 1°3 by the City of Montreal, acting by its council of agglomeration; 2°1 by the City of Laval; 3°1 by the City of Longueuil, acting by its council of agglomeration; 4°4 by the local municipalities of the North Crown; 5°4 by the local municipalities of the South Crown; 6°2 users or users of collective transportation services by the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal (CMM), including a user of public transport services and a user or user of transport adapted to the needs of persons with reduced mobility. It is the CMM which determines the municipalities or groups of municipalities that have an obligation to appoint independent members and sets their minimum number for them.

entries.55d559d5d819a67d1c90e2d7649446cf1a45679d: The governments of Quebec and Canada are providing more than 3,2 billion dollars to municipalities over 5 years to ensure the sustainability of infrastructure essential for the well-being of the population and the quality of their living environment. This funding comes from an investment of more than 2,2 billion dollars from the Government of Canada through the Canada Community Futures Fund, plus a contribution of 1 billion dollars from the Government of Québec. The Transfer Program for Water and Collective Infrastructure of Quebec (TECQ 2024-2028) provides financial support to municipalities for the implementation of drinking water, wastewater treatment, climate resilience, local roadway and other types of infrastructure.
entries.511e7a46a9da50122389bb5abd5387b2e10b2602: Adopted in December 2020 and updated in 2025, the Climate Plan 2020-2030 frames Montreal's climate action and is structured around 52 actions organized in 5. It aims to mitigate the effects of climate change by pursuing two major objectives: Reducing GHG emissions: Reducing metropolitan greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from 55 % below 1990 levels in 2030, with a view to achieving carbonutrality in 2050; Enhancing resilience: Reducing the city's vulnerability to climate hazards, such as heat waves, heavy rainfall, floods, storms and droughts. Since 2020, many initiatives to achieve these goals have been implemented by municipal authorities, civil society and the private sector.

entries.437a870154cdc38c80cdd36ed4aa79a53df166a3: Section 85.5 of the Charter of the City of Montreal, metropolis of Quebec (the "Charter") provides that the council of the city may, if it considers that it is in the general interest of the city, declare itself competent with respect to the exercise of a power or jurisdiction conferred by law on all boroughs, subject to certain conditions. The 23 August 2016, the council of the city had recourse to this power by declaring itself competent, for a period of 2 years, with regard to all boroughs, in order to adopt a Single Contract Management Policy applicable to all boroughs. It should be recalled that at that time, the Towns and Cities Act did not provide for the obligation to pass regulations in this area.

entries.799d1a00753f2189110d5538b430f26e218b8eda: The École de technologie supérieure (ÉTS), a university and research institution in application engineering and technology, is responsible for Ax.c.'s deployment strategy. Inaugurated in June 2025, Ax.c is an innovative entrepreneurship space of approximately 100 000 p2 located in the heart of Montreal's business district, on the former parquet floor of the Bourse and on two floors of Place Victoria. The project aims primarily to provide young technological start-ups with an inspiring, inclusive and world-class space.
entries.672a8d380e5dee5417c1f02c626c6d7101a5356e: As part of its medium- and long-term planning, SMRA has identified the need for a three-year Master Agreement (3) for the provision of fire self-propelled pumps with nominal capacity of 6 000 litres per minute to the Fire Safety Service, which is intended to allow the gradual acquisition of a total of thirty (30) self-propelled trucks at an estimated rate of ten (10) vehicles per year.

entries.96f35802cba344cfe8a47f85cd1b01b6800093b5: Created in the middle of the 90 years, Montréal International has a dual mandate to attract foreign investment to the Montreal metropolitan area and to host new international organizations. For the first activity, it is funded by the governments of Canada and Quebec, the Communauté métropolitaine de Montréal and the private enterprise. For the second activity, the reception and development of international organizations in Montreal, it is financed equally by the governments of Canada and Quebec and the City of Montreal, which contribute, among other things, to the Montreal International Development Fund (FODIM).

entries.f866ffec254c03fa2ef4159f153b94bae98ed402: As part of its Capital Plan, the Pointe-à-Callière Museum presents an asset protection project, namely the preservation of vestiges, renewal of permanent exhibitions and obsolete museum and technological equipment, as well as studies prior to the 3 phase of development. Since 1992, the year of the opening of the Pointe-à-Callière Museum, the Société du Musée leases from the City of Montréal buildings in which part of the museum is housed: 150, rue Saint-Paul Ouest, l'Ancienne-Douane, 350, Place Royale, the Éperon Building, in addition to the undergrounds that connect the Museum spaces and the 335 Placed youville (Caserne No. 1). In addition, with regard to its management, the Pointe-à-Callière Museum is one of the cultural facilities for which the City Council has responsibility under the Charter of the City of Montreal.
entries.33da7b49b033f02a10e8c4f9f00bc4678675f209: When the Tariffs Regulations (Fiscal Year 2026) were published, the Sports Facilities Management Division of the Major Parks, Mount Royal and Sports Service realized that errors were reflected in the document approved by the Montréal soccer stadium and the Claude-Robillard sports complex. entries.1edb9542acd0ae5f46159d9da856d0215fe23e64: The mission of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service is to ensure the availability and reliability of vehicles and equipment, as well as the provision of a variety of specialized services and products tailored to the needs of boroughs and central services in an environmentally responsible and safe environment. entries.20625ac343195cb13133bfb3374394f165d1701d: Since the 30 years, the City and the University of Montreal (UdeM) have coordinated their efforts to promote research activities in the field of plant biology around the natural pole of the Jardin botanique de Montréal. To this end, in 1990, they have brought together research staff attached to them, respectively, within the Institut de recherche en biologie phytologique de Montréal (IRBV), a non-profit organization that creates a critical mass of scientists in the field of plant biology and biodiversity; to establish favourable conditions for collaboration in carrying out research activities; to encourage the sharing of state-of-the-art equipment and to encourage the co-direction of graduate students. The IRBV, jointly administered by the City and UdeM, is recognized as a centre of excellence in the fields of plant biology and biodiversity.

entries.9ba1f022d529cff68abbcdcb633d349f66bacf88: Pursuant to the Act respecting the Grande Bibliothèque de Bibliothèque et Archives nationales du Québec (BanQ), adopted by 17 June 1998 and assented to the 20 June 1998, the City of Montreal has three seats on the board of directors of this Crown corporation: · two persons appointed by the City of Montréal; · the Director of Libraries of the City of Montréal, appointed ex officio as Chief Librarian of the City of Montréal. entries.e8982e889e31e4ea7606841c254fafc19451b745: The Viau Municipal Workshops, located at 2269, rue Viau, have been acquired by the City in 2004 and house centralized maintenance and repair functions of the Rolling Stock and Workshop Service (SMRA): the Montreal Fire Safety Service's (SIM) Heavy, Light and Emergency Vehicle Maintenance Garage, welding and ironworks as well as administrative premises. The facilities require a major upgrade of gas extraction systems and air treatment systems to meet CNESST standards. entries.d25d874fe7cbc50d1892d90d9da47e51408c060a: The City of Montreal, as part of its 2030 Economic Plan, reaffirms its commitment to improving access to and participation in economic life for the entire population. This commitment is particularly evident through strengthening the social economy, reducing territorial inequalities and promoting the participation of actors from under-represented groups. The 2 axis of the economic plan places economic inclusion at the heart of municipal priorities, including by supporting projects carried out by specialized organizations and mobilizing local ecosystems.

entries.cc3e8b88a74d89d198d9586755d5cf2b6db7e526: The Act to amend the Cultural Heritage Act and other legislation was passed on 25 March 2021 and assented to the following 1 April. This Act introduces an obligation for regional county municipalities (RCMs) and agglomerations in Quebec to adopt, by no later than the 1 April 2026, an inventory of all buildings constructed before 1940 in their territory that have heritage value. This inventory must be carried out according to the methodology and method of dissemination established by the Ministère de la Culture et des Communications (MCC).

entries.8799da07308b8cc20b2c05859125731c542b62e5: The Biosphere is one of the 5 museums of Space for Life, Canada's largest natural science complex, which hosts some 2,5 millions of visitors every year. Its interdisciplinary approach invites dialogue between scientists, artists, citizens and citizens.

entries.82f4f7c8d8fa4d3c327ff88db7c6cdc12c4da735: On 174-176, Notre-Dame Street East / 462, Place Jacques-Cartier is a building that has been under emphyteosis since March 7, 1983. The end of this emphyteosis, on March 7, 2013, resulted in the City of Montreal (City) becoming fully owner of the site. Since December 1, 1996, the Société historique de Montréal (SHM) association whose mission is to dispel, using authentic documents, omissions and errors that slip into the narrative of Canada's historical facts, occupies, free of charge, the floors and basement of the building, for an area of approximately 169.55 m2 (1,825 sq. ft.).
entries.14cf8c7a49ee501022ae288309748ecf95c5311d: Located at 3680 Jeanne-Mance Street, the Strathearn Centre is a sociocultural building. It houses several organizations such as Montréal intercultural arts, L'Atelier d'artistes, Ex aequo, Danse-Cité and many others. Since May 1, 2002, the City of Montreal (Ville) has rented to SME-ART (Organisme), a space located on the 4th floor of the Strathearn Centre, with an area of approximately 29.57 m2, for administrative purposes.
entries.b3b824f711168bcacea1932163ef3d2c1b4d7773: The City has entered into a tripartite promise (the Promise) to sell at 9536-1135 Québec inc. and Helpful Développement (l'Acquereur), the building known as l'Îlot Voyageur Sud, consisting of lots 3,523,567 and 3,523,568 of the cadastre du Québec, with an area of 7,062 m2 with built-up building, located at 505, boulevard De Maisonneuve Est, in the borough of Ville-Marie, for the sum of $20,000,000 payable with interest, plus applicable taxes where applicable. A first addendum to the Promise was subsequently signed in order to extend the initial deadline until June 25, 2026. Following this extension, the Acquirer completed several steps during his diligent verification period, including the estimation of asbestos decontamination costs, a call for tenders for demolition, obtaining a change of zoning accompanied by the required studies, as well as a search for titles to analyse easements.
entries.70404dc4d6f483e3d0f213dad0612260d175b7a0: The Housing Service (the HS) commissioned the Real Estate Strategy Service (the SSI) to sell to the Coopérative d'habitation Monde-Uni (l'Acquéreur), a building located at 7965 Boulevard de l'Acadie, in the arrondissement of Villeray–Saint-Michel–Parc-Extension (l'Arrondissement), known and designated as Lots 2,245 623, 2,245,625 and 2,245,626 du cadastre du Québec (Immeuble), with a total area of 789.6 m2, as shown on the attached plans. L'Immeuble will be the subject of a cadastral operation to unify the lots that will become lot 6,707,435 (lot Projeté) of the cadastre du Québec. The City of Montréal (the City) became owner of the Immeuble on February 1, 2021, by exercising its right of preemption.
